analysis.name: Anja Jovic-Humphrey
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took this class to fulfil a lit requirement and I was completely blown away by it. The professor said she wanted to give us intrinsic (as opposed to extrinsic) motivation, and she really succeeded in doing this. She managed to say something really profound about life (and not just books) in pretty much every lecture.

My absolute queen. She is an engaging speaker so lectures were more interesting because of how she tells her stories. The projects are creative and not too hard. The reading pace is fast but like lowkey not mandatory and she does give little breaks so it's chill and she kind of makes up for the fact that the books can be boring.

Anja made this class very fun and enjoyable. She also made it seem very chill which is good if you are taking a tough semester load. It's quite easy to do well and she shows a lot of funny videos in class. The only problem I would say is she sometimes called in sick and would let us know like an hour before class started which isn't fun.

Professor Anja is a very kind professor, her lectures are based on the books but also her life expierences and helping her students. Attendence in discussion counts towards most of grade. The classload is light, mostly reading along with 3 easy writtings/projects. Final exam :10 reading questions(basic comprehension).

One of my favorite professors at UW. Didn't realize I was taking a comedy class until the first day and thought about dropping, but I stayed and this is the only class that I actually look forward to attending. She is so funny, makes an effort to get to know students, and actually cares what we have to say. Looking for another class to take withher

analysis.name: Arif Qureshi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Arif is by far the best real estate professor I've had as an undergraduate.  His priority is literally to provide real estate students a leg up for when they are beginning their profession.  Expectations of students are clear-cut and he can be extremely entertaining.  Take as many courses with Arif as possible.

Arif is awesome. In RE631, he gave great lectures and was excited about all the topics he presented in Excel. Great help during office hours, always willing to explain how to get the answer for questions. One of the best RE professors here. Lots of work and fast-paced for 1 credit. Test grades are heavy, they can be challenging and require study.
Best professor in the Real Estate department by far. Well-defined and relevant curriculum. Lecture is incredibly entertaining; Arif's commentary is insightful and hilarious.
Arif is a hilarious dude and a solid teacher. His class teaches awesome concepts and is done via case competitions and exams. The exams, however, will determine your entire grade.

Arif is great at teaching, and he is very helpful during office hours. If you want to do well, start the material early in the week and understand everything on the quizzes. The exam is made up of the toughest quiz questions, and he will explicitly tell you what you need to know. I enjoyed his class, but it's definitely a lot for 1 credit.

analysis.name: Abdollah Mohammadi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
I actually hate this class, if you have the option to not take it here PLEASE do
Mohammadi cannot teach and thinks that concepts that are easy for him are just common sense and it makes it difficult for others to learn. pls do. not. take. this. class.

Thought it couldn't get worse after 207 but I was wrong. Lectures were incoherent and made the content more confusing. Exams were absurdly difficult and did not accurately reflect the type of content or questions seen on homework/quizzes. I would not recommend this class to anyone seeking to actually understand physics. DON'T DO IT!!

Worst prof ever. Spends more time deriving equations than explaining how to use them. Extremely disorganized course and the exams were unnecessarily confusing. He is condescending, rude, and teaches like everyone in the class has a physics background. I wouldn't recommend to my worst enemy. Genuinely the worst experience I've ever had in a class.

I think abdollah assumes that understanding concepts he's been teaching for years is easy so he doesn't put effort into helping you comprehend it. This class sucks overall but going to lecture after reading the textbook actually made me understand the class LESS.

I really liked Dr. Mohammadi for 208. His lectures often went through the conceptual part and equation derivation which most people didn't like but I liked it since it's critical to understand concepts to do well. He passionately did demos while also being accessible outside of class. Don't treat it as a math class, but an actual science class.

analysis.name: Autumn Kent
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 101 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: It was an easy class which she could've explained things in much simpler ways but overall, her explaining will do the job. Her exams are really easy but I mean the class itself is super easy. Attended classes at the start but honestly doing the homework alone using chegg was all you need to get an A.

Lectures were disorganized, making it difficult to follow or learn the material in class. I often left the lecture more confused than when I arrived. The final exam felt unnecessarily challenging for me, even though math is my strongest subject. I would strongly encourage you to avoid all classes "taught" by this professor.

findpassword.
if i write an essay, it would be how you shoulD nOt have this teacher who (iwishicouldsayteach) you math. 
1.lectures: so boriNg nOT even clear. 
2.random-TAgents-weird-joKEs. 
3.first couple of weeks the TeacHer was behInd on the curriculum becauseSpoke for more than 45 mins trying to explain limits. limits. 
4. unclear TEACHER

I skipped every lecture after attending the first one, Kent does not explain concepts clearly and oftentimes will go on tangents not related to course material. He takes too long on unimportant topics. I geniunely believe anyone new to this material would easily fail this class if they only attended leture and discussions. Do NOT take her.

VERY confusing and unclear lectures, with Professor Kent going off on almost completely unrelated tangents very often. I didn't take calculus in high school, and struggled in this class which very honestly should've been one of my easier ones. If you are new to calculus, plan to spend a disproportionate amount of time on this class.

analysis.name: Ana Oaxaca
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are pointless to go to she just reads off a slide which is copy and pasted from the textbook chapters you have to read, all of which are VERY long and have to be completed every week. She was always unprepared and seemed to be making decisions on the spot. She relied on TAs but didn't communicate with them well. She was bad at using tech

She was great! Super funny and kind. Her lectures were very much review of the textbook, but you should be reading it anyways so it's actually very helpful. Class is exactly what a college level class should be. Exams were extremely easy if you just read the book and know how to compose a decent 1 paragraph argument. She is amazing and very smart!!

Oaxaca was great. Textbook is necessary as she cannot cover all the content needed for the exams in lecture. Very reading heavy. Exams are long and semi-difficult, but home-learning assignments  give a great cushion for your grade. Lots of extra credit opportunities throughout semester. Discussion attendance is mandatory and so helpful for exams.

Not beginner-friendly. Moves fast and skips vital material. Lectures were her reading off slides from textbook (which you must read anyway, there are 2 of them). High expectations. Exams are hard and unnecessarily complicated for an introductory-level class. Doesn't give enough time to complete them either. Work was never graded on time.

She is a new professor and did not seem very prepared for the lecture. She gave out so much reading that it was hard to complete before the next lecture. She relied heavily on support from her TAs, but didn't seem to communicate very well with them. Overall, I don't recommend taking this class with this professor.

analysis.name: Ariel Juarez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took Dance 107 with AJ, and it was great! Show up to class, participate, and have fun! He is a very talented dancer and a great teacher. Canvas assignments weren't very organized or clear, but it was okay; he didn't grade hard.
Love him, he's so fun and dances were somewhat difficult for beginners but he posts videos so you can practice outside of class.

Fun guy. I took hip-hop with him and then Latin social dance. Have fun, make friends, and definitely don't worry about the in-class practicals. You probably won't ever need to practice outside of class.
AJs hip hop dance class was so fun! All he expects is that you show up to class, try your best, and work hard! Youll do warmups, hip hop technique, and learn fun combos.
He was not responding to emails, and the grading was not clear. Dance was difficult and hard to follow for beginners.

analysis.name: Amanda Buchberger
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I personally thought Dr. B was a great instructor. She was a little intimidating and could be blunt at times, but she always seemed to have the best interests at heart for her students and cared. She was always willing to answer questions if you went to her office. She's very enthusiastic about achem and tries to get students to feel the same.

Not much you can do to avoid her (teaches the class every semester because she's friends with the department chair), but just be aware, she is a very em0ti0nally charged decision maker. Try to get on her good side (if it exists????). Good luck, try to do everything you can so that the final grade project doesn't affect ur grade.

Not sure why my rating keeps getting removed--Dr. B is very knowledgeable, but she's so disrespectful to students. She sets the standards so high that not even the TA's can surpass them. She rarely gives any feedback (If she does, it's extremely harsh and unhelpful). They make this class so hard for no reason and don't even care about the students.

Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had in my three years here. She is so disrespectful and unhelpful, and not only does she not want you to succeed, but she actively wants you to fail. The expectations and setup of this course is entirely unintelligible. Instructors failed to tell us the requirements for our assignments and then gave us a 0.

Horrible person. Rude feedback, unhelpful rubrics, unhelpful feedback, will publicly berate you at any time. During our final presentation, she asked an unanswerable question, the answer she wanted being "no answer." GET BENT!!!

analysis.name: Stavroula Antonopoulos
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Stavroula was a great professor and I loved her class! All exams were open note, online, and you could take them at any time over the course of a week. Participation is graded for maybe 2/3 of lectures, but she drops the worst 7 and is super understanding of extenuating circumstances. Engaging lectures and easy grader as well!

Most people (myself included) take this class as a GPA-booster, Stavroula did a great job for having 400+ enrolled in her class. Expectations laid out very clearly in the syllabus, pretty light workload, some useful insights into nutrition, interesting guest speakers in lectures. Solid freshman year class to knock out some science credits.

Class so easy I question if I actually took it. Professor is really sweet and lectures are simple to follow. Participation is occasionally taken but I haven't attended class for the past two months and ended with a 96.

Always gave so much information in her lectures and was very clear about all assignments and when they were due. All exams were online and final was optional only to help your grade if needed. Gives so much extra credit opportunities and is very flexible if needed. Very kind professor and fun class to take!

analysis.name: Paul Barford
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Barford does not respond to questions in lecture. He is sarcastic and unhelpful.
Super difficult quizzes and exams which focus on memorizing small details on subjects. Lectures were interesting for the most part, but a lot of information is presented in the lectures.

TLDR: Never, ever take a class with Barford. He often snaps at people who ask questions or makes fun of them, if he even takes questions at all. He is lazy and does not update course materials, so you are left guessing on exams. Always cancels office hours. Projects unrelated to lecture material. Really disappointed. Needs to be audited.

Professor Barford is a decent lecturer. There wasn't a time where I was confused about anything. He's average when it comes to explaining algorithms. However, his quizzes are rather unfair as some questions have very subjective answers, and every 2 pts lost makes you lose 1% of your grade. "You have to choose the best answer". Ugh.

Nice person, but lectures are a bit old fashioned(talk a lot about historical stuff and physical layer) and not recorded. Must read textbook in great detail and take notes carefully.
This isn't a surprise if you look at his research focus, so decide yourself if you want a more modern style & content (take with Ming Liu) or Barford.

analysis.name: Alexander Shashko
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 192 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Shashko is a very engaging professor who presents material clearly and makes lectures interesting and relevant. The course has three essays plus weekly discussions and readings, all manageable. If you put in effort, you can do well. Attendance isn't required, but notes are graded and not posted. Loved this class.

Amazing professor! He makes every class so fun and interesting that you actually want to attend the lectures (plus you get to listen to some really good music). Attendance isn't taken but you need 20 lecture notes to pass the class-- so go to at least 20 of the lectures (and take notes!) or else you're kinda cooked. No exams, only easy essays.

Great professor, you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches and cares about his students' understanding. Although this course topic didn't particularly interest me, he made the lectures interesting to attend with very engaging teaching. Overall, a pretty easy grader as long as you do your work and follow the rubrics

very knowledgeable and is passionate in what he does. class is based on 3 papers, 11 discussion posts and lecture notes. TA's are usually considerate and easy graders. attendance isn't mandatory (for discussion it is) but recommended as he verbally explains the content and doesn't record them. highly recommend if you need an ethnic studies credit!

This man is invited to my wedding. By far the best teacher I have ever had, not just professor. Great office hours and the content is fun and engaging. Lots of students stay after to ask questions and the class is very approachable, mostly because of his enthusiasm about the material. Would 100% take again.

analysis.name: Bi Cheng Wu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 134 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: One of the top 2 worst professors I've had at UW-Madison. Not only are his lectures just reading off of an HTML file in class, he is condescending when meeting with him one on one in his office hours when you are confused about a question or concept.

Listen to the other reviews! If you are planning on taking STAT 240, do not take it with Bi. He is not a good lecturer and does not explain things well. I found many of the concepts hard to understand because of his poor teaching style. The layout of the class sucks, and he just reads off an HTML class while barely explaining things.
there is no any logic in bi's class

Bi's words were too many people passed the midterm last semester so he made ours impossible and complained that not many people passed and will make the final easier. When the final came he made it hard as **** and killed my gpa along with it. If I pass this class I will thank god that I will have to never see this man I hope no one lets him teach.

Nice guy, awful professor. He's smart but all he does is read off an HTML file, even then concepts are explained poorly. Exams are written awfully. For reference, mean on the midterm was a 50%. Exams are theory based and are absolutely nothing like the homework or discussion assignments. The 240/340 sequence needs to be reevaluated and audited.

analysis.name: Robert Beattie
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is passionate and interesting to listen to in lecture if you are also interested in Envir. Studies. The class is test heavy (4 main papers) but that is because there are only a few multiple choice quizzes and a final that make up the rest of the grades. The grading is relatively easy so the papers weren't bad. I would totally take his class agai

Loved Prof. Beattie; he was super caring and passionate about his field. The class itself was easy, yet you are graded mainly by 4 essays. The essays have many requirements, yet are limited in word count. Additionally, there is not much direction in the papers, so you lose points on things you didn't know you needed. Great guy, not great class.

great lecturer and cares a lot, but you need a good TA because there are 4 papers that make up 65% of your grade. my TA was way harsher than the others and it's hard to raise your grade if your papers get scored low. the lectures ended up feeling super repetitive, but the content was interesting. some of the concepts were kinda abstract.

I took this class thinking it would be relatively simple since it was just for my social science credit, but there are a lot of readings assigned for lectures, and papers are big. But they are helpful for the four papers. It's a little annoying when the paper prompts are posted two weeks before it's due, and future lectures are important for them.

Very interesting lectures, you can tell he is very knowledgable but the class itself ended up being very repetitive. Majority of the grade is based on four papers graded by TAs, so you need to have a good TA to succeed in this class. Content is easy enough, but grading criteria is very vague. I don't recommend this class at all.

analysis.name: Kara Bresnahan
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's one of those young profs who makes everything harder than it needs to be just to be respected, but it doesn't work. The exams are harder than they should be. She is rude and disrespectful to students time. Weekly content doesn't get posted until like Wednesday night. I wish she cared less about difficulty because it could be a great class.

The slides are pre-recorded lectures that she reads through way too fast, so you have to pause constantly, which takes twice as long as the “estimated time.” She posts necessary materials late, won't give extensions, and complains about being overwhelmed—as if we don't have five other classes, work, and extracurriculars.

It is a hybrid class so basically you're teaching yourself. The textbook is more helpful than the slides are. She's not very accommodating with questions and doesn't explain things the best. Problem sets focus heavily on Excel with minimal guidance. The class is interesting but content is presented in a way that makes it harder than it needs to be.

I was looking forward to taking this class, but I was unfortunately very disappointed. This class is hybrid, and the in class portion is often Excel based assignments. She gets annoyed when students ask questions. Exams are online and honor locked, and way harder than they need to be. She does not prepare students well for exams.

Posts lecture slides on canvas but attendance is required to sit there and watch her walk through an excel activity that nobody can see. "doesn't have time to answer questions" even though she posts the answers. She is mean and seems like she thinks less of her students.

analysis.name: Brian Powers
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Actually the worst test I have ever taken in my life. He is a pretty good professor, but the stat 340 curriculum needs a change. The homework has no correspondence with the tests and even knowing probability theory the test was straight-up unfair. The midterm average was a 50%. I would say the course teaches R very good, but the exams are unfair.

Worst class I have taken in college. It is a complete mess. We do all of our assignments in R and then take the hardest exam known to man on paper -- we got 50 minutes to do it which was no where near the amount of time we should have been given to complete that monstrosity. Given the amount paid in tuition here, this course needs a re-evaluation.

He just hit us with the worst test I've ever received on campus. This guys tests are near impossible. Nobody leaves the room until 2 minutes left on the test because everyone is fighting for their lives. Many just straight up leave their short answers blank because of the amount of time pressure this man put on us.

The course was ran very poorly. Lectures were a mix of typed out slides and coding, then homework was all coding, but then the exams were hand written questions. Made no sense. Why teach us how to code if we're going to be tested on solving problems by hand? Don't expect Piazza answers within a few days either. Nowhere to be seen before the final.

Brian Powers may be the worst math professor I have ever had at UW, and I have seen a vast variety. It is apparent that Brian has absolutely no idea how to effectively communicate and teach his class through lectures, and assumes you already know quite a bit of statistics. This class has guaranteed that I'll never take another stats course.

analysis.name: Kristin Branch
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class isn't difficult, but the exams are filled with the most random/unrelated questions that make it feel like a trivia rather than something you actually studied. Quite literally any phrase in the textbook is fair game. Her practice exam doesn't prepare you for the actual exam at all. Better to ask Chat to test you than use her resources.

I could care less about grades not being rounded; this is university, not high school. But I've never had a professor this boring/bad. She refused to fix TopHat issues, just read slides, ignored exam questions, and exams included material not in the slides/book. She did very little and showed little concern, by far the worst prof in the B school

She is extremely smart and a good professor in terms of learning. I enjoy her lectures. However, the exam felt like a joke. The grade average for this class can't exceed a 3.2 so she makes purposefully makes the exams totally random and barely related. We spend so much time going over main concepts and they weren't even on it.

Unnecessarily hard and unsupportive. Lectures were unstructured and her talking made key concepts unclear. She showed no empathy when I shared mental health struggles after a loss, allows no grade changes, and the curve does nothing for you. Having gone through a multitude of semesters here at Madison I can for sure say she's the most heartless.

Professor Branch was a very good professor for Marketing 300. She knows what she is talking about, and the examples in class were very interesting to me. However, the guidelines and grading were pretty confusing. And the lecture slides were difficult to understand if you miss a lecture. The exams were written OK, still misleading and confusing.

analysis.name: Katarzyna Beilin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Kata is a pretty easy grader, but the readings are very dense (10-40 pages each, 2x/week). The majority of your grade is based on 5 short responses and 3 medium responses to the readings, but you get to choose them. Participation is also very important, you need to participate pretty much every class to get full points.

The first couple weeks of lecture are tough to get used to for sure. She has an interesting accent, goes through her lecture slides extremely quickly, and the reading can pile up. But once you get used to her style of lecture, it is not too bad. Just make sure you keep up with the readings, pay attention in lecture and don't worry about copying eve

I've studied at 4 colleges in 3 countries and Kata is one of the best professors I've had. She is fun and dynamic with her lectures and reading materials. She is clear about what is expected and if she sees you putting in the time and effort you will do well in her class. Make sure to participate in class because that will help a lot. Great Profe!

Kata's take on environmental studies in the hispanic world is one of the most engaging Spanish classes I've taken at UW. Great balance of readings/documentaries for pre-class preparation; the class is mostly discussion based. Kata is both passionate for the material and compassionate for her students. Truly wonderful class, even though it's online.

I like Professor Beilin! She's kind of vague in what she wants you to do/when you should turn in your essays/even the topics you can write about, but she's very sweet and doesn't put too much pressure on anything. She accepts all types of participation, I never felt like I couldn't participate because she was judging me. I'd take her again for sure

analysis.name: Bipin Karunakaran
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Bipin was friendly and patient with the students. He was very patient, going back through steps that students missed or misunderstood multiple times. He was also always upbeat, he was passionate about data visualization, data analysis, and machine learning / how gen ai will affect our lives, but kept it simple and achievable for the students.

I really appreciated how hands on the course was, it was fun to actually code, run through machine models, and play around with data. I also appreciated that the professor made it easy to succeed in this course-- hard skills like coding aren't familiar or required for many post business school jobs, so making it easy to succeed in the course.

Bipin is extremely unorganized; most of the time, the programs he was "teaching" would go haywire/not work because his data/processes would be invalid, leaving the class confused and frustrated. He also loved to sidetrack on the unnecessary. Albeit, 308 is an easy class, but from this experience I would never take another class with him.

Course work is based on practical application in real world business. I found the lectures and projects very useful. They helped in fetching summer intership. I have registed for another class taught by this same professor.
This prof is unorganized, his code is random and hard to follow. He's more a tech guy than a good lecturer. The course is overall easy but no way I'll take his course again.

analysis.name: Clint Jensen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sorry, I just had to post, the last comment is talking about how the exams are so different from the course material which is craaazy! We just took our first exam last week, so I don't even know what they are talking about. Maybe the practice exam that had a super high class average score??? Exams seem totally fair and I'm loving this class!!!

Read the post about Clint not being a math person and teaching statistics. I guess I feel differently about that. I'm not a math person either, and I really liked his Clint's honesty about that and that he didn't take for granted that we knew everything. So I feel like it was super helpful how he talked about stats. I'm glad I was in his section!

this class is great, and highly recommend taking it with this professor. He is very passionate about these topics, and I think the exams are fair. As long as you go to lecture, read the textbook and study you will be good. Overall, would take another class with him.

Professor openly told the class he's "not a math guy" on the first day of Statistics. Curriculum was copied and pasted from online summer term. Flipped classroom with little to no content-related insight from him. Answer keys frequently wrong. If you don't understand a concept you're not going to get any help from Clint. Would have taken online.

Clint is a very enthusiastic teacher and I loved going to his lectures; however, he rarely checks for attendance in class and puts all slides online. In 202, he gives a generous amount of extra credit (5% if you do everything), so there is a lot of flexibility. Exams are not the best quality, but also not super hard.

analysis.name: Charo D'Etcheverry
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Charo is very accommodating and willing to give students opportunities. She often even sacrifices her own after-class time to offer remedial chances to those students who did not attend the lecture. The questions she sets are all intended to help students understand the class content, rather than to cause students to receive poor grades.

Charo was the best professor I had. She was kind and made the lecture engaging. Class expectations are made clear from the first day. It is not a lot of work or a lot of reading. Do remember this is a com b class with com b requirements! Discussion attendance is essential for the A, not the lecture. She also gives opportunities for bonus points!

Charo is a great choice for if you just need Comm B. She cares about the material, and uses contract grading so you get an A if you just do the homework. The only tedious thing in her class is that there are a lot of focus points on citing work, so the class feels more focused on that instead of the actual readings and ideas from asian studies.

Prof Etcheverry was super nice and helpful. It was contract graded, which means if you do a certain amount of work it will qualify you for that grade. I thought this layout was stressful, in addition to the very unorganized canvas site. The class material was interesting, but I'd recommend waiting until in-person classes return.
It wasn't difficult to follow her instructions and take A. Her class was very interesting.

analysis.name: Tracy  Carolan
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Showed up 30 minutes late to office hours and then acted like she had no time to answer questions. Barely lectured and was not good at answering questions. Basically just relied on other professors' lecture slides and videos. Was just super disorganized and never started exams on time but then hurried us to finish at the end. Would not take again.

Lectures as well as canvas are VERY disorganized. No real lectures given, mostly group work time on packets. Inconsistencies between answer keys with her and TAs. Homework and Canvas materials not reflective of what will be on tests. Have to self-teach for most of this class. Does not hold valuable review sessions and no study guides ever.

She genuinely doesn't care about her students. Makes weird comments in class like hitting herself in the head with a stick during lecture or calling herself an "old bat". She also constantly complains about canvas and has it organized badly even though all of the other professors seem to have it figured out. She also doesn't answer questions.

Doesn't use her own lectures, has mini lectures as an excuse to play NYT while we do group work, final was bad and I had to teach myself stats. Words can't describe how bad of a teacher this woman is. Would make uncomf comments to students, and did not answers questions clearly. Her TA did most of her work, and they gave different answers.

Note-taking and studying material were not her own, which caused discrepancies between out-of-class and in-class information. Seemed hostile if students asked questions or still did not understand after her explanations, even those with language barriers. Highly unorganized. Answers varied constantly between her and the TA. Recommend GUTS for help.

analysis.name: Cassie Williams
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

The course is designed well, and projects build off one another. The projects themselves are straightforward, so long as you've been attending lecture. A class act.

You go to lecture to hear him discuss graphics concepts that are interesting, but then you have less than a week to program the graphics concept in a "cool, creative way" in JavaScript. 1) The grading structure and overall class structure is terrible 2) This class DOES NOT teach javascript, but uses it heavily. If you don't know it you're screwed

analysis.name: Emily Stanley
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 133 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Almost all of your grade falls on the tests but are nearly impossible to study for given the breadth of the material discussed during class. Many times there were questions on the test I didnt have in my notes at all. Returning students from the field had a hard time with the tests. Too many guest speakers, didnt know what was important.

Doesn't post lecture slides, does not care if students succeed. Expects you to scramble and write down all material on the slides as she goes, no supplemental readings whatsoever. Completely based on lecture, so don't skip! Extremely condescending and rude if you meet with her.
Her bio class was awful I don't think I ever had a teacher as bad or as rude as her.

She gives too many quizzes based on the chapter book that has nothing to do with the tests and count very little. Her notes have no writing on them and she doesn't even post them online, The firs quiz had math problems which we did very little in class.

She was unhelpful and her lectures were so boring her tests are mix of multiple choice fill in he blanks definitions and explain why this or that is tha happens. They were some of the hardest test I ever took.

analysis.name: Yayi Fu
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
The worst math teacher/teacher I've ever had in my life. I don't like being mean but she REALLY needs to change.

Don't take this class if you dont have a tablet of some kind because the only notes are fill in the blank and she does not slow down EVER.

She almost never explains anything and just reads from her PowerPoint.

The lectures are just bad. She goes very fast and reads straight out of her notes. Exams are odd, a lot of reproducing proofs from class/notes, but also then easier to study for. She does a decent job picking reasonably easy problems and grades generously, but definitely plan to supplement lectures with her notes and other texts.

Worst instructor ever, only read her notes on lecture as a reading software does. HW and exam are not relavent, HW super difficult no one can finish without using ChatGPT, exams are all about proof theorems in the notes, which became writing and memorizing for almost everyone, if every instructor teach like her, UWMadison math department are done

Yayi Fu unfortunately only reads/fills out her PDF on her tablet, and does not really engage in the class. Nothing is explained intuitively,  but instead through theorems, lemmas, and axioms. Lectures are brutally boring, and it makes me question why I should ever show up. The TA, Elizabeth Hankins, is super nice though! She is super helpful.

Took this in the spring the lectures are b- quality but the final was way beyond the scope of the review and completely went over topics heavily studied in the class and was honestly frustrating to take

analysis.name: Ivan Ermakoff
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The warnings are true, professor Ermakoff doesn't allow any technology in his class. Initially apprehensive of this, I did find this to be somewhat valuable as it did help me learn. He's very knowledgable in the field but I found it to be intimidating to have to comment on his work. He is a very kind grader though.
One of my favorite classes I have taken during my time at UW! Definitely challenging, but well worth it and applies broadly across the social sciences. I would highly recommend!

Amazing professor!!! If you have the time to read definitely take this course. It's very challenging and you have to actually do the work but you will learn so much!! The professor is so knowledgeable and seemed to really care about our class doing well. 10/10
(graded on 3 exams, 2 comments, and participation in lecture)

Ermakoff is a little tough, but he is an amazing and brilliant lecturer and I very much admire him and was very happy to be in his class! Honestly one of my favorite classes I have taken at UW. He could be a pretty funny guy at times too, and we had a snack in each class. Highly recommend! Yes, there is a lot of reading, but it is doable.

Great class but be ready to read, we go through many great authors covering states/regimes, revolutions, and collective action. Could not recommend this class more to those interested in political sociology. Put in the work and you will see results!

analysis.name: Wendy Fritz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Wendy is an exceptional professor! She always encourages her students to think outside of the box and wants the best for them!! I agree with the post below that some of the policies required by the WSB make the course feel more challenging than it might otherwise be, but MHR 300 is just a class you have to take. Not necessarily easy or hard.

The material for this class is not very hard, however, the grade cap for the class makes it very tough to get a good grade in the class. Wendy is such a caring person and is willing to do anything to help you succeed. There are quizzes every other week based on the textbook reading. Most of your grade is on the team projects which are pretty tough.

Wendy is brilliant, caring, deeply experienced, and very creative. She has decades of XP as a team leader in F-500s, but the care of the best school teacher you could ask for. She rewards effort and creativity far above rote memorization. That said, the WSB imposes course limitations that make the class artificially hard. Be honest, & study hard.

analysis.name: Misha Finney
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She only ever reads off of the slides and her exam questions are not anything what she tells you they will be or how the study guide was structured. Her grading style and technique makes no sense and she takes a level 100 WAY too serious

Misha is a nice person but an awful teacher. Her lectures are just her reading the slides or saying the exact information from the book. Sometimes I feel as though she doesn't know what she is talking about. Much preferred the TA for teaching. Can't recommend.

Do not take this professor.  Exams=beyond difficult. Exams had nothing to do with what we learned in class.  The exam questions end up being random statistics and facts that were never taught in the first place.  Average exam scores are around 65%, but the rest of the class is easy.  Sitting through her lectures is also hard.  Hope this helped!

The lectures were easy to follow along with; taking notes and actively participating is very important for actually understanding the material though. Misha was great; she is energetic and passionate about what she does, and this clearly comes through in her lectures. She is very easy to reach as wel through email and before/after class.

CS&D 240 is the last class i'll ever have to take with dr. finney but oh my god i will not rest until this woman changes her canvas habits. misha, if you're reading this: let students see their quiz answers. let them turn in their cheat sheet later than 5 days in advance?? let them have scratch paper. hours will be saved. the world will rejoice

analysis.name: Maurice Fabien
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Fabien is a very smart man and is clearly evident when giving lectures. Only complaint I have is that the lectures were sometimes a bore and went off on tangents. Homework was hard at times, but there wasn't much of it, maybe 3-4 hours of outside work a week. Exams on the other hand were easy and mimiced the practice exams greatly.

Fabien was one of the nicest professors I've ever met. The class itself is really hard but I went to office hours often and he was really understanding when I asked for an exam regrade. I did well in the class due to hard work and lots of studying before midterms. The practice exams are very accurate to the actual thing

Dry lecture style, especially compared to some other profs. Hard to stay engaged. Maurice didn't really go above and beyond in any way, just explained the material as it is. Tests are worth almost your whole grade, but course is structured in a way that if you go to discussion, do the homework, and seek help when you need it, you should be fine.

Professor has a clear and concise (but dry) way of explaining material in lecture, but this is a quick moving class. Attend office hours or MLC for all the matters you are unclear about because he's great at answering specific problems. Three tests are 87% of your grade with a max. ~1% curve so study well in advance because it's unforgiving.

Although he was really nice and was happy to answer questions (which I appreciated), I will say that the lectures were very boring and structured weirdly. Very hard not to fall asleep. And very much a tough grader. Unfortunate how well I did on midterms, only for test anxiety to take the best out of me on the final and for my entire grade to fall.

analysis.name: Kate Fu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Super easy class. Did not like the drawing portion at the start of the semester, but the CAD modelling was easy and I actually learned a lot, all be it mostly on my own. The final project was decently time intensive but it really depends on your group. Kate herself was a very kind and caring person.

Professor Fu is a kind professor who is easy to access. However, the lectures are somewhat boring and don't have much to do with anything grade-related. The weekly homework assignments weren't bad, but some of the SolidWorks assignments were annoying. 

If you enjoy using SolidWorks, you should have no problem with this class.

Attendance was mandatory for discussion but not lecture.Her class was easy as long as you did your work. Assignments where you get walked through SolidWorks more would be helpful instead of throwing people into the deep end. She was super accommodating of mental health issues, being super flexible with extensions and I felt like she genuinely cared

The class is very easy and you seriously don't need to attend lecture after the drawing unit. She doesn't like when people whisper during lecture. When you get to Solidworks, use your lab time to get it done. They don't take long, but you will probably get stuck on something and having your TA to help is nice. Lots of opportunity for extra credit.

While I agree with people here that there are issues with the class structure as a whole, Dr. Fu was a good professor. I had trouble a few weeks into the CAD portion of the class and reached out, and she set aside time to meet with me (while 9 months pregnant) and sit down and work through the projects together. Very understanding and helpful.

analysis.name: Jennifer Franck
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor! For EMA 200, a class typically taken by freshmen, Prof. Franck went beyond just teaching course material. She encouraged students to network, build LinkedIn profiles, and get involved in activities outside the classroom to foster personal and professional growth early on. 10/10 experience.

Professor Franck was my first professor in the engineering department, and I couldn't have asked for more. She genuinely cared about each person in the class (25 people) and got to know them on a personal level. Furthermore, she was very helpful whenever you had a question. I am very excited to possibly have Professor Franck in the future!
Had her in Fall of 2024. She was absolutely amazing. We had a final project building a wind tunnel which was very fun to do.
Excellent Professor, made the intro course super fun!

She is really just a poor teacher. She has a horrible office hour once a week at an inconvenient time and is less than responsive on email and piazza. When she does answer questions online she doesn't answer the question, she just asks you a question or tells you to literally google it. Her lectures are exceedingly dry as she reads off the slides.

analysis.name: David  Fields
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Pros: I really enjoy Prof. Fields's lectures! They cover very interesting and broad topics. I can see that he cares about his students, and he is passionate about teaching. Many readings (it's a history class, so it's fine). Recommend this course.

Professor Fields is a great and entertaining lecturer. His course guidelines and expectations are clear, and he provides all materials necessary for any student to succeed! He also encourages extracurricular academic engagement, always promoting relevant and interesting guest lectures that complement course materials!
So extremely interesting and funny in the exact way all male history professors are. Loved him and his class. As long as you show up and do the reading you'll be alright

analysis.name: Florian Heimerl
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 71 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
Florian's lectures are largely pointless. He describes everything he does in excruciatingly gruesomely minute detail without ever actually explaining anything. He gives no reason behind what he does, he just describes what he's doing. 
Also, why is he whispering at the end of every sentence? It just makes it hard to hear. He isn't Bob Ross.

His way of giving lectures--that overly indulgent, magnanimous speaking cadence--is so slow and grating that it is impossible to pay attention. Speaking slowly and verbosely only makes it harder to listen and more painfully slow and boring. I ended up skipping lectures because the class is very easy anyway.

Lectures were super slow, watching them online at 2x speed is more useful than actually paying attention in lecture, however, his lectures were very helpful when trying to understand topics. Class was very disorganized though, as projects were unclear and just everything didn't seem to be proofread at all. Exams aren't super difficult though.

Florian is a great professor for a terrible class. His lectures on data structures and algorithms are clear and easy to understand, and the homework is manageable as long as you are not juggling five more classes. The projects are easier than those of CS300, but they are extremely dull—also, there are absolutely no drops, which is bad.

Not available outside of class. I have to watch other professors' lectures just to stay on the course path. At the time of writing this, he is currently behind a full lecture. The group projects are stupid and I am stuck with goobers as partners. I try to reach out for help, but no response. Without a doubt, the worst professor I have ever had.

analysis.name: Ralph Grunewald
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Grunewald is SUPER passionate about this content. It makes his lectures super fun to attend and the coursework engaging. However, one of his TAs is awful and made the class horrible. This made discussions unhelpful and, honestly, made the course content more confusing. However, this does not reflect on Grunewald.

Professor Grunewald is great!! He made SOC 131 so intriguing, especially the Fourth Amendment unit, which I did not expect to find so interesting, but it got me thinking and wanting to learn more about the Constitution in law. I wanted to go to every lecture because they were so amazing, and tests aren't bad either if you pay attention and review!

The professor can be rude and dismissive, assuming questions reflect poor attendance. TAs and the professor are often not on the same page. The Bluebook portion of exams is tough, so students must prepare independently.

Good Professor overall, however some of his content was not relevant to the tests. Discussion section is mandatory, and there are readings due every week (textbook/related articles). Some of the content that was presented on the midterms/final was not covered heavily in class but rather brushed over at times.

Easy class, lectures I found to be boring&unneccessary.  Basically everything is graded by your TA so hope you get a good one.  There were like a hundred pages of reading assigned every week but I never did any and got an A pretty easily.  Quizzes/midterms are online, and for the written part you are given the questions so its just memorization

analysis.name: Gregory Pac
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 92 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Really loved Pac. His lectures are funny and he puts effort into making boring content applicable and relatable. He provides tons of extra credit opportunities and is always open to questions and office hours. Wish I had the chance to take another class with him - will miss his jokes and tangents

This professor is very passionate about economics and it shows. He comes with great background of experience in the world of business. However, sometimes his handwriting is hard to read and that made it confusing. Class needs a lot of outside time to reinforce subjects because he moves very quickly but overall great lectures to attend!

Not sure what all the hate is about but I thought he was a good-natured guy, if not a little awkward.  Lectures were a little boring but were very helpful, and exams weren't anything we hadn't been over multiple times in lecture.  There were many opportunities for extra credit, and he allowed a large curve which I thought was nice.

This class is completely doable by just doing the work. Professor Pac is very lenient with his grading policies, giving many extra credit opportunities. The class is organized and there are no surprises on the exam. If you simply pay attention in lecture, actually go through the mind taps and discussion worksheets you will get an A.

I love this man. Genuinely if you go through an Econ major at UW without getting to listen to Prof. Pac lecture, I feel so sorry for you. He is fun and engaging, and teaches you real world skills that you can be sure you'll actually use. Helpful and engaged in office hours, I've never had a better professor that I could tell actually cares. 12/10

analysis.name: Julia Greenberg
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's fine but I would never choose to take a class with her or take this class. The class itself is very very slow and lectures were not great. I'm sure it could be worse professor wise but I really hated this class in terms of content, it was so boring and slow. TA/lab section was great and actually felt useful for my future.

This class is VERY tedious, but with the amount of extra credit opportunities, your attention to detail to the rubric for assignments, and by using the textbook to study for exams, you should be fine. I didn't find Greenberg's lectures very helpful for the actual graded material (she rambles), the TA you get really determines your grade the most.

PSYCH 225 is a very tedious class in general, but Dr. Greenberg helps to make it a little bearable. The exams are straightforward and are similar to practice problems from lecture and the textbook. Highly recommend taking notes from the textbook. Research proposal and labs can be tedious bc rubric isn't always clear so you can lose a lot of points.

225 is tedious and slow, but Greenberg is informative and well-structured, and the knowledge is beneficial. Labs are easy if you have a good TA; easy exams; RP is done mainly out of class, which is annoying, but practical knowledge in the long run. You lose points for nitpicky things, which is avoidable if you take the time to follow APA.

Asked her questions during office hours, and she just looked at me and expected me to suddenly know the answer. Exams were confusing, a lot of questions seemed like they can have more than one answer. No clear grading criteria on anything, so you have to guess and hope you hit everything. TA is super helpful though.

analysis.name: Paul Hooker
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 98 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Hooker was the best STEM professor I've ever had (both 103 and 104). I struggled initially learning how to study and keep up with heavy and hard coursework. I got a C on the first 103 midterm, started going to office hours and ended up getting an AB in the class. He was very motivational while being realistic and gave great feedback!

Dr. Hooker was an amazing professor who made Chem 103 a super enjoyable and manageable course. If you do the readings, pre-lecture activities, and show up to lecture, you should get an A. His lectures struck the perfect balance between entertaining and informative, and the notes he took on the slides were SO helpful to my understanding of content.

Professor Hooker genuinely cares about his students and is very approachable outside of class. His lectures are clear and thorough. Chemistry isn't easy, so readings take time, but expectations are always clear. Exams are fair. The midterms test your ability to apply concepts, while the final is easier. Highly recommend going to office hours.

Professor Hooker is an incredibly engaging and funny lecturer. Lectures were very well organized and he is a very clear instructor, although he sometimes got behind. Quiz and exam problems were great to build on knowledge instead of just being repetitions of problems in class. He was an even better instructor outside of class during office hours.

Paul Hooker is the best chemistry teacher in the UW-Madison chem department. Chem 103 is a rigorous course, but Paul prepares you well. Lectures reflect quizzes and exams. Also, he is very entertaining during his lectures. He teaches in a way where you want to learn more. He has a soothing voice and a british accent which accentuates the lectures.

analysis.name: Hina Mahmood
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The course itself is a bit dry but her straight, to-the-point teaching style makes it easy to understand difficult topics. She takes time to explain concepts and diagrams in detail, and asks for understanding before moving on to a new topic. She also revises concepts in every lecture and goes over things multiple times to reinforce understanding.

This course is not easy, but the prof is pretty good. She is accessible outside the class and always willing to answer questions. Lectures are helpful in understanding the material, as she explains concepts in detail. Homeworks  and exams were pretty fair. Do not take this course if you are not willing to learn and looking for an easy A.

Nice and supportive prof, very easy to talk to and cares about her students. Quickly responds to email inquiries. If you attend lectures, keep up with the readings and homeworks, you will be fine. Final exam was pretty easy. Would definitely recommend her!

This course is inherently difficult but she puts in every effort to make the lectures engaging and encourages student participation. She may not answer every question during the lecture due to time constraints, but is super approachable and helpful outside the class. She often runs over her office hours to ensure all student questions are addressed

Dr. Mahmood is a super nice prof who actually cares about students a lot. Although I was officially enrolled in another section, she helped me whenever I went to her office hours. Her ability to explain complicated concepts in simple language is amazing. Not many professors make the effort to ensure that students truly understand the material.

analysis.name: Kael Hanson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely atrocious. He makes multiple mistakes every lecture and clearly never goes through the lecture slides before class. Bro's learning it with us... I swear if he says "ya know" one more time:(((((((( Like no, actually, I don't know. When he talks...wait nvm actually y'all know what I'm talking about...moving on...

He's a nice guy, no personality issues. He's passionate about physics, planes specifically, which is great for him, and nobody else. His slides are word dense and aren't that relevant to what showed up on the midterm at all. In fact, his unit, according to the other instructors was one of the "easier" ones. It was the lowest midterm average for us.

While he seems like a lovely person, Prof. Hanson is a confusing, unorganized lecturer. He is too smart to be teaching an intro physics class, and does not explain concepts for our skill level. Tough class, tough professor. I would take with someone else, but odds are you don't have a choice.

HORRIBLE PROFESSOR! Didn't know what he was talking about during any of his lectures because his stuttering was to hard to understand, acted as if this was his first time ever doing physics (got example problems wrong when doing them). No one in the MANDATORY NON-RECORDED lectures understood his attempts at teaching during his entire unit. HORRIBLE

Hanson is definitely a nice guy, and I appreciate that he tries to make class fun with cool demonstrations.  But, at the end of the day we all just want A's. He doesn't teach you anything you need to know for exams, or work through any relevant example calculations in lecture. Everything I learned was either self-taught or taught by youtube.

analysis.name: Jonathan Gallimore
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 186 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Over-hated in my opinion, however is not great. Lectures extremely fast despite randomly letting us leave 10 minutes early. Every single homework assignment is the most useless and repetitive BS you will ever do. Tests were extremely straightforward. You CAN receive an A despite never opening the book. Like everyone else has said, DO EXTRA CREDIT.

dr. gallimore paints himself as this guy who wants the best for you, but my god he's terrible at teaching. he spams the same tedious assignment structure every week and the class in total has 5 exams, pretty excessive for an "intro" level course. also the exams have hyper-specific questions, so it's difficult to make useful study notes.

The class is interesting however the tests are really hard. Even if you go to lecture, do readings, etc the questions that are asked on the test are really specific. Also, the last unit test is right before finals week. So the cumulative final is 3 days following a unit test. This dropped my grade right before the end of the semester from an A.

His lectures are basically him reading right off the slides. He says he wants to set you up for success but makes the exams way harder than they need to be. He also gives no proper study material or actually helpful homework. I would not take this class if you aren't a good test taker. There are other classes more worth you time than this one.

Overall, the class is straightforward if you do the work and study. However, I found the professor condescending and belittling. His communication was very passive aggressive. Additionally, he would consistently point out material in class saying it was going to be on the exam, but it never was. Exams often contained irrelevant details.

analysis.name: Nick Hill
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely terrible. He has a horrible attitude that is only matched by his highly inflated ego. Rude and disrespectful. One of those professors that makes you wonder how someone gets into the teaching career.
Seems to be okay in the lab videos but god help you if he responds to your piazza post. Might as well be asking a brick for help. Super unhelpful and likes to respond in riddles

WORST INSTRUCTOR OF MY LIFETIME. As a 4.0 STEM student, he is the most useless instructor I've had. I use all provided resources on my own before asking for help and I've never struggled w/ any ochem concepts. His Piazza responses are unnecessarily rude, beyond unhelpful, and he exhibits no regard or support for his students especially being online

This class is a joke. Teaching staff (minus the TAs) are not helpful, and Hill especially is not helpful whatsoever and rude on Piazza. Please take the O-chem boot camp at a different campus and transfer it over vs. taking this class. For a 2 credit class, this class expects too much out of its students. Do better.

If I could rate zero, I would. He would routinely insult students, not answer questions, and just made even the most limited of interaction insufferable. I don't know what this dudes problem is, but honestly the entire 344 crew is garbage. Madison deserves better.

analysis.name: Oh Hoon Kwon
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 84 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This is class is tough especially if you're not good at math but he is there to offer help.  He is a tough grader though and could be a little more sensitive in that respect but he is a good guy, but be prepared for difficult tests.  But he lets you correct them for points back.

Oh Hoon is the sweetest man ever. You can really tell that he cares about his students and wants them to do well. He makes this class really easy to do well in. All of the tests cover the exact material that's on the homework sheets given in discussion. Would definitely recommend.

Spends all of class teaching us the math which makes it much easier to learn instead of us guessing what to do. He constantly asks if we understand and for feedback on the homework and tests. He really seems to care about our class and about this math program. Would highly suggest Oh Hoon.

Oh Hoon Kwon is a caring but unorganized professor. I never used the book even though he said that we should. The subject matter wasn't hard but the way that it was taught made it difficult. I recommend going to every lecture as that is when I learned the most. He would give the subject matter of each test and quiz the lecture before the test/quiz.

Well he did not assign any readings but asked to read the textbook because he said his lecture was going to be a brief outline of what we need to study. It was quite obvious which parts in the textbook were important or not. Do not miss his lectures. It was boring because I already knew the stuffs but if you are new lectures would be very helpful.

analysis.name: Marcella Hayes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: You can tell she is passionate about history. Gives good feedback, grades leniently and also encourages, but doesnt force, participation. Attendence matters. Only thing is, she talks alot throughout the entire lecture and often drops names/dates without any proper explanation/context. Overall solid teacher, would reccomended the course

Really caring, structures the class well so you learn how to make a good argument. TA graded pretty easily. Lectures can be a bit dense but it's like she's sharing juicy gossip so it was super entertaining. She just wants what is best for the students so def would rec!

Lectures are important to attend, but engaging and interesting. Hayes cares about helping her students succeed, and was very helpful in office hours. Readings are helpful but you don't need to do them all. Grade is participation and writing-focused. Would recommend!

her lectures are super interesting and based on a lot of her own research, which is super cool for an intermediate class. graded on three essays, a midterm, and participation. would definitely recommend her class
All of the staff that I encountered was wonderful! The ambiance is very nice, what you would expect from a fine dining steak house.

analysis.name: Rania Huntington
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is extremely strict and never shows any leniency when it comes to attendance.
Lots of fun stories and good enviroment.

Despite this class being very new in UW, I love it! Rania is extremely helpful outside the class. I did my essay review with her, and she gave very helpful tips to meet her expectations. Really responsive through emails. Classes can get a little bland but not too bad. Readings can get heavy, just prepare ahead of time. Very easy class.

I took 3 of her classes (EA 321, EA 322, and EA 371 Journey to the West).  Rania Huntington is an excellent professor. She's very passionate about the subject and helpful outside of class (from giving students research materials for projects to job recommendations). review_highlights.comment: Nothing is explained properly, the workload is ridiculous, and every assignment feels like punishment instead of learning. It wastes time, kills motivation, and somehow makes everything harder than it needs to be.
It's my favorite class this semester. Ms Parthy is so nice!
The course organization is pretty effective. Parthy really created a welcoming environment for us to study English and socializing. The atmosphere of the course is engaging.
Love her class! She is super clear and tells you exactly how to do all the parts of a paper. If you pay attention and ask what you're not sure about, you will do well.

Parthy did an amazing job transitioning to online instruction. She's extremely organized. This made my online learning experience top-notch. ESL118 is hard, but if you do exactly what she says, you won't be disappointed. Parthy is someone that other teachers need to learn from when it comes to transitioning to online classes. She's one of the best!

analysis.name: Quentin  Riser
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Riser has easily become my favorite professor at UW. He is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches and is a great mentor. His lectures are interesting, and he is extremely funny. He genuinely cares about the success of his students and encourages them to be the best researchers, learners, and leaders they can be.

Q is a great professor! He is very invested in his students' well-being and success in his classes. His material in his classes is beneficial, and I feel like I got a lot from them. I find myself laughing in every single one of his classes and wanting to participate in class! I highly recommend taking one of Q's classes!

Q's graduate seminar "Families and Poverty" was an insightful and meaningful course! I appreciate when instructors incorporate applied activities, and he excelled at this (my favorite was a class debate). It's clear that Q has a wealth of expertise to learn from, and is committed to student success. Also, he's funny! Classes were always a good time

Q is not a standard professor, but more like a fun camp counselor while still being very educated. He will always have strong connections with people in his classes, and if you ever need to take a class with him as the professor always choose him

Riser is a GREAT prof! He is somewhat new to SoHE. Very understanding, communicative, and funny. Grading criteria was clear, super responsive to emails, and an overall nice guy. I am also a student in his research lab, his work is very interesting. Riser is teaching Families&Poverty in the Spring (asynchronous Fridays).

analysis.name: Daniel Quint
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Amazing class, amazing lecture. The reason my rate is low is because of the fact that he grades on an INVERSE curve.... I ended with a 94.4 and that equated to an AB instead of an A... Really dissapointing. Other than that, he is GREAT!!!!

Definitely my favorite class taken at UW. No need for prior law knowledge either, you actually get to learn some pretty interesting stuff throughout the class. Lectures were great, lots of real life examples pertaining to the content every class, and stories from his personal life that also relate. 75 min lectures were a breeze.
Great class but inverse curve hurt. Shoutout Martha the TA you are awesome.

amazing, incredible, showstopping. i love this man. this course was the highlight of my entire time at uw. the content is challenging but he teaches it very well, and discussion sections are very helpful to practice the material. every econ major should take this class!!!!

Dan is a great guy, and his lectures are very interesting. I don't think they're necessary to get a decent grade in his class because the class itself isn't terribly challenging. That said, they're really interesting and I think it's well worth your time to attend. Definitely my favorite class at UW as an undergrad.

analysis.name: Amy Quan Barry
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is for ENG169 - Poetic Forms, which wasn't listed above. Prof. Barry is a very good teacher, and if you attend all the classes there's nothing to worry about. However, make sure you do not miss any classes, because your grade will tank. There is also some memorization involved in the midterm, so watch out for that.

No textbooks but 'makes her own' book you have to buy for like 27$ 
other than that, easy A if you go to class and do the weekly questions.

AQB is really passionate about poetry. Kind of strict, but you can tell she really enjoys her field. Tends to often dominate class discussion. Would require a student presentation but never left enough time for a proper presentation and would constantly but in during presentation. Overall solid teacher but you have to go with the flow

Very efficient with time, makes a single 2 hour period feel more useful than three regular lectures. Will often drop useful tidbits (e.g., "imitative fallacy") as a quick aside - be prepared to jot these down, or you may found you've missed half the material in the class. Great choice of readings.

Funny and intelligent. She gives really good feedback and keeps class structured nicely. She's a bit of an oddball, but, overall, definitely a good professor. Maybe there's a big difference between how she teaches grad classes and undergrad, but I definitely recommend her if you're taking undergrad.

analysis.name: Qiongshi Lu

review_highlights.comment: He wants his students to succeed and directly told our class if we show up and do the homework, we should get an A

Professor Lu's lecture is just okay. He just take screnn shots from papers and put them in his powerpoint. This leads to lots of inconsistent notations. He doesn't care if the students understand, and just keeps moving forward with the lecture. Unlike other professors, Qiongshi is not patient to his students. Overall I don't see him enjoy teaching.

analysis.name: Quanda Johnson

Despite taking months to grade short assignments and often posting assignments days before they were due, she gave  students no flexibility. Save yourself a headache.
One of the best profs I've had at UW-Madison
Awesome teacher. Makes every student feel seen and heard.

I took a class with Dr.Johnson this summer and it is amazing! The course name is AFROAMER 225 . I even dropped one of my required class to take this class. I love the classroom atmosphere which is encouraging and discussion-based.I would recommend all my friends to take her class. If I have the chance I would definitely take her class again!
I took this class for Comm B, and found Quanda to be really patronizing. We were assigned a text that was basically rules for writing a paper that should have been learned in high school.

analysis.name: Quentin Dudley

review_highlights.comment: Prof Dudley was very kind and clearly puts a lot of effort into being a good prof. He was a bit unorganized (his first semester teaching 326) but he provided lots of resources and was fair. His HWs and exams were straightforward and he offered extra credit. I think once he gets into the groove of a class he will be a department favorite.

Required us to get 2 textbooks, recommended 4 total to us, and then pulled from and cited other textbooks we do not have access to. If you hand write your notes, it will be impossible to keep up as his lectures are often prewritten. Nice guy, but has poor organizational skills. Often posted necessary homeworks or solutions late.

Lectures were really slide heavy and sometimes a bit disengaging because they were 75 minute power lectures. Professor Dudley was willing to meet outside class and go through hw problems and exams if needed which was helpful. I think the more times he teaches the course, the better it will be, because I know he is a newer professor.

Lots of material covered in lectures, sometimes unclear what we needed to know. However since it was a small class he was available to communicate one-on-one with students and provided constructive feedback.

analysis.name: Rajula Srivastava
