review_highlights.comment: As others have mentioned, she teaches this class as if everyone has taken calculus before. She spends way too much time on simple concepts and nowhere near enough time on topics that actually need it. Her class is fine to take if you've taken calculus before and have some kind of background knowledge, but otherwise do not.

Came into this course with only Pre-Calc experience from high school. Would not recommend this course if you are in a similar situation as I felt behind and confused almost every lecture. She went over content very quickly, assumed you had seen the topics before and didn't really help during office hours instead just brought up unnecessary content.

Rajula is an incredibly intelligent person, however, she was not very good at teaching concepts. I came from a pre-calc background, and was learning a lot of things for the first time. I would come out of lectures extremely confused and ended up having to reteach myself majority of the concepts. Use the MLC if you want to get a good grade.

Srivastrava is okay, you can tell shes real knowledgeable and also will take the time to explain something to you if you dont get it, but theres nothing that stands out in particular as an exemplary teaching trait. Wouldn't shy away from taking another course with her, but I wouldn't necessarily be overly exuberant to

I liked how she made the classroom atmosphere light! She was great at articulating her words during lectures. Her slides pace were a bit fast, but she always went back and gave up class time for midterm/ exam review. Overall, she was great (coming from someone who has never taken calculus).

analysis.name: Rajiv Rao

review_highlights.comment: Profe Rajiv is great. You can tell he really loves phonetics, and he makes is easy to understand for us, keeps things light and interesting, and it super enthusiastic. Great guy, great class, would highly recommend.

Rajiv is a great professor! I learned so much in his class, and even though I thought I would hate phonetics, Rajiv actually made it interesting and fun! He explains everything so clearly and will never make you feel like you're asking a stupid question! He also wants all of his students to get an A, which is super nice! Take phonetics with Rajiv!
GREAT TEACHER! Rajiv is so personable and kind to every student. Extremely flexible and makes assignments where you learn but don't get overworked.
Literally the coolest professor ever. I hate linguistics so so much, but Rajiv actually made it fun and engaging.

Hands-down my fav professor yet! Loved his class & his teaching style so much I'm taking another class with him. Genuinely cares about his students and always has a smile on his face. analysis.name: Sean Paul
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: If you are thinking of taking a 234 class with this professor, then I would say try to avoid him at all costs. He is really smart, and he thinks that everyone is as smart as he is. He does not understand  that I am a beginner knowing nothing about the materials and trying to learn new stuff!

When your professor says you are supposed to get stuck in one of the questions of a MIDTERM and you lose 20 points because you are "supposed to". You know something wrong. Many people told me you will lose nothing in attending lecture, well, I both lost time and self confidence after each of his lecture. 0/10, would not recommend

Sean Paul is the worst professor at UW. A good grade isn't too difficult because his exams are straightforward. However, you won't learn anything from him. The textbook is extremely useful resource so read it and do all the practice examples. Make sure you go to class though because he announces random changes only in lecture. Doesn't answer emails

analysis.name: Rebecca Glawtschew
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 88 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr G is very knowledgeable about the material in Econ 301, I'd honestly say she's a great professor. The course is very exam weighted, but that's honestly the nature of all Econ courses. I learned a lot despite the material at times being filled with 'jargon.' HIGHLY recommend attending her office hours, if you struggle with material in the course.

There is no excuse for doing poorly in this class. Each chapter has a study guide and practice problems attached. Between that and the weekly problems sets all should prepare you for the tests. I though she was very nice and truly tried her best to make everything comprehensible. She was always available during office hours or to talk after class.

Dr. G is amazing. She seems unapproachable at first but just go to her office hours and you'll see how helpful and sweet she is. She really just wants her students to succeed. You have to work hard in the class to get an A, but if you go to her office hours, your life will be so much easier. Just trust me, she is a great teacher if you try.

I really enjoyed this course! Prof. G's lectures were extremely clear and greatly support learning. Furthermore, outside of lectures, she provides an immense amount of resources made to aid our success and understanding. The wrap-ups and exam reviews were specifically helpful as they reflect exam structure and content. Exams are graded quickly too

Class really only depends on exams - of which 3 are midterms and one is a final. Midterms are more difficult than anything in problem sets and one is 2 days after you come back from thanksgiving and a week before final which is annoying. Other profs have 2 midterms. Do questions from the textbook I have seen she picks a bunch from there.

analysis.name: Steve Trost
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Trost is organized and clear about what he expects of you. He is knowledgeable and great at explaining things. He seems like a cool guy, too. 20% of the grade was 2 online quizzes, in which the lowest of the 2 was completely dropped, which was nice. Only downside is that lectures felt long at times. All in all though, Trost is a great professor.

Took 101 as first-ever econ class and Trost was perfect professor to teach it. Made concepts easier to understand and provided plenty examples in lecture to help explain things. 3ish easy hws per chapter. 3 quizzes (2 online) and drops ur lowest, plus a final. Posts lectures, PowerPoints, and practice tests online which helps a lot for studying.

Steve is a great guy. Funny, and explains concepts really well. You're graded on a lot of things, which can really help your grade (Also offers extra credit if you attend half the lectures!). That being said, I did find his lectures incredibly boring at times. It's important stuff, but man is it hard to pay attention. Good guy, would take again.

Great professor. Interesting lectures with funny examples. Attendance is not required but going to at least half of the lectures will get you extra credit. The homework is very easy and helps you understand the concepts along with the discussion practice problems. As long as you put in decent effort and study well for tests you can do well.

Professor Trost is very knowledgeable in his field and cares deeply about the topics at hand. I would highly recommend making sure you pay close attention during lecture as if you have not taken an economics course before it can become confusing very fast. There is not much homework at all but I would highly recommend doing extra practice.

analysis.name: Saylin Alvarez
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Saylin is amazing! Your semester grade is based on 3- 2 page compositions (40%), 4-1 page essays (40%), participation (15%), and homework (5%). If you have any doubts on your paper, Saylin is always more than willing to help answer your questions. Spanish 311 with Saylin was easy and very fun! Highly recommended.

I could honestly write so many positive things about Saylin. She's a wonderful, caring, and hilarious teacher. I think its important to mention there's no "final" exams in her class, just quizzes, and a big group project that counts as your "final". It involves a video, essay, and a presentation. She also only speaks Spanish in class unless needed.

Saylín is the best! She is a super easy grader and very lenient with deadlines. There was one day we were supposed to write an in-class essay, but she just shrugged and said we didn't have to do it on the day of. The essays are also open-note.

Very kind and caring professor, who wants to see all of her students succeed. She will stop and make sure everyone understands. If you study a bit for the midterm exams, and put effort into everything else you can earn a good grade in this class.

Saylin is incredibly understanding, kind, and passionate about her work. The effort she put into her class did not go unnoticed! Homework was manageable and the criteria for projects were clearly stated. I highly recommend taking a class with her!

analysis.name: Mai See Thao
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She does not provide lecture slides, if you don't show up in lecture, the only way to recover the missing contents is asking another student for their lecture notes. There's also WAY too much reading, prepare to read at least 100 pages of a super boring anthropology research book almost every week and write your response on that.

Anthro 265 was way too much for an elementary course. We had book chapters assigned with 30 page readings every class. There were assignments due every week. She wanted a power lecture of 75 people to discuss out loud what we thought of readings. She seems like a sweet person, just a bad elementary professor. She would be better teaching a seminar.

Is the content interesting? Yes. Is it presented in a logical or introductory way? Absolutely not. Professor Thao presents slides in such an scattered and incomprehensible way that lecture content too dense to gather all tested information from. Readings have repeatedly exceeded 100 pages in a week and most assignments feel like are busy work.

Dr. Thao is a nice professor, but her class is not one that I would recommend to others. Lots of readings are assigned every week and due dates/the syllabus often had errors and were unclear. The lecture slides are paragraphs long and the content was usually thrown out and hard to understand. You have to teach yourself the concepts before tests.

Dr. Thao is a smart professor, but does not treat this class like an introduction to anthropology whatsoever. Do not expect to leave class with any understanding of the content. Tests aren't horrible, but you have to figure out the terms on the study guide on your own as the lectures do not help. Would be much better teaching actual anthro majors.

analysis.name: James Tinjum
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Tinjums slides are unorganized, there is a lot of homework and a lab and gives you more work then a 3 credit class should take. That being said, if you do the work, go to exam prep sessions it isnt that bad. He tells you essentially what will be on the exam so you know what to prep for. he even gives you part of the exam ahead of time.

James does not deserve the rating that he gets. He is a good professor and makes this class not that bad. He shows you basically everything that is on the exams, and grades pretty easy on some harder exams. He also likes his dad jokes. Go to lecture. You get extra time on the homework if you guess the correct score of one of his favorite teams

Nice guy but unorganized and terrible at teaching, The HW is basically a head first dive into the unknown. Studying for exams is tough cuz his lectures are all over the place and u never know exactly what ur supposed to learn. Ive never rated a prof before but i had to for him. Don't take this guy unless you want to teach yourself and waste time.

Homeworks don't have a clear point value assigned to each homework and grading seems a bit arbitrary. Relies very heavily on his spoken statements to quiz you, making you go back to listen to video lectures rather than just easily referenced slides. Seems like his goal is to simply keep you working rather than effectively communicate concepts.

I'm in my 7th semester of engineering here at Madison and Tinjum is one of the hardest professors I've had yet. His lectures are impossible to follow and his hw has absolutely no directions or expectations stated. I spend about 20 hours per hw assignment and still am barely passing this class. Do NOT take his class unless you absolutely have to.

analysis.name: Jeffrey Schmidt
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 74 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very straightforward when it comes to exams. He pulls his test questions from four sources: lecture, homework, discussion, and optional quizzes posted after every lecture on Canvas. If youre diligent in these four areas, there wont be a single problem you havent seen by the time you sit for an exam. Also, take the practice exams he posts.

He seemed to know the material very well however the way that he presented it in lectures was awful.  His powerpoint were absolutely terrible, I don't think I have ever seen such dense slides (looked like he typed up the textbook).  Luckily the second professor, Gary Shiu, did an excellent job of translating those slides when he  did lectures.

Dr. Schmidt is a very smart person but take a wrong way to teach general physics to Non-major student. Concepts are really not explained in lecture and important steps are sometimes skipped that make students even more confused. One good thing is that he provide some practice problem that could be similar to some exam questions.

Avoid his qm classes unless this is your second time learning qm. His lecture is fast but poorly explained. He follows his own notes instead of textbook but it doesn't align well with the lecture. The physics department took this course out of the major requirement instead of trying to improve it. I mean is it that hard to give us a TA?

Decent professor, but the coursework didn't connect well. The homework assignments were impossible and didn't help at all, and sometimes the discussion problems were too hard too. He's a fine professor and explains things in an understandable way, but the class doesn't connect well.

analysis.name: Thomas Purnell
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Purnell is a really awesome professor. His lectures were easy to follow, but if you don't attend the class they will not make sure. He is helpful in explaining content, if you don't understand a topic. The books that he assigned weren't necessary to pass the course. Overall, the class was interesting and enjoyable because of Purnell.

Overall the class went well, but it took a lot of extra work; the lectures weren't very helpful because he often ended up on tangents and examples used in class weren't relevant to the exams or HW assignments. Discussion was where the majority of learning happened.

Do not take this class. Lectures are mandatory, but are unhelpful and rarely relate to course material. Homework is confusing and graded harshly, even though key concepts are barely explained in lecture. Prof makes simple concepts sound complicated. Had to teach myself most of the content.

Not good. Lecture attendance was mandatory but never really relevant to what our assignments and tests were on, forcing me have to teach practically everything to myself. Lectures were a big waste of time and almost always boring as a result. The TA, Joe Moran, was fantastic, though!

316 with Tom was a pleasure. I'm not sure what others are talking about. He is one of the most accomplished researchers at UW, and he shares his expertise in a really accessible way. Great instructor. You don't have to work too hard to learn a lot, but you can't slack on the assignments (HW, and your take home "quiz" midterm & final). Recommended.

analysis.name: Uchita Vaid
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She creates a very positive and welcoming classroom environment and is approachable when students need help. Her lectures are engaging, and she explains concepts clearly with helpful examples that make the material easier to understand. I found the course enjoyable and would recommend taking her class.

Uchita is the most amazing professor I've ever had. DS 221 is such an interesting class, and her lectures are excellent. She responds to emails super fast, is always available outside of class, super knowledgeable, and is just a fantastic person overall. Plus, she even wrote a recommendation letter for me—truly a GOAT.

Class always had interesting content and she's a great speaker. The class wasn't challenging but I always appreciate a professor that actually teaches me new concepts in an engaging and educational way.

I hear a lot of complaining about this class and I don't get it. Attend lecture, take notes on what's NOT on the slides, then use print outs of the PP slides to fill in that information later. If you try to copy down everything she puts on the slides and nothing else, you'll miss a lot. This is college, people. Do the rdgs to ace multiple choice.

The professor makes this class really interesting even when the topics could be kinda eh. She really cares about participation and attendance, but she is also reasonable and it seems like she genuinely wants her students to succeed. Def take her class, so much relevant info to learn from her and the material. Also very well prepared.

analysis.name: Allison Powers Useche
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Actually one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. She is incredibly kind and caring. I am not the biggest fan of history but she made it surprisingly engaging. My TA was also amazing. He helped me with my other classes at the time. Overall would highly highly recommend.

If you're a STEM major looking for a lib studies class, look no further. Prof Powers genuinely cares about her students and class. She removed one of the main assignments because she didn't want to overload us. You should read the sources each week, if you do the class will be easy. Just a few writing assignments and two papers. Take this class!

While the readings every week sometimes felt lengthy, theres minimal work to pass this class. No exams just a few essays. Powers is the most compassionate and caring prof I've ever had. Gave extensions with no need for reasoning and while attendance was mandatory if you emailed her and explained why you were missing she'd give you the points.

She is a very kind and caring professor. She didn't mind shifting due dates or giving extensions to students. The lectures and readings were very interesting. There wasn't a ton of work for this class. As long as you paid attention and kept up with readings, the quizzes and papers were simple. This class was quite enjoyable.

I had zero interest in the subject matter, so I didn't enjoy the class, but that doesn't take away from the fact that professor powers is fantastic. She is very passionate about history and cares deeply about her students. The essays and quizzes were not difficult. Only take this class if you are somewhat interested in the subject matter though.

analysis.name: Caglar Uyanik
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

If you talk to him after class and pay attention to lectures you will know questions on the upcoming test. He seems like a cool guy, calc 3 was just really hard for me.

This lass is exam heavy but if you just pay attention to lectures and attend discussions it's easy to get an A. Doing really well in one exam can help a lot (it did in my case where I had 96 and 89 in midterms and 88 in final but overall was 92 which is borderline A) and first exam is really easy.

Professor Uyanik is very knowledgeable and has a great sense of humor. You will find this course easy if you attend the lectures and discussion sections. The only thing I regret about this course is not going to his office hours (partially because of the free chocolate I heard he gives out, haha).

Caglar is an awesome professor! He explains everything in lecture in a very thorough & engaging manner. The homework is challenging and time-consuming, but he often shifts due dates to accommodate if he feels the workload is too heavy. Despite this course challenging me, I didn't worry about my grade because he offered exam corrections at 1/2 cred.

He will still teach this accelerating classes next fall. If you are freshman and interested in math, just take this course with him. He is amazing and this accelerating classes is super helpful for learning knowledge. His lecture is legendary, it is enjoyable to study math when you have an amazing professor. He also care about his students.

analysis.name: Uri Andrews
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Funny. Wears cooL shirts. Goes off on tangents. Keeps you engaged. Currently wearing a shirt with two kittens in between a hamburger bun. My personal favorite shirt of his has a Llama sipping tea and saying "indeed".
Uri Andrews taught me how to take the limit of my grade as it approaches zero. Thank you.
Extremely clear during lectures. Proofs very easy to follow. However watch out for the homework and tests, they're very hard.

Notice for which classes he gets good reviews, and for which he does not. As for his teaching 542, he's clearly a logician, but still does a good job.
He's a great lecturer and is very funny. He tends to go on tangents about math but it's quite funny.

analysis.name: Óscar Useche

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed his class. It was pretty easy and mostly writing assignments. We do lots of peer reviews, and he gives thorough feedback quickly. He grades generously. Participation is mandatory, but I only spoke a few times and still got an A. Just show up and do the work. He is a nice guy and truly cares about his students.

Pretty good professor for a pretty boring course, generous with grades, gives good feedback, generally cares for his students and is a pretty nice guy overall. He is Colombian though so his accent and arrangement of words are a bit weird sometimes (his vocabulary and writing skills are great though!)

Overall, the class was a fun time. The Professor was a blast to have and always in a good mood. I would recommend participating in class when he asks questions or thoughts to get a good grade for attendance and participation. He does have a little bit of broken English, but can still understand clearly.

Oscar is a really funny and interactive professor! I participated in class discussions maybe 7 times and got an A for participation. He is very good at teaching the course content. It is an English class, so get ready to write a lot. He gives very good feedback on writing assignments.

Óscar Useche is a really personable professor. He does a thorough job explaining course content to make sure we understand the content. He also has scheduled meetings to make sure you are understanding the content. He provides helpful feedback on work and is a flexible grader. Would want him as a professor again!

analysis.name: Daniel Ussishkin
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Online canvas modules with weekly podcasts and a synchronous discussion. Lots of reading and weekly discussion posts. The homework is at times overwhelming with the essays. Sometimes it felt like he was more focused on themes of gender roles than the actual events of the WW1, but I did learn a lot about the societal background of the time.

History 350 is an online course with Usisshkin and was great overall. There is a lot of assignments and discussions because it is an online course so you have to stay on top of your work. The tests and papers have very clear grading and it's not hard to get an A if you try. He doesn't make WWI boring and is a great overall online class!
Pretty good professor! Lectures can be a bit unclear at times, but the slides + office hours are really helpful!

Professor Ussishkin was great. In a small seminar environment, he did a really good job of facilitating a super engaging discussion and you could tell he really cares about what he teaches. He's definitely not the clearest professor when it comes to putting stuff on canvas, but he's a super easy grader so if you put the effort in, you'll get an A.

I would absolutely take this class again, but it was not my favorite. Ussishkin isn't the best lecturer, but he's very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject and his students. I would say if you don't enjoy history to some extent, this class isn't for you. The class was basically pass/fail, so if you put effort in, you will get an A.

analysis.name: Luke Urbain
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: They are super friendly, a good listener, and validate your efforts. I never dreaded going to their class. Tests could be tough but always fair, and there were other things like writing, oral, and group activities that can help out your grade a lot. You could tell Luke cares about every student and their health

Luke is very passionate about Spanish, and wants his students to show their interest as well. Grading isn't too clear, as most assignments (papers) are graded based on specific parts of the writing, and so percentages aren't given. Be sure to use sites to double check translations if you want to be certain about your work.

Professor Urbain is great! He is very passionate about Spanish and student learning. He gives great feedback and sets you up for success. This course is easy and slow pace. I would definitely recommend Professor Urbain for this class.

Luke was great! Very easy to access outside of class. Participation is important for the class (as well as attendance), but he makes it so easy to earn your participation points. Grading is very clear.
Luke is a great instructor. He makes his lectures interactive and he's always very clear about deadlines and his expectations. He's prompt in grading and offers good constructive criticism.

analysis.name: Manolis Vlatakis
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Manolis is approachable, supportive, and genuinely enthusiastic about helping his students succeed. His lecture slides are detailed and easy to follow, and the pace of the class is well-balanced and manageable.

He is a goated professor. Never skipped his lecture. Got enrolled late in his class, one of the best decisions i could've made. He's really engaging and ensures everyone participates. Gives bonuses, but most important of all, he's really supportive. He'll be there for you, will stay hours longer in his OH but will ensure that concepts are clear.

The topic he taught is very hard but I genuinely enjoy coming to his class because of his enthusiasm. He not only enjoys teaching his class a lot but also enjoys helping the students actually understand the material.
Great and caring professor. Takes time to interact with the class and learns the names of everyone who regularly attends. Homework is long but interesting questions.

I took a gamble taking 577 with Manolis during his first semester teaching and it absolutely paid off. Manolis cares deeply about his students learning, and carries a passion in lecture that other teachers of 577 don't share. You'll get more out of this class if you participate more, but it is not part of the grading.

analysis.name: Peter Vranas
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Course is designed down to a science. Some readings are mandatory, others are not. Quizzes become increasingly difficult. Problem sets are consistently difficult. Exams are generally difficult. Generous grading for all assignments. One can reference an enormous catalogue of past content for additional help. The course is extremely rewarding.

He is organized and clear on what's expected of you. He always hands out the answers to the homework right after you turn it in, and the homework is always returned the next class. Textbook is not needed. He uploads practice problem sets and also every past exam since 2007 online. Be wary, the material in the third part of the course is very hard.

Logic can be dry but Prof. Vranas explains it very clearly. If you can manage to pay attention you should be well prepared to do well in the class. You will need to practice outside of class if you intend to do well. Also beware, this isn't a traditional philosophy course... it's more akin to math.

Logic changed me.
The most well-prepared class ever. Peter gives clear lectures throughout the semester and there's little confusion about content if you pay active attention to class
The last 2 weeks' content is challenging, so work on more problems. A very uncommon question appears on the final, but if you do RECENT past exams you should be good.

An OG if there ever was one. But seriously, great experience taking his logic class - amazing TA Jordan and Peter organized everything so well. The material itself is quite useful, the grading scale lenient, and the structure of the course is exceedingly logical - 'nuff said.

analysis.name: Viren Murthy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing guy! Sure, his course did include a lot of intellectual thought, but it's nothing dense. Three exams and one final paper. No need to do the readings.  Go over the terms on the study guides and understand the passages that he discusses in class.  Don't think you can get away with just looking at the slides... go to class!

Prof Murthy  knows his material very well, and is also good at telling them. Hearing him talking make me think that I'm reading a novel. History part is crystal clear, but u need a bit of talent to understand the philosophy and religion parts. He gives fair grade and 9% chance of extra credit. By the way he knows 6 languages. Nice professor.

Poor lecturer. Talks super slow, says exactly what's on the slides. Will ask questions, disagree with the answer, then say the same thing adding 0 extra details. Misquotes philosophers and thought "I am the state" was Henry VIII (it was louis XIV)

I was really looking forward to this course, so I went against my initial instinct to drop it-BIG MISTAKE. This class was incredibly difficult to get through; brutal might be a better descriptor. The professor spoke to us all as if we has the same level of understanding as he did on the topic (which we obviously didn't). All in all 0/10 do not take
Not the greatest teacher, but he does seem to be knowledgeable. His class is fairly easy if you can sit through his long and disorganized slideshows without falling asleep.

analysis.name: Sharon Thoma
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Thoma was very kind and welcoming in office hours and open to answering any questions you might have. She offered a lot of recreational activities to students like nature hikes and was very passionate about biology. Even though this was not my major, I still loved her lectures! Would recommend to someone looking to fulfill a bio credit

This class was incredibly challenging as a freshman last year, so be prepared to go to every single lecture because there is an insurmountable amount of content in each. PLEASE go to her office hours if you can! She is incredibly kind and will give you extra study materials. She WANTS to see you succeed! I finished the class as a better student.

Dr. Thoma's lectures are very engaging. You have to attend lectures to succeed in the class, since she does not post annotated lecture slides. Taking your own notes on the lecture slides is incredibly helpful for her class.Her exams ask very specific questions so you have to know the content inside out. The learning center packets are a lifesaver.

Best professor I have had in a LONG time. She is extremely knowledgeable and makes difficult concepts easy to digest. She taught the first 2 exams in BIO 101, and the 2 other exams were taught by 2 other random professors. I much preferred Thoma as she was the best at explaining biological topics in simple terms. Would 100000% take again.

Prof. Thoma is a great lecturer, and friendly to her students. This does not make the class easy- it is very fast paced, especially if you have no Bio experience. There are no projects or labs, so the exams are a huge part of your grade. Don't miss the videos or lectures- it'll be very hard to catch up without them.

analysis.name: Victor Jew
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

This professor provides NO structure and almost no relevant information. He rambles manically about stuff from 150 years ago. WHY are we paying so much to not learn anything? Interesting content, pretty manageable if you show up to lectures (mb with an energy drink or coffee), at the very least skim the readings, and watch the documentaries. Dr. Jew is definitely more old school than I think a lot of people are used to, but if you can't adapt to different teaching styles than this class is the least of your worries.

Slides are not helpful and his lecturing has useless yapping. He tells you to right down random stuff and gives readings that don't help. His tests are about a lot of random stuff that doesn't relate to what he says is important. He says the final exam has a written part, then tells you a week before that its actually a 5-8 page essay.

What does a circus and this class have in common? Clowns. This guy is funny and that's all to it. The classes are so damn boring, MC checks are stupidly written, and he makes up these "concepts" nobody cares about because they have never been spoken before. I want to drop it, but I'm almost done with the semester. This class makes me want to jump.

analysis.name: Veronika Kusumaryati
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

had her for anth 100. interesting lecs

analysis.name: Katie Vermillion Kalmon

Dr. Vermillion is an outstanding professor. She was originally a high school science teacher, and it definitely shows in the best ways. She made her lectures extremely interesting and easy to digest. Easy class. Attendance is required. It is an introductory course with tasks such as building a resume or planning your future. It is not hard, just do the assignments, and you'll get an A. Main assignments were the essay and the group project.

Easy class and nice instructor

Online course, grade will be an A/B. Online class- so super easy and only 4-5 grades total. 'lectures' are PDF's online and quizzes are every two weeks. VERY easy to understand, and he adds some chuckle-level comedy to them. great class, great prof. easy A

Straightforward, have to have good notesheet. Must use lectures and discussion for notesheet. Everybody saying exams were bogus probably did not go to discussion. Lowkey top 3 ME prof

This was the worst class I took in Uni. I hate the fact that the material was ruined for me due to the professor. Nothing good.

601 is hard. The TA is nice. The midterm is impossibly hard. The syllabus is too full and very math dense and not related to the homework. But the grading is okay, as there are extra credits. analysis.name: Michael Xenos

analysis.name: Lyn Van Swol

She was one of my favorite professors at UW Madison! She's funny and makes very interesting lectures. I liked listening to her talk which actually made me pay attention. analysis.name: Abiral Phnuyal

The essays are open-ended and therefore not difficult if you put in effort. There is a lot of reading and it can be tough to get through and understand as it's old stuff.

Abiral was very passionate and invested in what he was teaching, but it was easy to get started as someone with little background in Philosophy. He was easy to work with and made the whole class feel involved. This class had a lot of reading, but he gives that disclaimer at the beginning of the semester. Overall a great course.

analysis.name: Abigail Letak
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: The best. Super flexible and caring, you could tell she really enjoys both her students and subject matter. If you have a question about her class material or policies, just reach out to her, she wants to work with you! If you have a chance to take a class with her, do it!

Definitely one of my favorite professors. Her lectures were very easy to understand and follow, but you need to show up to lecture to pass. She made learning engaging & enjoyable. Abby is a fantastic teacher and she really is my favorite prof in this school. She is caring, humorous, and knowledgable, especially she is young. She gives great examples for difficult terms and explain them in simple ways. No exams just really easy quizzes. Attendance occupies a lot in final grade. Just go to class and you will be fine!

Professor Letak is great! Lecture attendance is mandatory, but she was always super understaning when I had to miss class due to sickness or other reasons. Assignments are spaced out well so it does not seem very overwhelming for a 4-credit course. She actually cares if students do well and tries to make things more understandable!

Professor Letak has been my favorite professor at UW so far. She is an amazing lecturer and really cares about her students health. There are 4 quizzes which aren't too difficult and she is always available to meet out of class time. Papers are relatively easy and she makes lectures super interesting. Highly recommend.

analysis.name: Seth Abramson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: He has this belief system that he is correct about everything because he studies major political figures as his job/passion and writes about them. I approached him with respect on a twitter account he doesn't know is mine and, as expected, he called me a rude name...
He knows what he'a doing and makes English class very pragmatic in nature. I'm very glad I took this class. He even bought pizza on the last day for everyone.
He is incredibly kind and very helpful in regards to proper English grammar.
Makes class really interesting and focused class on Criminal Justice.  Always welcomed questions about the outside world and how the legal system worked.  Recommend this class to everyone!

Seth is probably the smartest man I have ever had teach me. He genuinely cares about your success. His Metamodernistic spin to the class may be frustrating at first, but once you truly understand it, it's actually very interesting. analysis.name: Faisal  Abdu'Allah
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Professor Faisal's class is the best art class I have taken in three years. I took Art 348 Digital Printing (no option in rating). His expertise and friendliness are incredible. He teaches extra skills and field trips, is helpful, and appreciates you. This class forms a community like no other, and you learn about literacy as an artist. 
、

If you need someone to really challenge your work, Faisal is the professor to go to. He is constantly playing "devil's advocate" which can be a little frustrating at times, but it also sparks a lot of growth. Faisal has turned my head upside down more than a few times and is one of the most complex conceptual thinkers in the program.

I can't believe Faisal has only 2 ratings, best professor/teacher I have ever had. I was perpetually mind blown by his knowledge, experience, kindness, supportiveness, etc etc. I would recommend to take one of his classes no matter what your degree is. His class changed my perspective and encouraged me to continue pursuing art.

It's a learning community seminar, so he's probably easier on this class than in his true art classes, but it's pretty easy and a lot of fun. It's interdisciplinary, so no one's judged on skill and everyone's encouraged to experiment & go out of our comfort zones.

analysis.name: Rebecca Addington
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

Although she often read off the slides, she used great examples in the lectures that helped me remember concepts. Her tests were VERY fair. She also gave us an exam review sheet for every exam which was extremely useful.
Her lectures are very boring, tests aren't easy, and short essay questions are graded harshly for an intro level course.

The material is really easy to learn, but she will make the class appear more difficult than it actually is by having exams with poorly worded questions that will stretch your reading comprehension more than they will stretch your understanding of the material.  The class averages on the exam can't possibly reflect the understanding of the material

Everything on exams was straight from lectures. You can tell she cares about students & was nice to accommodate me when I was sick. Not the best class, but it's okay. I even took 210 with her which was more difficult but she breaks stuff down. The exams were harder than the homework which sucked, but I did notice she made a point to learn our names

I really liked her. Her lectures were very straightforward and she even tells you what concepts to study before the exam. I found the exams to be pretty easy. She also does review sessions before the exams which help alot and she records all of her lectures.

analysis.name: Ron Wakai

The class was pretty interesting. Got to learn how all the imaging equipment in the hospital works, so this class is great for pre-meds. Otherwise, the lectures were kind of boring and not that engaging.

analysis.name: Abhishek Deshpande

He is nice but this class matters so I wouldn't recommend him

He does not understand that this isn't a proof-based course. Just wasted time and was not clear what the exams were going to be like. Avoid him.

Abhishek "is this clear" Deshpande. If you take this guy for a math class, you'll hear this phrase around 25 times a lecture. Even this man's handwriting has an accent. You're better off watching a 10 minute youtube video than you are by attending a lecture.

Professor Ragsdale really cares about his students. His lecture slides were very clear on what we had to know and provided a lot of practice problems. He is a little bit of a nervous lecturer but has all good intentions. The readings for class were helpful but definitely not mandatory.

I have nothing but good things to say about Professor Ragsdale. He truly cares about the success of his students and shows this by providing clear grading criteria and easily accessible (relevant!) practice quizzes.

Prof. Rock-Singer was a really good professor and a great person to work with in general. She always brings a bright bubbly energy to class and it never fails to make my day! Lectures are a little fast-paced sometimes but other than that no complaints! TA's are very knowledgable also :)

Ron was an amazing professor, and you could tell he was super passionate about poultry. I would recommend taking as many classes with him as possible because you literally can't fail. Yay for Prof Ahlquist!! Challenging material, but if you work for it, you should know the material by the end of semester. Also, prof Ahlquist is always willing to help you understand more.

Mandatory attendance even tho she just reads off the powerpoint. The other posters are correct... she has a tendency to ramble about her life. Class isn't crazy difficult, but lecture was boring and long. 6 or 7 quizzes, and u drop the lowest score. Doesn't put in grades???? U don't know until after the final exam how u r doing in the class.

(I took PS 120 but it's not an option)
So incredibly disorganized, she constantly changed due dates and assignments
The readings were interesting but you didn't have to do them. Idk if I learned anything this whole sem
Midterm and final was writing essays but we get a notecard for final, grading isn't hard but frequent quizzes and assignments

analysis.name: Ahmad  Saatchi

review_highlights.comment: If I could give him zeros I would. Everything said in previous reviews of him are all accurate. I go to lecture everyday and I could get a D.

Plus the book is useless and nearly impossible to understand. He never makes clear his expectations for HW. My only advice is do the online HW cause quizzes are based on that.

He wants us to learn the material and he's trying but the man doesn't know his head from his feet. Too much homework. You have to read the book to learn anything and his quizzes range from obscure information you skipped over while studying to a copy of the homework.

He is an awful professor. He has no idea how to teach or even what to teach. He simply reads off of the provided powerpoints and he is impossible to understand. Whatever he says the TA's say the opposite. His tests are impossible and there is tons of homework.

Saatchi may as well be a text-to-speech robot. He stands at the front of the lecture hall mumbling through powerpoint slides.  He is also not helpful when you ask questions, and often can't understand what you are asking. The TA's are just as clueless as the students as to what we should be studying or learning because of his lack of communication.

analysis.name: Albert Ai
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: actually garbage, avoid at all costs. the problem is the class is relatively easy but its explained so poorly its impossible to know what's going on. Literally lecture is watching professor ai fill 2 entire pages with greek symbols and random syntax to "explain" something like flipping a coin. The worst professor Ive ever had.

Honestly, one of the better professors for math 431. The material is relatively easy, but Albert tries to explain the deeper reasonings for each problem to prepare for later problems in the book. Realistically, any professor would be the same in the course since they all teach directly from the UW-licensed book in order.

Not responsive to questions on online forum. Doesn't present challenging topics clearly in class. Doesn't have a strong handle on the material he's teaching. Homework is not representative of what's covered on exams. Don't take the course with him, seriously.

Professor Ai is always patient and caring. He writes math proofs on board carefully and rigorously. He often provides the motivation for the mathematical concepts and has a good organization of course content.
The exam is very difficult, Fast progress. Suitable for students who like to challenge themselves

analysis.name: Aida Hussen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: reads straight from lecture notes which use overly complex language to explain simple themes throughout the books. lecture is only mandatory to take pop quizzes and is almost useless for the midterm. Grading is strictly based on TAs and some are much easier than others. Class isnt that hard if you have a good TA but a struggle if you have a bad one

Although she is not good at giving lectures, she is very intelligent and the course material is interesting.  A lot of reading but otherwise manageable work load.

Aida is one of the best professors I've had. The course material was challenging, but Aida provided a learning environment where students' ideas were never shot down. Her intelligence is remarkable and her passion for the subject made learning enjoyable. Class is mostly focused on discussion, so be prepared to analyze theories presented in the text

Aida is AMAZING! Best professor I have ever had at UW-Madison. She is brilliant, creative, articulate, and generally lovely. 574 covered super interesting topics related to feminist literature, which is obviously one of her passions and something she is extremely knowledgeable about. I could listen to her lecture all day. Class with her was a joy!

analysis.name: Sana Aiyar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Course name in class search is very misleading, but it still turned out to be an interesting class. There are three papers, a book report, and a presentation, besides that, there's no homework. There's a lot of reading, but you can definitely get by with skimming. Know the concepts, take good notes. Professor is very nice and approachable.

The class was interesting and so were most of the readings.  Her quizzes are horrible, which I think she realizes and may change for future classes.  I missed class a couple times and failed the quizzes, but I still got an AB.

She's a pretty cool professor harsh grader on papers so make sure no grammatical errors and you put in your own ideas/thoughts about a topic. A lot of reading at the beginning of the semester. Take home exams are super nice
Great professor with high standards and interesting lectures. Has a really good BS filter for papers, so you actually have to make them good.

analysis.name: AJ Boydston
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Boydston is an really good professor that makes a tough class like Ochem 1 much easier to learn. The class is graded mainly on 3 take home quizzes and 4 exams. The lectures are easy to follow and even if not, Boydston is very approachable during his office hours. The exams are hard but as long as you put in the effort then you will do well!

He truly wants his students to learn the material. He understood that online learning is difficult and adapted his syllabus to reflect. There are three exams worth 15% and a final worth 20%. The exams are take-home (but very in-depth questions), but he allows you to retake one of the three to replace your worst one. A very smart and forgiving guy.

The best professor I've had at UW so far. He is so kind and overall an amazing guy! His office hours were super helpful. However, taking his class and then going into the "quad" of professors for 345 (since he doesn't teach 345) was a big adjustment, so be aware of that, but regardless I think it is worth it to have him teach 343

Proof Boydston is amazing. He is great at explaining concepts. His tests are more conceptual which I appreciate. He once got everyone donuts to celebrate cyclohexanes and our test scores. He also hosts office hours sometimes before exams over the weekends which were super helpful! I cannot recommend this professor enough truly the best!!

Possibly the best professor I have had. Professor Boydston had lots of availability through his office hours and would also answer piazza quite frequently. I especially liked how he made extra office hours closer to the exams to help better prepare. He made me like organic chemistry which is something I never thought I would say.

analysis.name: Simeon Alder
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Alder is a really nice guy and is very passionate about what he teaches. Maybe its the difficulty of the class but 312 was one of the hardest classes I have taken. I honestly think more math should be required to take this course and there were a lot of derivations. The homework is very hard and didnt always seem applicable to the exams.

Poor time management, unorganized notes, The worst part is the homework/exam structure: only 24 questions but many of them are 'chain-linked.' If you make one tiny error at the start, it ruins the next 3 to 4 questions. There is absolutely no margin for error. You'll end up teaching yourself everything from the textbook.

By far the hardest class/prof I've taken at UW, and it won't get worse than this. Very difficult homework, takes attendance at lecture and discussion, exam time management is BRUTAL (exam median is F). Don't take this class if you have a busy course schedule. He's a nice guy but brutal class

Prof. Alder is a great guy. His office hour and tutor are helpful but his lecture is not really well organized. Taking office hours more and discussing with him are helpful with your learning. His exams are more difficult than other professors'. Students need spend more time after class and study by themselves. Choose carefully!

Simeon is incredibly smart and a great lecturer, finding ways to integrate daily examples into his lectures. One of the most common things I've heard about him is that his train of thought is incredibly fast and hard to keep up with. He has a pretty flexible grading policy.

analysis.name: Alexander Meehan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Philos of Quantum Mechanics - Was a very interesting topic and he presented it well. Philosophy of Quantum mechanics course. Was a great guy and great at teaching. Rubrics were not specific, but if you put in effort you will get a good grade. Dr. Meehan is very available and will set up meetings outside of class if asked and responds to emails very quickly. Would recommend him, but be ready to put in real effort.

Meehan's course is the perfect choice **for those interested in philosophy**. The selected readings are inspiring and worth reading. The grading though is weird. TA told me she has to grade more than 60 people's essay. And every time TA would duct your points for reasons she made up, and arguing with her could get the points back but painful.

I DON'T recommend this course to anyone who has never learned philosophy because I wish I had known some knowledge on philosophy before taking this course. TA (Not Alex) was very transparent however tough grader. This course is a lot of thinking and rereading of the readings and lectures. It's very reading-heavy and writing-heavy.
Lovely chap and very interesting class. Strongly recommend.

analysis.name: Albrecht Karle

not a very good lecturer. Lectures are incoherent and all over the place. Does good demos which does help with learning some concepts but the demos are rushed and not explained well. If you want to actually learn the content of the class, you definitely need to seek outside sources for help.

I see what other people say with him not being the best lecturer, but he obviously cares about his students. He isn't the most tech savvy but I appreciate his kindness. He mumbles a lot. Lectures are completely useless and the only reason to come is to get the 2% of extra credit given for answering the clicker questions. Get ready to read every single chapter of your textbook. Discussions are everything in this physics department, so don't take them for granted.

analysis.name: Moses Altsech

Group project at end of semester.

overrated imo. like the other review said, he thinks way too highly of himself. he has this wack attendance policy where you can't even use the bathroom (yes i'm serious). lectures were engaging but not worth the stress. take a class with Milt Hwang if you want someone engaging

does not care about students and stresses them out. And oh also falsely accuses you of cheating DO NOT TAKE HIM.

The professor's teaching level is not bad, but he seems to dislike class very much. He did not come to class for three times, because the teaching assistant taught the class for him. On this point, I think he lacks respect for this class.

Really enjoyed the way that Professor Mikkelson taught this course. I ended with a very high AB and was very close to the grade cut off, but the class wasn't curved at all. This is no fault of Mikkelson's- the course is taught by 3 professors but rather something to be aware of. Overall, Mikkelson was one the best (and funniest) professors I've had

analysis.name: Paul Apisa
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Already graduated UW-Madison in Math and Data Science. This is the hardest thing I have ever done in my entire life. Nothing compares in difficulty. You are in for a ride.

The difficulty of his courses are extreme but he's a pretty good lecturer, has good lecture notes and gives a nice curve. His homework and exams are some of the most difficult out there but you can tell he actually puts time and effort into teaching, knows the material, comes prepared, and covers more topics than a normal class.

This class was so unbelievably difficult, averages for exams were 20-30%. He's a nice guy and cares a lot about the students but moves too quickly into harder concepts before we get to understand the basics. Nice curve but I'm not sure if I learned much, it was a bit of a fever dream. Homework was long, maybe 10-15 questions per week and hard!

Lectures are smooth and uniquely inspirational. Paul is passionate about the course content and genuinely cares about whether his students learn the math. If you want to learn a lot, take this class. I think we covered half of Linear Algebra 2 in 341. He's really accessible during office hours and clearly dedicated to his teaching.

analysis.name: Aparna Dharwadker
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Dharwadker's lectures are very dull, and while she clearly cares about the subjects, she is not very responsive to opinions that differ from her own. I did not feel like I was in an environment where I could contribute my thoughts, yet she seems annoyed when people don't participate. The reading selection was good though and exams were easy.

I feel like the people who rated her low didn't actually engage with her lessons. I was not confident about my writing assignments and still got As on them! I love that all the writing assignments are in class, it is way less stressful. She is very smart and had really interesting insight into the topics. I also loved the selection of literature.

Prof Dharwadker is clearly very passionate about what she teaches, to the point she will dismiss or scoff at literary interpretations that differ from her own; this discourages anyone from speaking in class, and then she will scold her students for not discussing. I witnessed her laugh at a student's genuine interpretation of a poem during class.

Thankfully, this professor knows that this class is primarily taken by people who don't care. Even still, she is not great at encouraging participation as she primarily wants to teach her interpretation of the text. Your full semester grade is based on four in-class writings plus attendance which is very stressful.
She is flexible and kind as long as you participate in class. Her lectures are a bit long and can be boring, but she is passionate about her work and knowledgeable.

analysis.name: April Haynes

The material is really interesting- you'll learn a lot!

This class made me decide to become a gen&ws major! Her lectures are awesome and her PowerPoints make things super clear. It is not an easy class, but having a teacher that so so knowledgeable and passionate about the subject ensured that I always showed up and put in the work.

April was extremely passionate and knowledgeable amount women throughout history. This was an empowering class, and although April has a very calm demeanor, she definitely had fire in her lecture meanings. Read the prompts carefully and prepare well for the in class essays. Meeting with TA's also helped a lot- made getting a good grade very doable!

Apri is a passionate professor and I loved having class with her. You have to truly love the topic of gender and history to gain something from the class, however. This was a 201 course so a big chunk of the grade and time spent for this class was focused on the final essay. This is not an easy A class and the essay is grueling but the class is incredibly interesting and professor Haynes clearly has a deep love for and knowledge of women's history. Her passion showed in lectures and I personally loved it.

analysis.name: Antonio Hernandez

He is the only option when it comes to choosing an instructor for this statics class. He gives weekly quizzes which are worded terribly. Hernandez teaching statics is like an annoying boss battle you have to beat to before accessing the rest of the college of engineering.

Amazing professor, she is super nice. She made sure classes weren't too difficult and earning an A was very attainable. Easily one of my favorite professors and I am taking another class with her this semester.
Genuinely my favorite professor at this school. She is wonderful, will help with anything you need. Amanda is very forgiving and accommodating.

Great professor. Very good at explaining proofs.
Dr. Cochran has that rarest of all teaching qualities: She actually cares about students learning.

I never read the textbook and was fine.

Dr. White is very kind and very intelligent, but there really isn't anything to glean from her lectures. She won't record class if you're ill or offer virtual options, even though her class is on accessibility for those with disabilities. The CBL component is poorly integrated with the course as a whole, but it is the only redeeming factor here.

She is super nice and the class was actually so easy. She cancel class a lot. Best part of class is when people come to speak. Lectures are super short. She means well but seems to not really know what she's doing. Basically always graded on completion I ended with a 100%. If you're an education major def take this class its a breeze.

Might just be me, but I felt she was sometimes disinterested in being there, a little disorganized, and was gone way too much. Don't miss a lecture - she doesn't take attendance but it's hard to keep up if you aren't in class - you won't do well on the quizzes without the little nuggets of info you get from lecture.

analysis.name: Randolph Ashton
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Long readings are assigned with reading quizzes before each lecture and the readings are pretty dense. Three exams make up most of your grade. Dr. Ashton is a nice person and very passionate about his research in biomaterials, but he goes through lecture slides quickly considering how much information they contain and lectures can be a bit dry.

He puts whole essay's worth of information on every slide. Not easy to keep up since the exams will cover everything in the slides. I took this class early on in my undergrad so my study strategies had room for improvement. I recommend taking this class later if you can, even if you are on the biomaterials track.

Hands down worst BME class I have taken. The first day he tells you the only way to succeed in the class is to memorize the slides. Then, he proceeds to give you a 50 page reading assignment every lecture. I spent days studying for the exams (which make up the entire grade btw) just to get average. Lectures are boring, he just reads off the slides.

If you are interested in biomaterials and tissue engineering, you wont be after this class. Dr. Ashton doesnt explain any background information and spends the entire hour and fifteen minutes talking at you about concepts you dont understand and refuses to clarify them. The reading makes no sense and he tests you on it after admitting its hard.

analysis.name: Athan Biss
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

Lots of reading assigned but it's usually just background for the information in lecture. Read the textbook if you need more info but I really enjoyed his class!

Need to attend lecture to pass. A lot of outside reading and homework assignments that are grades pretty toughly. Essays are graded extremely hard, so the finals and midterms are easy except for the essay portion which get graded tough. He makes you read A LOT. The exams are all short answer and essay, but he tells you the possible topics ahead of time. Also on the final we were allowed to have a "notecard" which was actually a full sheet of paper. I don't like history and I thought this was an easy class

analysis.name: Sarah Atis

i had her as a guest lecturer, and i had a very hard time following her train of thought, her notes.. i had no clue what i was supposed to get out of the lecture. so if you have her as a guest lecturer, consider skipping the class if possible. i must say, though, that she seems like a very sweet lady who probably does better in smaller settings.

I have taken 2 classes with prof Atis and she is probably my favorite professor. She's very clear about what's going to be on the test, her lectures aren't super structured but I enjoyed class and what she had to say.

Nobody pays attention, all you have to do is read all the stories and readings for a few days before the final, memorize those pretty well, and you will get an A on the 20% final. Papers are graded fairly easy, 20% of grade is a comparative paper, 40% is research paper, 10% is oral presentation of said research paper, 10% is attendance

I signed up for Turkish folk lit. not really knowing anything about it and I ended up loving the class! A little hard to hear at times, but just sit up front or better yet stop by office hours. She'll be more than happy to work with you, she's extremely nice helpful and encouraging. Really cares about students.

analysis.name: Atefeh Oliai

One of the Best teachers Ive had in every aspect.  Teaches well, and even caters to your learning style.  Gets everyone to bring delicious food.  No one really falls asleep during class because she keeps it exciting.  However we call her crazy atefeh because, well shes just plain crazy.

The best class I'm taking this semester is her class. I can not miss any. She is the best ever. I like her style. and all of what she says is great. I hope she can be my prof. for all of the subjects, so  I will be able to learn everything.
it was an awful painful experience, will never take Persian in my life ..... hate the Prof and the course

Audrey will push you has an actor and will always raise the bar. 250 is a big step up from 150. She did not make herself very available outside of class time, if so it was very rushed. Feedback got repetitive into the course, not much personal student-to-professor investment. But super fun course with so many talented actors.

I am a Standish fan. She is so kind and cares so much about her students. I had her also for 150 and she just inspires the room. I think she's the best professor at UW Madison in theatre. I took 250 in the fall of 2024 and she would buy the class coffee, get to know us, and really inspire us to go further. I grew tremendously as an actor.

Audrey is by far one of the most caring and loved professors we have at the UW Theatre Department. I have also taken 360 with her and have never had a more organized and thoughtful director in my entire acting career. If you have the opportunity to take a class with Audrey, DO IT! You will be a better theatre artist after just one class.

I have had Audrey for three classes and I would take classes with her 7000x over. She is an extremely dedicated, organized, caring, and fun professor. You can get so much out of her classes if you do the assigned work, pay attention, and participate. The participation is not at all painful, and she sincerely cares about your growth. I

analysis.name: Anthony  Auger
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His test questions are easy to understand and his exams are fairly easy. He is a good lecturer and helps break down the complex aspects of hormones and the brain. He is also really sweet and is pretty engaging.

I took Tony's capstone course on epigenetics. It was difficult since I had no genetics background, but he made the material easy to understand. Assignments seemed difficult but he is very helpful and wants everyone to succeed. He's an all-around great guy and great professor. I learned a lot in his class!

I absolutely loved this class. Multiple topics were brought up that were never even mentioned in other classes I have taken at UW, and there definitely was evidence used to support his claims as this is what we were tested on! Professor Auger was extremely kind and understanding towards his students and I would take his class again in a heartbeat.

He sometimes flies through dense/difficult course content, but would often end lectures 10-20 minutes early so it wasn't too overwhelming. His tests are very fair, and he is definitely very caring. I would not recommend taking this course if you are not a neurobiology major. The class is far more biological than any psychology class I've taken.

Loved this course! Anthony can move a little fast during his lectures so you make sure you're taking notes. Three big exams are each 25% of your grade. Exams were a lot easier than I expected since the course materials were pretty heavy. Overall, lots of memorization but interesting topics. WATCH THE REVIEW VIDEOS FOR EXAMS! SO HELPFUL!

analysis.name: Audra Sterling
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: The best professor at UW-Madison. She's extremely knowledgeable about the field and is willing to guide students not only through her class, but also grad school applications, interviews, and more. She's also incredibly kind, caring, and accepting. I also took CSD 481 and it was lovely. 100% would take her classes again.

Audra has been one of my favorite professors in the CS&D department! She is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the material that she's teaching. She is very clear about what she expects you to know for the exam. She always has her student's best interest and is more than willing to help/meet with you to help you succeed!

Audra is AMAZING! You can tell how passionate she is about her research, and all of the topics she talks about in her classes. She is so personable and you can talk to her about anything. Oh, and this class is easy as pie! Her lectures are really interesting, so even if you hate lectures she's really good at grabbing your attention!

Popping in here to give a recent review of Audra! She is the BEST and widely respected among her faculty and students for a reason. Super straightforward lectures and exams are exactly what she says it will be. One of the sweetest people and very aware of her subject area. Clever and kind

She is so sweet and loves talking about her research in this class! She is very approachable for all things CSDgrad school. This was a super easy class and I really enjoyed getting to know Audra! Recommend going to class for pop up assignments, but all the info is on the slides.

analysis.name: Aurelie Rakotondrafara
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lecture and lab attendance are mandatory. In person and online lectures with a quiz each week. Lectures aren't bad, just redundant and not helpful. 3 in person exams and all lab assignments make up your grade. Opportunity for extra credit, but more work than it is worth. Expect to get no direction in lab and to be left without much instruction.

Her lectures were mainly just review from video lectures but were mandatory for participation points. A general knowledge of plants is probably best but it's not too hard to pick up. Three midterms but no final.

Interesting course, not recommended if you already have a heavy course load. Far more work than a typical 3 credit 100 level course. Expect 2-5 online lectures per week paired with a weekly quiz, HW, discussion, lab and reports. The material isn't difficult, there's just a lot of it and often feels disorganized. Professor is passionate & talks FAST

Dr. Rakotondrafara's class was fun and informative. Most lecture material was review of high school biology and environmental science, yet I appreciated learning about plant pathology, agricultural disease management, and how to be a conscientious consumer. I enjoyed the labs; most were self-directed with a small lab group, and the TA helped too.

The content itself is not that hard, and if you want an easy biology class I'd say take it. But the professor doesn't seem like she knows too much about what she's teaching. It's a hybrid class so a lot of the lectures are online. Many of the concepts are poorly explained and you can tell she's reading off of a poor script. Easy grade, bad class.

analysis.name: Aurora Santiago Ortiz
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is a very educated woman, but her lectures are terrible. she has over 25-30 slides each day, and the slides are packed with information. Although she is extremely passionate about lecture content, her lecture slides are horrifically long. One of her presentations was 46 slides long, loaded with content. She will often remark "i'm going to speed through", which isn't how lectures should be. She overwhelms students with content and simply copies paragraphs of text into the lecture

Professor Santiago Ortiz is knowledgable and passionate. However, the course is poorly organized, we often don't have clear instructions on assignments and the canvas page also lacks specific guidelines. She assigns very difficult and advanced readings and does not really break them down in lecture.

I went into this class with high hopes but was severely disappointed. The entire course consists of pretty much only dense, difficult, and jargony readings and pointless lectures. All she does is pluck quotes from the readings, stretch it out for fifty+ slides, and provide pretty much no additional content or her thoughts about the subject.

The class was very interesting but was too difficult to be considered an intro-level course. Professor is knowledgeable and cares about what she teaches, but readings are usually long and difficult. It doesn't help that instead of breaking down the readings she just copies and pastes quotes from the readings onto 50+ slide powerpoints.

analysis.name: Awad Hanna
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

Professor Hanna is an unavoidable part of the Civil Engineering department, which is unfortunate. analysis.name: Aws Albarghouthi

Excellent professor with engaging lectures. Cannot recommend him higher. Reasonable workloads, values quality of work over quantity, very available for questions and concerns, course was strong in theory but his lectures were in plain English and he did a great job of making it easy to grok the abstract.

He is passionate about both the subject and teaching and it shows. While I recommend going to lecture, he publishes full notes online and they are amazing. The projects are a bit repetitive but make sure that you understand the material. Overall a really solid professor.
Good at breaking down concepts in an understandable way, always willing to go back and answer questions to make sure everyone understands the material, holds useful review sessions before tests.

Aws was fantastic! His lectures were really clear and helpful. The course had a lot of material online that supplemented what we covered and was great review. I visited office hours once with him and he wasn't super helpful, but the TA's were fantastic. He was also willing to adjust my grade at the end of the semester. Would definitely recommend!

It is hard to understand the class content because there is often no logic. This course has in-class quizzes this semester and has midterm and final exams.

Never been more frustrated with a professor in my 4 years at UW. Extremely disorganized lectures, countless mistakes, and jumping around. I was surprised abt Joe's rating. I thought he was entertaining and prepared students well. The content isn't super interesting, but Joe tried his best to make it more interesting. PSYCH414-Class was unorganized and uninteresting, expectations were unclear. Exams were unfair and Joe was unwilling to hear out students, he was quickly defensive and never held himself accountable. DO NOT TAKE any class offered by Joe, you will not be the one student who enjoys him or the way he teaches.

analysis.name: Axel Presas

Axel is a huge linguist, which makes his class pretty awful because he spends a ton of time talking about what can used here or there, and as a result we do almost no speaking in class.
