Axel is a great guy. He's funny and makes the class really interesting. As long as you do what is expected of you, there is no reason for you not to get at least a B in his class. Excellent professor and I definitely would recommend to take a class from him if you get the chance!

Funny and entertaining professor! Will work with you one-on-one for papers, which I highly recommend. He enjoys students who are outgoing and put themselves out there. However, don't ask a stupid question or he will call you out in front of the class.

analysis.name: Axing Zhu

A-xing is friendly, yet is truly a terrible teacher. His accent makes him difficult to understand and he has a very rambling way of lecturing, so it's very difficult to follow. analysis.name: Richard Aviles

You can tell he knows the material but he just flat out can not teach it. Therefore, going to discussion and having a good TA is very important. He stutters a lot during lecture and often times talks very fast but essentially reads off the slides.

AVOID HIM!! He mumbles horribly, You can't understand him at all, and he is VERY unhelpful. The tests took 3 weeks to get a grade back. I went into this class thinking it would be one of my favorites but it was absolutely terrible.

analysis.name: María De Avila

review_highlights.comment: This semester was horrific.  I'm fairly positive this was her first time teaching 311 and it showed. We're taking a petition to the Spanish department head about Maria.

Horrible, horrible, horrible TA/prof. Full of herself, made students feel stupid, regardless of whether they were also native speakers or not. If it wasn't Mexican Spanish, it was wrong. Doesn't give clear instructions for hardly anything. Expects you to read her mind. Grades unfairly and expects you to be visiting her during office hours constantly. Gives excessive homework. Nevertheless, I feel like I did learn alot altho she is a terrible grader and even though I'm doing everything I can I probably won't get the A I deserve.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. she does little to nothing to help you do well in the class. even if you ask for help, she will not correct anything on your papers and will wait for u to turn it in so she can give u a C. I've gotten A's in every spanish class I've ever taken. Avoid her at all costs.

Horrible professor with ridiculous grading scale. She had ridiculous expectations that she never clearly states, but rather expects from students. She's helpful if you go to office hours but you have to put in a lot more effort than the class is worth. Avoid her if you can!

analysis.name: Richard Avramenko

review_highlights.comment: Nice guy, but unnecessary amount of reading and he pulls small vocab out of the text to test you on the final exam. TA completely determines your grade as he grades your paper, and all of your tests. When i had it one TA was noticeable easier so it kind of depends who you have as a TA. DO NOT TAKE UNLESS YOU ENJOY READING BOOKS FROM THE 13t century

There is a lot of classical reading involved with ILS 205! If you don't feel comfortable reading Plato, Homer, etc, then this class is not for you. Prof. Avramenko can seem a bit pretentious at times but is overall an excellent lecturer. His lecture outlines are not posted online, so take good notes in class. The exams and 1 paper are fairly easy.

I took ILS 205 Fall 23 and would highly recommend it. He's a fantastic lecturer- I always felt like I really understood the dense readings after lectures. I had Avramenko himself for discussion and liked it- he really pushed students to think more about the texts and truly listened to everyone's personal thoughts and philosophical ideas.

Don't take class if you want easy humanities credit. Grade is entirely dependent on TA and A's are hard to come by. I didn't read a single of the 7 assigned readings, all I did was show up to every lecture and take notes. He doesn't post anything so lectures are crucial. Finished with an AB.

the greatest and most attractive professor probably ever in the history of UW. very interesting lectures, but doesn't post them on the internet so you have to go to class... it's worth it, though - ahh just love him

analysis.name: Kendall Aycock

Goated professor for Spanish 203!! 10/10

Kendall is an awesome professor. She cares a lot about her students and wants them to succeed. She is passionate about Spanish and wants to help you. Also, she is pretty cool. Definitely take a class with her if you can .

analysis.name: Mouna Ayari
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Kacem is very nice, approachable and willing to help you if you ask questions. The logic of the class is clear and she talks about some of the complicated algorithms used in each program before the due date. Overall you can understand her lecture and get the help you need.

She is very accessible outside of class. Many students find that she is very caring and understanding. Sometimes her lectures are slow, but they will prepare you very well for exams. Go in for office hours whenever. I've never had a better professor. She always makes sure that everything she says is clear for everyone.

She cares about her students; she is easily accessible after class and at office hours. After class, she stays and is more than willing to look at homework issues, answer questions about lecture, or answer any other questions you have. The exams are relatively similar to the lecture material, and she posts notes from lectures to review.

Professor Mouna is an extremely kind and dedicated instructor. She is easily accessible outside of class and provided clear and useful information. Her lectures also typically include information directly pertaining to the assignments.
She means well, but she isn't the greatest at teaching the course material. Tests and exams cover content that was brushed over in lecture, and is pretty difficult.

analysis.name: Aydin Bal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Favorite class of the semester. It's one three hour lecture per week, with a 25 hour service learning requirement. Lectures have plenty of breaks, and are usually accompanied by a  guest speakervideo clips. Assignments are clear-cut and easy to do well on. He's compassionate and helpful, and values discussionengagement in the class.

Lectures were interesting, didn't cover the textbook during them. You're expected to read it on your own. I enjoyed the volunteer work, there are great opportunities. You had to read a chapter, watch 2 videos, and submit a reflection answering 1 question of your choice about the chapter each week. 3 exams not cumulative & get test questions before.

This is a 3hr lecture, but he fills the time well. He gives lots of breaks that usually go longer than he says they will. Everything is given to you before hand, so it's pretty hard not to do well. There are lots of in class activities, & attendance is taken 2x a class that count for a chunk of your grade, but do the weekly questions & you're good!

Overall Professor Bal is amazing!! Although the lectures are pretty long, he gives plenty of breaks and keeps the class interesting through guest lecturers, Ted Talks and other videos. The tests are very straight forward and he gives you all of the questions beforehand. He makes sure everything is well explained. Loved the service learning project!

Professor Bal is a really nice guy. The three hour class was a bit frustrating though. Having to sit there and listen to a dry lecture without taking notes or having any other stimulation was incredibly tiresome. It made the lecture feel like it lasted three days instead of three hours. Service learning is amazing and easy to get an A. Ok course.

analysis.name: Tim  Aylsworth
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Although it was only my first year at this esteemed University, I can already say that Tim will be one of my favorite professors. I entered the class assuming I would despise every moment of it, but that was not the case. Tim made it enjoyable and a pleasure. Although lectures can get long, he is always well prepared. Take Philosophy with Tim!

Tim Aylsworth is one of the all time greats, his lectures are funny and engaging, and he displays a passion for the material that rubs off on the class. His main concern is not giving hard exams or trying to create a grade distribution, but making sure that students learn and grow by taking his course. 101 with Aylsworth is a legendary course.

He gets so into lectures and you can just tell he loves Philosophy. This makes a class that could have easily been one of my worst for the semester, my favorite. 3 short papers for completion and 2 easy midterms (if you attend lecture) and a 3pg paper at the end. No need to read, he goes through everything in class better anyways. Nice guy!

Tim is not even 30 yet and entirely understands what it's like to be a college student. Half the time I wouldn't read the assignments which he would post online (no textbook) and I would still easily be able to participate in class. He makes a sincere effort to learn the names of his students which is nice in a decently large lecture.

Truly one of the best instructors I've ever had. A pretty easy A. Readings were pdfs of articles and excerpts, they were unnecessary though as he makes sure to cover them in lecture.  His own passion for the subject was imbued in everyone, kids who normally would be apathetic to philosophy found themselves engaged in his discussions. Great teacher.

analysis.name: Aziza Jones
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Jones was awesome, I wish she taught more courses. Her exams are very fair, open note and she makes it clear that she's 'not trying to trick you.' her attendance policy is also very fair and she's accessible. she brings in a real client and you're able to list it as an internship. hands down best marketing course at UW;everyone should take it

The class was very inapplicable to the real world, and I learned very little about marketing. I did not enjoy the class, and the entire grade was weighted on one group project that she gives no feedback on throughout the semester. She will meet with you and say that you are on the right track and then blindside you with a below average grade.

I really enjoyed having Prof. Jones. She brings in real clients for a real campaign, and you can list this as an internship on your resume. She was great with feedback and grading and she was accessible. She overall was just very nice and extremely knowledgable. I would definitely take with her again.
Gives no constructive feedback and blind sides with a bad grade for a project worth 55% of your grade

Aziza is an awesome professor! She is very passionate about her students. The class is super easy, with 2 open note exams, participation, and a group project that is a campaign. It got a little boring sometimes, but was overall a super fun and easy class!

analysis.name: Alejandro Azocar
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Easily one of the best instructors in the ESL department! Just concentrate and give him all your attention, and you'll easily pass. I visited his office multiple times during office hours, and he was very understanding and supportive.

Even though he did not provide clear grading criteria, he was helpful and fair overall. Visit his office to get extra advice for your paper before you turn it in. It would help you a lot. I got A in this class but it was not easy. You should put effort and time outside class to get a good grade. I would like to recommend him! :)

Professor Azocar is one of the best professors! 118 class is time consuming, no matter who you take it with. But if you are lucky enough, you will get to this professor. He is very kind. Always ready to help. I am so happy I took this class with him! I highly recommend him!

Professor Azocar is really a very nice teacher. I. took his ESL116 and ESL118 during the freshman year. He really give great feedbacks of my essays, and as long as you could talk to him and understand his points, you could get good grades.
The best professor to have for ESL 118, especially since he's so flexible with deadlines. He clearly cares for his students and is always willing to help improve your grade, 10/10 would recommend

analysis.name: Azadeh Davoodi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The course itself is interesting and easy to follow but the exams can be a tad bit challenging. The midterm was lengthy with tricky questions while the final was pretty straightforward. Just attend her review session before the final and you should be good. She is a lenient grader and really wants her students to learn. Lectures can be dry though.

She cares for her students but this was her first time taking the course and unfortunately, it showed. The material is not too difficult and the workload is manageable but the lectures are heavy. She updates the same set of slides before every class which causes a lot of confusion. The tests are incredibly long and slightly on the difficult side.

I can definitely she knows the material inside and out, and shes is never afraid of giving you an answer. This doesn't mean her answers are very clear, however. She made the midterms fairly easyusual for a class that dumps a full data path custom layout, so hopefully you have at least one good partner. Accent isn't bad, but she rambles often.

She knows the material very well and explains it thoroughly. Her quizzes and exams are extremely fair and grading is to the benefit of the student. An effort is a must to do well on the project. Overall, a great professor.

Contrary to previous reviews, I found the lectures very useful. Davoodi is obviously enthusiastic about the material and knows it well. Extremely helpful and always available. Love the open door policy! Highly recommended.

analysis.name: Maria Azocar
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Maria is one of the nicest teachers I have had. She cares very deeply about her students and is super flexible in making her class the best experience that she can. Her class has been one of the most influential on the way I look at the world and society. I would highly recommend her to anyone.
Maria is very devoted to her work and very accommodating. If you show up and skim the readings you'll do fine. She is very accessible and wants her students to succeed.

Maria is very approachable and is always happy to answer your questions. Her lectures are always interesting, and she asks the class questions to keep them engaged. She tries her best to facilitate arguments, but sometimes things can get out of hand if there is a sensitive topic. If you skim the readings and can explain the terms it is an easy A.

Professor Azocar is an intelligent, respected professor and has interesting, helpful lectures. She actually let me join the class about 4 weeks into the semester and helped me to catch up on all the material I missed, so she is very understanding and caring towards students.

Maria teaches a class to a severe bias. If there is a disagreement in class, she will often let other students gang up on an individual. If you have a different viewpoint than Maria, my advice would be to never speak up. More often than not Maria avoids facts in lecture and rather points to feelings to provide evidence. Do not take this class.

analysis.name: William Aylward
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 176 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: King of Dad Jokes. Classics 370 is basically just story time, it's great. I also took him for ILS 204. Don't take ILS 204 with him. He's way too passionate about the subject to teach a survey course. He gets too bogged down in anecdotes. Classics 370 was a blast though. He's a good story teller and tests were easy. Socially awkward but a nice guy

Professor Alyward is super passionate about what he teaches and you can tell he cares about the material. That being said, lectures are very boring and you could probably get by with reading the spark notes and looking up flashcard sets on quizlet. He gives out study guides which are really helpful and overall I would recommend the class!

Aylward is awesome! I took 304 to fulfill a lit requirement and now I'm considering a certificate in classics because of Aylward. He doesn't post his slides, so you kind of have to go to lecture, but he's so engaging and funny I didn't even mind. I was in the honors discussion section with him and he always had interesting stories and fun facts.

I loved this class, not going into the field or anything just took it for credits but I'm glad I did. I love when a professor actually shows the passion they have for topics and that is exactly him. I genuinely learned a lot and I could put this class on the back burner when I got busy. Highly Recommend.

Really great professor. Makes a lot of dad jokes during lecture. Grading on exams really straight forward, which makes studying easy. He does ramble on occasionally and can forget what he's saying from time to time, but it's not that bad.

analysis.name: David Baum
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 85 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Baum is one of the three professors for Bio 152, and he makes the content very engaging and easy to learn. Participations during lectures are required and you will need to get them right. The labs for this class are not as hard, but instead you will have to do a semester long research project that will be presented at a symposium so be ready!

Had him twice for BIO152 & ZOO410--Dr. Baum is maybe my favorite professor from UW. He genuinely cares about students and is very accommodating for McBurney Students! SO knowledgeable, respected, and always making sure students understand the bigger picture of their education. He is accessible and encouraging, as well!

I liked Dr. Baum as a person, he made lectures/slides funny. He was kinda hard to understand,which is not his fault at all, but he was incredibly helpful in office hours. He did a good enough job explaining the content. In my opinion, Evolution was the hardest 152 module, but that also could be because I barely paid attention in lecture.

Dr. Baum is one of the reasons I saw the true value in going to a well respected research university. He incorporates his research into the lectures - which may sound intimidating, but it actually made the lecture more interesting. He is invested in helping. His exam was very wordy and 3x as difficult as the practice test, so beware of that.

Baum taught the evolution section of Bio 152. His lectures were insightful and useful, but it is hard to understand him most of the time, in part due to his accent and slight lisp. He has real-time subtitles in his lecture that never work, but his lecture recordings have a correct transcript that highlights his effective lecturing.

analysis.name: Bart Skarzynski
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Gave good and useful feedback, and grading was clear once he had graded it. However, before having graded it we were often not given instructions on what to do or what was expected and then had to learn this class "in hindsight", which was incredibly irritating at times. Was kind and connected to us despite being online.
He grades way too harshly for an online class.
Bart is the kind of teacher that I wish I had more often. He pushes you to think critically and perform to the best of your ability. Not afraid to throw some humor into class.

Great professor. He teaches a required class that no one wants to take but somehow having him as a professor made it better. He will not give you an A for fluff, and you have to participate in his class. He isn't going to give you a good grade without putting in the work, but he teaches the way classes should be taught. Very highly recommend him.
Absurdly harsh grader and isn't an engineer so gets lost in technical details. Rude when grading as well.

analysis.name: Genevieve Bates
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lecture slides pulled almost directly from the book. For this reason, I rarely attended lecture. The book is dense, but read and you'll know everything to know for the tests (plus examples in the slides). The 2 noncumulative exams were designed to make you succeed (MC, T/F, matching) with EC. Discussion attendance is required. Would take again 100%

Professor Bates was amazing! Her exams were straightforward and as long as you knew the reading material and went to most of the lectures you were fine. In office hours she is so engaging and kind and went out of her way to help me find resources to add to my understanding. Would absolutely take again!

I took Principles of intl law w Professor Bates and I loved it. The class is relatively easy if you show up, take notes, read course materials, and study for the exams. Both the midterm and final exams require intense studying if you want a good grade. Also, she is very knowledgeable and makes the lectures engaging and informative. Would take again
She's truly awesome and you can tell she really cares about her research and teaching.

analysis.name: Baha Balantekin
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: baha is way overqualified to teach this class. it just kind of shows. but if you truly understand the material (easy) you'll be fine on exams, which are 75% of your grade. no major curveballs or anything that's impossible to figure out if you actually studied. the labs were very poorly written and designed (not baha's fault) but you can do it!
He has no patience with students. Does not want to spend any time with you to help you understand the material. Lectures are unclear. The other prof is better.

I am greatly disappointed with his special topic course. I thought such courses are for graduate students to learn something that they can use for research. His course is so low level that it does not prepare you for research. I would rather take another advanced course that other professors offer.

No help from this guy. When asked to schedule an office hours appointment, he came up with all kinds of lame excuses like he has other important meetings. I talked by his office and saw him just gossiping with his colleagues.  I was greatly disappointed.

Baha is a funny guy, but this class was absolutely impossible to follow. I've been successful at physics in the past, but I had absolutely no idea what was going on in this class. The only reason I passed was because I was able to slightly tweak the homework solutions to fit the test questions. He made me seriously consider switching my major.

analysis.name: Annie Bauer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Annie clearly has no background knowledge about what she's teaching, cannot answer in-depth questions about the content, and doesn't care about helping students or seeing them succeed. Truly astounding that she even got hired to teach at UW.

GeoScience109 was SO hard, especially for an "elementary" level course. At the beginning of the semester, I, along with other students, expressed to the professors how difficult the content was to follow and they basically ignored the situation. They adjusted what was "passing" THREE times because so many people were doing poorly in the class.

This was the hardest class I've taken in college. I thought this would be an easy and interesting 100-level course, but I read/watch everything, take notes, and for some reason started with an A but have been getting Fs or Cs on the most recent quizzes - which you have every week. This class caused so much unnecessary stress - do not take it.

Annie is nice but her class was painfully hard. I was initially excited for the course because it covered National Parks but I found myself so stressed that I never enjoyed the content. The quizzes/exams are atrocious. I always watched lecture, went to office hours, asked her for advice, etc. but still got D's every time. Tears were shed.

Dr. Baur has interesting lectures and is willing to help. She is willing to help you understand concepts in office hours which her counterpart is not. Her lectures are engaging but she talks very fast.

analysis.name: Bob Batt
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM. All his classes weren't fun to stay in, an hour was an eternity and his class weren't like the exams. His lectures were all over, didn't help with problems that were 3 mins. I never wanted to go to class but he made attendance mandatory even though he records lectures.
This was his first semester lecturing for otm300 with a complete restructuring that I was not a fan of. Did not submit final grades on time with no excuse.

It was his first semester teaching this course, so it was very disorganized. I learned nothing in lecture and found it a waste of my time. The first exam was extremely difficult, but I think he realized his mistake and made our final exactly like the homework. Overall, not a hard class- just feels like a waste of time.

He'll go to the extent to "record" the lectures to be "nice", but he'll only record his voice and not any of the calculations so that the recordings are of absolutely no use. He also makes attendance mandatory. I'm sure he's competent, but he is the opposite of a nice person.

Good guy who breaks down the service industry in a very interesting way. Although the content may be dry at times, it offers a very interesting perspective on many of the big organizations. If you read and participate, you will absolutely do well. Quizes are open note, and homework encouraged to do with your classmates. Wants students to succeed.

analysis.name: Setareh Behroozi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I had Dr. Behroozi in her first semester teaching here. While I didn't like the format of this class (lectures as homework and homework done in class) that's an ECE252 problem not Dr. Behroozi's problem. She is VERY knowledgeable about computer engineering and is great at explaining questions if you ask. She is super helpful you if you seek help!

The class is set up as a flipped format, so the professor isn't really important. But there's a optional lecture time that I really liked. Setareh runs it and she's great at breaking down what we covered the previous week. Plus, she sometimes brings candy, which is a sweet bonus.

Setareh is a good professor and knows the material. She is a good lecturer and is very helpful in class. However, she is very hard to reach outside of class and is almost not worth attempting. The bulk of her grading is not done by her and often responds to grading questions with non-answers. Overall, good professor but not always the most helpful.

I think Setareh is a nice professor who really wanted people to succeed. She is to a certain extent, strict. That being said, most of ECE was a flipped classroom, so I didn't learn a lot from Setareh herself. At the end of the day, getting help from the TAs and going to office hours is the best way to succeed in this course.

like her style of teaching, a very nice prof with the heart to help you go through all the difficult materials. DEFINITELY take her class! she is really helpful and are always willing to help you go through the assessment and homework.

analysis.name: Carl Barlett
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Carl was my favorite professor in the entire business school. He really cares about his students and puts so much effort into the course. RMI 640 is not an easy class and you almost certainly will not do well if you do not come to lecture. That being said, if you find the content enjoyable and/or are willing to work hard, you can get an A.

Professor Barlett is fantastic! I took RMI 300 as an elective course for the business certificate and absolutely loved it. His lectures are really engaging and you can tell Carl cares a lot about his students - for example, even if it's a 300 person lecture, he definitely knows your name. Class content was really interesting too!

Good lecturer and really knows what hes talking about. The book serves as a good starting point but the lecture is where the value is. The simulation is a ton of fun! You essentially run an insurance company at the end of the semester and compete against others in the class.

Cares about his students and is enthusiastic while teaching. Gives students material to think about which is applicable in the "real world".  Helps students succeed by working through difficult problems in class, encourages collaboration with other students for peer teaching. Very intelligent and makes his students feel comfortable asking questions

Love this professor and this class! He's engaging and clearly cares about his students. If you go to lecture and take notes, you'll do fine on the tests (MC + short answer). The class structure allows a lot of opportunity to do well - he weighs the midterm you do best on the heaviest and you can get an easy 5% boost from opting into discussion.

analysis.name: Nader Behdad
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bedhad's passion and enthusiasm for the course content really shows. He has a deep understanding of the concepts and is always willing to answer any extra questions. Do note that he is particular about students coming to lecture, but he is a good lecturer, and if you really listen and care about the content, you will enjoy them.

Professor Behdad was a joy to study under. While his class was difficult, his riveting lecture style and passion for electrodynamics made every lecture a joy to attend. He teaches with passion, and it is clear that he knows the subject very well. He was the highlight of my semester, and I hope to take more classes with him in the future.

Had Nader for ECE 222 last semester and I was really worried after seeing his madgrades, but He ended up being one of the best professor's I've had in EE. His class is not easy, but if you go to lectures, do homework's, and study 2-4 hours for exams you should have no problem. Attending office hours is also very helpful!

Professor is very passionate, and definitely takes pride in knowing students on an individual level. Has improved (from what I've heard of in previous years at least) in terms of being really open to student suggestions, even gave us an extra 5% in the class for getting to a 90% response rate on the course eval.

Tests were unnecessarily difficult. Almost half the class dropped after the first averages on the exams were around 40%. Most of the grade is based on test scores which are not curved. Test questions were much more difficult than assigned homework problems. There was no review and no posted review for the exams other than one past exam.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Anne Hooper-Lane
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is one of the most amazing teachers I've ever had. The lecture is so engaging, and the way she teaches it means the information sticks in a way thats usually not the case. The content is so engaging, and she is so knowledgeable. Could not recommend more.

When I had Liz for the History of Interiors Class, I was beyond inspired in the field of historic design. She is very detailed and gives great information that is incredibly interesting, and this makes tests easy to study for and pass.  I am so sad that she isn't teaching this particular class anymore, but I'm positive she would be great otherwise.
Never met professor, the TA's will rip your heart out and ruin your mental health. This was a required class and was the worst class I had ever taken. Only thing I learned was that I suck at art.
I had her at UW-Stevens Point. She is my favorite professor. Don't skip lectures or leave early she gives extra credit to the people that stay for the whole two and a half hours.

Am non-design student. Class was hybrid: online prerecorded lectures & in-person studio sessions w/ TA. Class consists of weekly quizzes on the boring lectures and 4 studio projects. Projects are extremely time consuming and require lots of digital art knowledge (which I had none of). TAs are rough graders who take off points without explaining why

analysis.name: Jeffrey Beneker
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed Classics 320 so much, I had declared a Classics certificate by the end. I took it as a Com B requirement, so it was very writing heavy, but in the most accessible way possible. The grading was very forgiving, but Professor Beneker would have made it worth it even if it wasn't. He was calm, friendly, and engaging- definitely recommend.

Beneker's lectures are necessary to do well in the course, but very informational and entertaining. The material covered is interesting as long as you have a general interest in the Greeks. There are lots of outside of class readings to support the lecture, and weekly responses that are 600 words to prove understanding. Overall great course.

Prof. Beneker is very engaging and I genuinely learned a lot. However, I found myself spending more time to stay afloat in this class than my STEM classes and at the last week we four different assignments due. Yes its comm B and grading is lenient but there gets to be a point. Overall I enjoyed this class

Professor Beneker gave awesome interactive lectures! He had a severe personal issue arise during the semester and did his best to support his class and get sub-professors for the class. I really appreciated his efforts and sincerity in this, plus his exams were straight forward and he gave a lot of support in through assignments/groupwork.

AWESOME PROF. So passionate about what he teaches, and it shows in his lectures. He knows a ton about classical mythology and conveys it to the class really well. Lectures were laid-back and informative. All of the TA's offered cool ideas and topics of discussion. Not a ton of work, just reading, 2 papers and 2 tests. Would totally recommend 370

analysis.name: Betsy (Lindsay) Stovall
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Alright, ignore all good reviews for math 217 for this woman. She's bad. Doesn't explain a thing, just writes equations on the board then repeats what the equations say. Tests are a pain because she doesn't explain ANYTHING and goes on to give hard problems. 010, and you get to feel super unprepared for a cumulative final. Thanks Khan Academy.
Do not take her if you do not have to. She just rambles on up front and does not seem to care that the average for her first exam was 29%. Her tests are very hard.

Betsy is an amazing, kind prof who explains hard concepts clearly. HOWEVER, Math 475 (Spring 2025) was horribly structured: almost no resources, one massive book, HW w/ very theoretical qs, no solutions b/c they were from a friend's book. Got my first & prob last BC. I DON'T RECOMMEND HER for Math 475.

Professor Betsy was a great professor. She would go over the homework on Tuesday so we get more prepared for the weekly quiz. Exams weren't too bad. So if you pay attention in class and sometimes read the textbook for clarification, you should be fine. By the way this review is for Math 475, I don't know why it is not included in the course code.
Tests are one hundred times harder than quizzes and homework. Her teaching style is confusing and there are much easier methods she does not teach

analysis.name: Beatriz Botero
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is supposedly an easy grader, but only if you're the same ethnicity as her. I have had her ask me some questionable things, she is very passionate but you don't know your grade till the end of the semester and if you're not an amazing writer you won't get an A.

I Took ILS 367 with Professor Botero. She is the best professor I've had; super caring, passionate, and enjoys teaching her students. She is a very good literary analyst and explains difficult concepts between texts with ease. Be ready to read books, attend every discussion section, and participate in discussions by asking and answering questions.

I took ILS 367 (Migration in the Americas) in F24 with her. She is super passionate about what she teaches and the course material is always unexpectedly insightful. Her lectures are delivered with thematic clarity and always end on a conclusive note. She makes you think about the hidden details in passages that may otherwise not have been noticed.

Beatriz is the best professor at UW! She cares so much about her students both in class and out of class. She is extremely knowledgable and culturally fluent. You would be making a huge mistake not to take her class! Only criticism I can give is she doesn't put grades in canvas and there is a lot of reading required (but it is very interesting).

One of the best prof I have had here. She is super energetic and passionate about her lectures, and you can really tell that she is aiming for the best for her students. The course material is interesting, and the lectures are structured so that we get to share our experiences and thoughts throughout the semester.

analysis.name: Maria Soledad Benguria Depassier
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 133 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Prof Benguria appears to care about her students, but outsources too much of the work.  Homework assignments are poorly prepared.  Exams do not reflect the material covered in the course.

I have taken a different math teacher since algebra and not only was this the worst math class I have taken. The tests are hard and are 80% of the grade. There is also no direction on what to study for each test which can add more stress. Complacency is the problem here.

I would highly recommend taking her for Math 222. She shows lots of examples and she will stop in the middle of lecture and ask if we have any questions and clarify any. Super sweet lady. Although her tests aren't terribly hard, the course itself is tricky and she makes it more understandable. Gives a generous curve!

I thought she would be a good teacher, because all of her reviews were pretty good. I was highly disappointed by her teaching style and lack of communication with students. I dreaded going to her class and it was the worst one I have taken here. DO NOT TAKE HER

Prof Soledad is so sweet. She always gives many examples to ensure that you understand the concepts. The weekly homework was super long and not too related to the material on the exam but overall the class was a good experience.

analysis.name: Bjorn Eraker
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very hard to follow lectures that don't exactly correlate with exam materials. Lots of talk about topics he finds interesting rather than course relevant. Easy grader but having him actually grade anything is rare, as on the day of the final the midterm grade wasn't even visible in Canvas. Course is decently interesting but hard to take from Eraker

He is very smart but lectures can be all over the place. I have no interest in the subject so they were boring to me, and I taught myself everything right before tests, but that's not really his fault. Midterm was difficult but he provided lots of practice materials and graded generously. This class could've been torture but he made it manageable.

This was one of the most disorganized classes I've taken. Expectations and grading were unclear, and communication felt minimal throughout the semester. I often felt unsupported in understanding the material. I would recommend other instructors if you prefer clearer structure and guidance.

Bjorn is hilarious and enthusiastic about his work. Very intelligent guy and can relate to students well. 330 is the hardest class in the UW Finance curriculum, so no way around taking this class. Bjorn is a great option. Trading assignments are real world, so it's not just theory and models. Can come across as intimidating but definitely isn't.

Professor Eraker taught an interesting class; however, the lectures were difficult to follow and take notes on due to tangents and frequent back and forth between slides in class. It's incredibly important to pay attention to detail in the slides, and reference them frequently for studying and assignments.

analysis.name: Rikhil Bhavnani
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Probably the best Professor I have ever had and will ever have. Rikhil teaching style is the most organized and easy-to-understand I could imagine. He makes every topic in the class interesting and every reading if fruitful and serves a purpose! The exams are fair and did not spend a lot of time studying for them. Would 100% recommend Rikhil!

This class was fairly easy. He did not clearly outline the first of two exams and I did not know that he would expect us to be able to attach the names of the authors we had read throughout the course to their ideas. There is a very small sample size for the evaluations in the form of 2 exams consisting of 5 IDs and 1 essay. Do the readings.

Lectures were interesting and material may be applied to real world situations. Professor was very knowledgable and has a background in development. I looked forward to going to lecture. Tests are IDs and an essay but nothing that isn't difficult. Readings are long but may be skimmed. Recommend to anyone interested in the topic.

Course title "Indian Politics in Comparative Perspective" was hands down one of the best courses I've taken in Poli Sci. Professor Bhavnani is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject (he studied at Yale and Stanford, from Bombay originally) and is a fantastic seminar facilitator. Not necessarily an easy A, but worth it.

I really enjoyed Professor Bhavnani's lectures, you could tell that he knew what he was talking about and really enjoyed the subject. analysis.name: Sean Bishop

Sean was an engaging teacher who didn't care about the quality of your writing, but focused on making you a better writer.
As long as you did your work (which was very manageable), you were able to get a very high A. I loved his class, it was fun and straightforward.

Sean was a great professor for our class on Literary Publishing. He cared so much about helping us succeed in this field. He really wants us to do well. The content was super engaging and interesting. He always made us laugh, too. I appreciate how realistic he was, but how much he believed in us, too.

analysis.name: Bill Bement

analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bement is a sweet guy though his teaching felt sub par. You can pass by reading the words in blue font on the slides without going to class, which may help some students, but I prefer lectures that reshape ideas clearly in a digestible way. An A is doable but takes more work than the other units because he doesn't really elaborate in lectures.

Dr. Bement is a really nice guy and wants his students to succeed. He has additional office hours before exams which is really helpful. He has everything you need to know on his lecture slides. Terrible lecturer, slides used in classes are way too over crowded and he just reads everything on the slide instead of explaining how things actually worked.

Tangental and comedically monotone. Lectures can be boring and even painful to sit through, but it's overall an interesting course and professor Gartner is always happy to answer a question or discuss.

Prof's Gartner's exams aren't bad, but you need to go to lecture & study to do well. Lectures are amazing anyways--easily one of the most engaging professors I've ever had, incredibly passionate too. analysis.name: Billy Jackson

analysis.name: Brendan Blackwell

analysis.name: Brandon Bloch

Dr Blair was a good professor and has an awesome hat collection. His slides were a little unorganized but all lectures and slides were posted online after class so it helped when retaking notes from lecture. Overall, effective prof and the knowledge expected on exams was made clear.

Seth is a good guy, but his lectures are not very inspiring or exciting. Uncurved class, and exams are pretty difficult. Lab sections are very boring and sections in this course is disorganized. Insanely lecture-heavy, but constantly has a horrible lecture structure spending way too much time on everything easy and brushing past anything difficult. analysis.name: Paul Block

He was a great professor. You have fun in lectures and don't fall asleep. He makes you appreciate the class and has set it up really well. She's great! It's clear she really really cares about her students and has a heart of gold. You will do well if you show up and do all of your quizzes.
