review_highlights.comment: Tests are an unreasonable estimation of lecture and textbook understanding, and questions are phrased ineffectively. There is a lot of textbook reading (hundreds of pages) and lecture material is just as important. Brad's constant attempts at distasteful humor distracts from the interesting material, and his personal anecdotes get pretty weird.

This diva was genuinely the worst experience of my life. Lectures felt as if he was reading out of a diary, but not a damn cohesive thought was in the room. 3 exams - 34 questions each, genuinely set up for failure. Words cannot describe the distain I have for this professor. DO NOT TAKE WITH HIM!!!!!

If you have a neuro background, the class isn't too bad, but no matter how much you study (whether you're a Neuro major or a Psych major or anything), it's easy to get tripped up on his confusing exam questions. The fact that he won't usually put his slides online means you have to pay VERY close attention during class.

I  really liked Postle but his class was very hard. The readings take a long time, at least an hour each and there are multiple a week. Without the readings you really can't get a good score on the exams. His lectures are informative but he moves quickly and his slides are mainly diagrams that he explains, but easy to miss details

He's okay, obviously knows what he is talking about which is always a good thing and was able to make real life connections to what we were learning. Study the quizzes for the exams, as the exams are worth 75% of your grade. He can sometimes come off as arrogant or pretentious, but I suppose you'll have that in a professor who studies what he does.

analysis.name: Brooke Godfrey
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Brooke has a very fun personality that makes her teaching both memorable and exciting. I've had several classes with her and she is very understanding and also teaches a lot of great lessons that can be used in the real world. She's extremely creative which is very useful in design studies courses. I've enjoyed every class I've had with her.

Brooke is extremely talented and very helpful when you talk to her outside of class.  However she reads word for word from slides so it is very hard to write everything down and she always seemed like a harsh and unfriendly person during lecture.  Tests are easy as long as you know the material but the projects are VERY time consuming.

Brooke is the best teacher I've had at Madison. She is a backbone of the design program. She is so willing to help, meet outside of class, and engages the students easily. I could not recommend more. She is phenomenal.

Brooke is by far the best teacher I've had at UW.  She is extremely helpful and knowledgeable.  I loved her class and she makes the entire experience really fun.  I can't wait to take another class with her!!!
Important class for art or design majors.  Still useful for other people, but a lot of work.  Covered the basics, what I expected for a 100 level class.

analysis.name: Bulent Sarlioglu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Sarlioglu is so kind and understanding. He truly wants the best for his students. 230 is one of the hardest classes (a flipped classroom) I've taken but he ended up curving the entire class by a decent amount. You have to attend class and stay really on top of content or it stacks up fast.

230 is a flipped classroom, but still a solid professor. He is understanding (5 extra minutes on midterms), and describes how to set up circuit problems. The course itself demands a mix of memorization and application, which the professor follows w/ good balance. Occasionally makes mistakes, but nothing more than a sign flip.

Professor Bulent was great he made a great effort teaching the material in lecture and was clearly passionate. The coursework itself was flipped so you had to study before hand a lot but overall pretty achievable.
Professor Bulent was very knowledgeable about the material and spoke very clearly. Would take a class with this professor again.

analysis.name: Derrick Buisch
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Derrick is such an amazing and caring professor. He was flexible with due dates and offered extra credit if needed. I took Art 222 and it was one of my favorite classes I have taken, so I definitely recommend him.
He is such a caring and chill guy, he's super flexible and always willing to help. He offers revisions if you want to earn more points on projects, as well as extra credit opportunities.

Beyond amazing - doesn't make you do annoyingly specific projects. You guide your learning and use him as a resource. I look up my instructors art before and after taking a class, and I got a new vibe from his work after having him as an instructor. He's quiet, yet awkwardly funny. Opposite of his pop art style, which makes his art more intriguing.

Great prof with an easy-going personality. Positive reinforcement teaching style. Gives detailed assignments, but talks one-on-one with students making sure everything's clear. Very knowledgable in color and painting techniques. He is very strict with time, and the class time is 8:50. Make sure you are good at time management if you want to take it

Derrick is a very chill professor, with a somewhat quirky, dry humor. I had ART222. Most of the class he gave us the prompt and some vague direction, and then let us loose to paint, with the ability to use him as a resource. He'll go over the exact points of why he's giving you a grade, with the ability change your work for a higher one.

analysis.name: Barry Burden
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Burden is great. He makes the issues of elections clear in a digestible and fairly non-partisan format and feels more down-to-earth than most professors. His intelligence is also very clear, but he never felt like he talked down to us. His lectures were quite topical and focused with room for questions/participation. Light readings.

Dr. Burden is probably one of favorite professors at this school. He knows everything about American politics and often does panel talks for the University related to that field. The lectures are interesting and focus on concepts you would cover in a civics class. However, I never opened the textbook, and I'm not even sure why he assigns one.

I took two classes with Professor Burden, and both were great. Exams are most of your grade & draw on readings/lectures, so making sure that you do the readings and know main ideas is really important. Lectures were amazing and taught me a lot, and going over them before exams helps you figure out what the key terms for short ID are going to be.

I enjoyed this class and all of the discussions. This is such an interesting field of study. My only issue with Barry Burden is his lack of staying non bias. While it is clear that he tries to stay non partisan, many times throughout the semester his political side would show which did not help when trying to form your own opinion.

Prof Burden has been the best professor I have had at this school. He is great to talk to and great to listen to. He knows what he is talking about and conveys his knowledge in interesting ways. His research is very interesting and definitely worth a read. I would 100% recommend any of his classes to any student.

analysis.name: Sam Butcher
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Butcher teaches the first unit of Biochem 501 and he is an okay professor. His tries to make his lectures engaging but it really depends on you if you like the subject. He almost always runs out of time for the amount of content that he planned. The class is test heavy but as long as you study and do the practice exams, the tests are fairly easy.

Extremely average instructional abilities; very mid at explaining conceptual stuff and quite bad at explaining math. Will be saving his lecture recordings to use as white noise because goodness knows they put me to sleep. Practice exams were really helpful, they're just like the real test. Overall impression: really boring but not outright awful.

Compared to the other Biochem 501 professors, I really liked Sam. He teaches in a way that is easier to understand for students that have never heard of these concepts, even though he's studied this stuff for years and does research on it. Accessible outside of class and very kind and friendly.

Overall it was very clear that Dr Butcher cared about me and the rest of the students he taught. He is available outside of class and is willing to go beyond the lectures if you are curious about the material. Highly recommend!

He was a good professor because he did his job well. He teaches what is on the exam. He does provide background information, but lets you know it is not required. His exam reflects the material covered.

analysis.name: Nick Buttrick
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Buttrick is very knowledgeable, and a funny guy, doesn't feel like a professor but more like a friend. He understands his material well and teaches it well. He's also very forgiving with grading, and he knows you are human. Great guy

He is very knowledgable, well-spoken and his lectures are intriguing. After exams, you can get some points back by doing a "report" about your wrong answers. He takes feedback on exams, so if someone points out a mistake, or if over 75% of the students get one wrong, he will regrade that question. However, some readings are long and time-consuming.

There is a lot of reading, but it is manageable. Lectures are mandatory and checked with TopHat, but TopHat has had a lot of issues so I'm not sure if it's going to stay for his next semester. Tests are online and open-note so very manageable to do if you prepare well.

Lectures are interesting and engaging, though heavily based on research studies. Lots of reading that can be exhausting, but if you're interested in culture, it'll be interesting by default. There are 3 exams, a final paper, a discussion section, & attendance. Exams are open-note & online, so take good ones! Overall easy, informative, good class.

This class for the most part wasn't difficult. Tests can be challenging as its mostly reading and applying whatever concepts fit. Its not like a basic question and answer level test. Paper at the end isn't hard tbh, just get a feeling of what your TA is looking for.

analysis.name: Byung-jin Lim
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He's an amazing professor and great at his job. He makes studying Korean fun and entertaining. Attendance is mandatory for all sections of class, but it's definitely for your own good. There's homework assigned after each class, but if you keep up with the material, it doesn't take long at all.

My favorite professor at UW. Korean can be a difficult language to learn but he makes it fun and easy. He tries to include TV, music, movies, and culture into the lectures so it's not just straight grammar and reading. There is a lot of repetition, but that's necessary for language learning. He's always super helpful and will answer any questions.

He's one of the best professors I've ever had! The lectures are really interesting, the homework isn't busy work, and he genuinely cares about us as individuals. He tries to make connections to Korean media he thinks we'd be interested in and he gives us a lot of autonomy when it comes to pair work and projects. He grades very leniently as well.

Prof Lim is a great, straightforward professor. I didn't always learn much during lecture, but he put in a lot of effort to make sure the content was understood. He does call on people a lot, but he won't call on you if you ask him not to. There are a lot of small homeworks, but they are very easy. He can be a little scary, but he's really nice :)

Great Professor! One of my favorite classes I've taken as UW-Madison. If you follow the class expectations, it's easy to get a good grade-just study and you'll do well! Very friendly to talk to, and his concern and care regarding students is easy to see. Would definitely recommend him to anyone debating taking Korean at UW-Madison.

analysis.name: Byron Shafer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The 2.5 hour lecture does get long, but he is a very knowledgeable person.  HIs past experiences allow him to go more in-depth on topics other professors don't.  However, lecture is very boring.  You have a midterm that is wroth 40% of your grade and a 20-30 page term paper.  Study the lecture and terms from the book and you'll get an A.

To offer a more pessimistic rating, I would not recommend this professor at all. There were only two grades for the entire class, so if one grade is poor, then the final course grade will also be poor. Minimal work though, none of the reading mattered besides the terms. The term paper at the end is tough, so get a head start on it!

I took him for Intro to American Politics for Honors and it was a fairly easy class.  A 25-30 page research paper is about the only major thing to worry about.  His tests are not very hard and the books are not used at all. He assigns readings but very little comes from there that he doesn't cover in lecture.  Very nice guy too!

The material wasn't thrilling, but that being said Shafer is a very knowledgable professor and I would definitely recommend him. The class consisted of a midterm, a final paper, and a final exam... which was cancelled (based on what the class voted on). Start the paper early, 20 page minimum requires a lot of work.

Professor Shafer knows a lot about American government.  However, class was fairly boring (due to long lecture).  Mid term was pretty easy, and the class votes whether or not to have a final after midterms.  20-30 page research paper also due the day of the final...ouch!

analysis.name: Charles Byers
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Awesome professor and really interesting class. Easy to take difficulty for granted because you basically don't do any work until the exam, which can be pretty difficult. Make sure to take good notes and don't zone out because test questions are one's you probably didn't cover that well. Hilarious guy though.

He's hilarious and lecture is very entertaining. Tests, however, are pretty tricky. You may think you know the material, but he likes to throw in "all of the above" and "none of the above" in EVERY multiple choice question. Sometimes throws in bogus questions, but that's just my opinion.

Prof. Byers is so far my favorite prof I've had in three years at UW. He loves what he teaches and makes boring topics seem interesting. He is very smart. His tests are more difficult than they should be, and sometimes studying doesn't even help. It's certainly not an easy A but DEFINETELY worth taking!

My first and greatest professor. He has a great sense of humor and makes the information very interesting. Even after lots of studying, his tests are difficult. If you know the concepts and are confused by the wording or just are unsure, ask him because he is extremely helpful and very patient.

Byers is a funny teacher and is clear during lectures. He managed to entertain me for the majority of the semester. Take good notes and pay attention in class and you will do well on the exams. I recommend this class if you are interested in evolution at all.

analysis.name: Matteo Camboni
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Camboni seems like a really nice guy but the class was brutal. Exam averages were always below 50% and were much harder than hw. My biggest gripe was there was no way to gauge how prepared you were for the exam as there was at most one homework every two weeks.The only class Ive taken where somebody gave up on the exam and turned it in blank.

Tests were nothing like what was covered in class or the problem sets; old practice tests don't help in studying as the format changed from each one. Clearly is knowledgeable but fails to simplify concepts. Few examples given in lecture. Problem sets were only form of practice. Did not provide extra resources. Mostly accessible outside of class.

Matteo was amazing. His exams are wacky and non-standard, and the whole objective of the class is to break out of the repetitive algorithm of microeconomics. We spent a lot of time analyzing edge-case scenarios, learning to think out of the box. There is no structured syllabus: he adjusted the deadlines based on the learning pace of the class.

Matteo is a really sweet guy and cares about his students. Always attentive to if students have questions or what they want more of in the class. Exams are hard and theres little practice questions. I recommend using the book even though its optional. There's a heavy curve so the difficulty doesn't go unrewarded.

good lecturer, cares about his students and promotes a casual atmosphere. one con: he often moves through course material linearly rather than repeating key concepts, so it can be easy to miss something critical if you zone out for a few minutes. but the problem sets help you realize anything you missed.

analysis.name: Jill Casid
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I would strongly urge NOT taking this course. In theory the readings are thoughtful, and the concepts are interesting, but there's little to no organization for assignments, and noticeable unprofessionalism in lectures. Overall, for how much the class is oriented around communicaton; it GREATLY lacks instruction to achieve a good grade!!

This class was all about accessibility, which is ironic. She shamed student presenters and assigned incredibly dense, long readings. The readings were hardly ever discussed in class. The cherry on top was the tone-deaf assignments. We had to create a project based on "the closest we have ever been to disabled." Triggering and problematic.

I concur with many of the comments presented here about Prof Casid.  Wonderful human being and subject matter expert, but not a competent educator.  I enjoyed the exposure to visual culture, but Jill is simply out of touch with reality about student needs to an concerning degree. I do not recommend her courses to those new to art history.

I don't recommend taking this class. The readings are super long and unnecessary, and the slides don't help clarify anything. The projects all have confusing prompts that don't make sense. Attendance is mandatory. I took this class for the ethnic studies requirement, but there are definitely many more interesting courses with better professors.

DO NOT take this class if you are someone in touch with the real world. Many of the required readings and videos for the class are extremely unprofessional. The class deeply struggles to intertwine all its content (nothing has anything to do with what you do in the next class), and the professor is obviously unprepared for the lectures.

analysis.name: Matt Bowman
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 294 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Matt is the best instructor I have ever had. Exams were very fair and he gives you all the tools you need to succeed. There is a little extra credit (.01%). Lectures are fun to go to. There are 6+hrs of office hours per week with nearly an extra 20 before the final. A very caring, friendly, and funny guy. Matt is seriously the best!

Matt is THE professor to get for o chem. He's super nice, personable, and extremely helpful. Class is based on 4 quizzes and 5 exams. Matt posts lots of helpful videos and worksheets to help understand the material better. Lots of practice exams to prepare for actual exams. The best professor hands down!!!

He is an awesome professor that makes Ochem as manageable as it can be.   My advice for doing well in the course:  Do the problem set worksheets as they are given (one almost every lecture) and understand them.  Also, reread your notes everyday, takes 10 minutes a day and makes a huge difference.

Professor Bowman is hands-down the best professor I've ever had. Ochem is difficult on its own, but Matt clears the path for you to really dive in and learn what you need to know. His online videos are fantastic and great for better understanding. Want success? Do the homework he provides and stay diligent. He is truly cares about his students.

Matt's lecture is really worth taking. His course website is really good. Lecture notes, lecture videos, practice exams and video of some answer keys are all available and updated really fast. He himself is a really nice person. Funny and caring. A good choice if you want to learn organic chemistry.

analysis.name: Carin Loewen
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Loewen is very kind and cares a lot about her students. I see a lot of people hating and I don't know why. An important caveat to her classes is that you have to be interested in the topic and willing to take lecture notes as well as pay attention in class. She is very helpful during office hours and always easily accessible by email.

AWFUL! Multiple assignments (wc~300) on top of very, very long required study guides (~60 long-form questions) each week. Tough grader + lots of busy work. Had technical problems for an exam and didn't let me retake it. Kinda rude over email as well. Many classmates had worse experiences as well. RMP has a WC limit, but I have a lot more complaints

I've enjoyed Neurogenetics with Dr. Loewen this semester. She's a passionate and entertaining lecturer. Exams are online and open note, so I found taking good notes helpful. Some busy work for pre-lectures, but not difficult to complete and makes lecture easier to follow. If you're interested in the topics, I would recommend.

Very interesting course, and Dr. Loewen seemed passionate about this material. She is accommodating and is quick to reply to emails. There are pre-class assignments before each class, with five drops. The exams were all online and doable with a good understanding of the material.

All of the lectures were recorded and posted onto Canvas, making it easier to look back on notes. She also spoke in the perfect speed. Although, the quizzes had material that we never covered in class.

analysis.name: Alicia Cerezo-Paredes
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I normally hate literature, so I was really worried to take a literature class in Spanish, but Alicia made it a decently enjoyable class for me. She does a great job of connecting with students and helping them. She also makes content very interesting and understandable. Attend class, do the readings, and participate, and you should do well.

At first I wasn't sure about Alicia, but she is AMAZING! She went above & beyond to help/check on me when I had a family emergency and genuinely cares about students' success. Make an effort to contribute to class discussions one or twice each class period and you will get an A. Also, some of the readings are actually phenomenal!

Alicia is the absolute best! I took 3 of her classes and loved them all. Show up to class, do the readings/homework, and participate. Assignments are designed to facilitate our understanding of the material and she makes sure EVERYONE in  class understands. Alicia is the most caring, hilarious, and thorough professor I've ever had!! Take her class!

First of all, Alicia is the cutest human. That said, she is also a great professor. I find literature classes challenging to begin with, so taking them in my second language is normally a nightmare. However, Alicia is a wonderful professor. She really makes a great effort to make sure that her students understand the material. Tests are fair too.

She is a wonderful professor, but sometimes she goes overboard on reading assignments. Having to read 170 pages of a Spanish book for two class periods and write is simply ridiculous. I would take her again, but for some of her bigger books she has you read you really need to plan ahead, and hope you don't have any other exams that week.

analysis.name: B. Marcus Cederstrom
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is knowledgeable, receptive to feedback and differing opinions, engaging, genuine, funny, kind, and interesting. He is one of those rare teachers who really cares about his students well-being.

Marcus is a really great professor. He is very interested in Folklore, and even though I am not, I found his attitude towards the subject made the class more enjoyable. He is a generally easy grader, he wants you to focus on the content and knowledge you gain from the readings and activities. For sure take one of his classes for humanities credit.

Prof. Cederstrom really cares about your mental health and allows for paper extensions. The content is super easy and you only really need to attend lecture a majority of the time, the main content is the first few weeks then everything is building upon it. 5 main papers/projects that aren't too hard, but don't wait to finish them. Easy graders.

Professor Cederstrom's awesome. His lectures were super interesting and filled with memes. The class enabled me to relate folklore to my daily life + have a better understanding of the communities I am a part of. There were a few papers and a final project due, but it's definitely manageable + enjoyable. Would 100% take it with him again :D

Marcus tries to make his lectures interesting with humor but they didn't help me much. The lectures aren't mandatory but there are pop questions that are either graded or for extra credit. The discussions are mandatory. This class has lots of papers but are very easy to get full credit. Definitely recommend if you want an easy comm b class.

analysis.name: Belkis Cerrato Caceres
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Don't even try to take notes because the content she uses on exams and quizzes is nothing that we learned. There were multiple occasions where I was asked a question on an exam and I had never heard or seen the content before, and I read the book along with attending every lecture. She uses irrelevant examples and they do not make sense at all.

Belkis is not the primary teacher for this class, and it really shows. She uses outdated examples in her lectures and isn't the clearest on some ideas, but the topics covered in this class aren't difficult so it is not that bad. The annoying part was the group project and paper due just before the final exam. Show up to class and this won't be bad.

She cares about her students but her experience teaching seems a little questionable. She has a PhD in Econ and clearly knows a lot about the subject. The class wasn't  difficult as long as you do all the assignments and attend lecture. The end of the semester was annoying because of the group paper, presentation, and then the final on top of that.

analysis.name: Cecile Ane
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Cecile is a sweetheart. Do extra practice problems because the homework isn't enough. The group project makes this class feel like 4 credits, not 3. She can be vague, so be assertive and keep asking questions. Grading was picky, they were skimpy on partial credit. And problems were worth a lot of points each. She uses the R project extensively.

Best professor ever! Cecile uses extremely interesting examples, and offers real insight. She is very helpful during office hours, and gives fair exams. She also extremely attractive. So extremely attractive. And she has a French accent, which multiplies the attractiveness by at least ten. It makes a good class that much more interesting.

Ane is very helpful and obviously passionate about this material. While the material of this course isn't too difficult, the course itself was harder than I expected. Homework was pretty difficult and relied a lot on the statistics program R, of which I had no prior experience. It also seemed to be graded inconsistently or arbitrarily.

the most adorable flake you'll ever come across!!  she simplifies anthing that can be simplified and information for tests is given straightforward in lecture and in homework.  the class is, miraculously, easy yet semi-interesting.

Pointless. Haven't been to lecture or discussion in over 4 months. Stats lab is essential for homework, which is worth a big part of your grade. Tests are open book, making it easy to teach yourself most concepts. Try to get the other 371 teacher, I've heard they're better.

analysis.name: Duncan Carlsmith
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 101 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: AVOID AT ALL COSTS. 5cr. class, feels like 10. There is a mountain of HW to do every week. Lec's r completely pointless and popsci for an hnrs/acc seq. Lec's r mandatory (TopHat att. and Qs). Matlab is used for labs--extr'ly diff. & time-consuming. Mumbles in lec. Not once has he gone through and done a complete example Q in lec. u willearn nothing

Lectures are pointless and far too pop sci-y for what is supposed to be an advanced introductory physics coursehe once spent a lecture talking about bombs, which had nothing to do with the scheduled unit. Doesn't care to talk about math much. Provides relatively little material for exam preparation. Labs are alright, but terribly time consuming.

Interesting professor with tons of energy and enthusiasm for physics, but lectures are not representative of the exams. Spends more time on digressions than the actual subject you are learning. Averages grade in the class was about 50% but that ended up being an AB. Avoid this professor, his lectures only serve to confuse you further.

Please listen to the recent reviews. This class is an easy A, but I promise you will learn nothing. Lectures: barren of real teaching, maybe had 3 examples the entire semester. Labs: annoyingly impossible Matlab programming. Homework: ton of it, all useless. Exams: stupid and relatively easy. Discussion TA: saved our lives. Take another intro class

Best place to browse reddit and have a laugh, look at flat earth theories, convince your self that it is flat. Good 50 mins to get caught up on homework your two days behind - three times a week. Also one of the classes where you spend considerable time thinking about the miserable life choices you made, and drifiting away from reality

analysis.name: Sara Chadwick
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Chadwick is an incredibly passionate and knowledgeable professor. Her lecture slides are always well-designed, well written, and often includes relevant media, like TikToks/videos to prompt discussion. She's got great humor and wit, so class discussions are a blast & you learn a lot. Much reading, but each is broken down accessibly in class.

I LOVED Professor Chadwick. She was so engaging, relatable, funny, intelligent, and charismatic. Her lectures were super interesting, and even though the textbook got a little boring, she would find an interesting study/video to tie it back. This was her first class as professor and she knocked it out of the park!

Very organized, very knowledgeable, lectures are well structured and interactive, offers EC, fun discussion sections and the course content is sooo interesting. You learn something that improves your relationships and sex life every day. Some people saying tests are too hard/specific but if you're a real STEM major you'll sleep through this class
She basically just read from the PowerPoint.

Sara is a great professor, and very engaging. The class material was fascinating; however, the final grade depends on 4 exams (the last is cumulative!!) an article response paper, and an essay on a book. So if you bomb an exam, it will tank your grade. The discussions are mandatory points, you only get one sick day, not worthwhile in my eyes.

analysis.name: Chris Rycroft
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Incredibly dense class, but he makes it work. His lectures are good, he uses a lot of graphs to help you understand different theorems and such. His homework problems are long and difficult, but they're (usually) fair, and they do a great job at solidifying your understanding of different topics and theorems. One of my favorite lecturers at UW.

Highly recommend mainly bc we rarely used Rudin. Lectures closely followed Kenneth Ross' book, which is very accessible. Caring prof and responded well to Piazza questions. Homework was very hard, with 2 weeks for ~12 problems. Exams had very strict time limits, but class was curved heavily (A:76, D:40). Practice exams closely matched exams. 8/10

This was the worst class, wish I had never taken it.  Disorganized, lectures were rambling, difficult to understand.  And the  color theme with coordinating nails!  Save yourself from sitting through this.

Module assessments or "exams" do NOT align with this class being approached through global health. Group project was also a terrible experience.

One of the worst instructors at UW. She made her personal mission to harass students saying more then 50% of the class used AI to complete the work even though many people didn't, she asked us to redo the assignment for half the credit even after providing proof and continued to give random scores for assignments that are graded on completion.

Participation is necessary and if you miss a few lectures your grade drops. The podcast project is time consuming and you will need access to a recording studio if you plan to get a good grade on it.

The content of this course is pretty interesting but she doesn't present it that way. Very monotone and tends to go on tangents about things that seem unnecessary. The course itself is pretty easy, she seems passionate about what she teaches but is not entertaining.

analysis.name: Levi Cross

I wish I could take another portuguese class.

Levi is now of my favorite professors. He is passionate about what he teaches and it is clear that he wants all his students to succeed. I enjoy coming into class and learning because of his teaching style and personality.

Levi is my favorite professor I've ever had. He is so engaging, and a really effective teacher of Portuguese. I learned so much in little time. He's very approachable, understanding, funny, and kind. I definitely recommend taking a class taught by him.

analysis.name: Scott Coyle

Prof Coyle was amazing as his first time teaching the final unit of Biochem 501. Explains things very straightforwardly (well, as straightforward as you can get in biochem). I wish I had a Dr. Coyle for all my classes!
I took biochem 501 alongside zoology 570, and this unit was super easy because of it. The exams are fair and his lectures were engaging and fun. My favorite lecturer in 501 by far!

analysis.name: Shauna Crowther

Too many homework and tough grader.

Very tough grader. You have to revise your assignments over and over again and might still get a 0. Loves to torturing students. Tons of homework.

Teeeeeeeeeedious, arrogant, nowhere near as good as he thinks he is.

analysis.name: Katherine Cramer

She was an incredible political science professor I would recommend to anyone! Her honors seminar was well thought out and well-run. She genuinely cares for each of her students and is accessible should you need her!

Professor Cramer is great. The class was very discussion focused in a good way, you get to know your classmates and I think it increases the depth of the material. Comments below sound like they are salty they are never going to make it as lawyers. Fischer is hands down the most enthusiastic and caring professor at UW.
