review_highlights.comment: CNS SCI 357- retail theory- is a really easy class to earn an A in if you do the textbook reading. You only meet once a week and she writes notes on the board each class that she copies exactly into her exams. She wants her students to do well and she cares about what she teaches!
Awesome professor, really knows her stuff. Also, she is super friendly and easy to talk to. Take time and talk to her after class if you have time. I would highly recommend her and this class.
Cynthia is super awesome and her classes are very easy. You lead two discussions and write one 8-10 page paper graded on completion. Probably my favorite UW professor of all time

analysis.name: David Wassarman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He was good and got his point across, but his lectures/slides were often hard to follow/not clear what you were supposed to take away. He was a tough grader on FRQs (the questions were simple/didn't seem to need very detailed answers but he would deduct if you didn't go in depth parts enough). Some FRQs ask about scenarios not discussed in class.

I loved Dr. Wassarman! I had an understanding of MCB before coming into class, and so his unit was very easy but I also still learned a lot. Participate in class! Talk to him after class! You may not get a 100% on the exams, but it's very easy to get a 7/8 on every question as long as you show some understanding of some relevant mechanism.

David was a good teacher but his material is TOUGH, no matter how much I studied I just could never give enough information on my short answers. I would verbatim write something from his slides and he would tell me I did not have enough depth in my answer. His exams averaged more than 10% lower than the first exams he did not teach.

Exams were incredibly difficult and he's a very fast paced lecturer. Clearly explained the processes and gave several examples, often giving many chances to ask questions after giving a summary of sections. Was very understanding and kind, truly cared for students!

He was an good professor who would would help you if asked for it, passionate about his content. The class was very difficult though with him rushing through many different things in one lecture making it very difficult to keep up.

analysis.name: Jennifer Detlor
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you can talk to her individually she is very helpful when solving problems, but its hard to initially learn when the examples given in class are pre-solved and are the example textbook problems, meaning we get like 1 example per topic. TAs also weren't very helpful. The HW took forever some days with concepts we never discussed in class.

I've missed Prof. Detlor every day since having her for statics. She goes through concepts thoroughly in a straightforward manner. I have heard she isn't super accommodating of emergencies, etc. but she clearly cares about student success and making learning a good experience.

Good lecturer who uses her time well and explains things clearly. However, she is not at all understanding of extenuating circumstances, and she did not respect my accommodations. I would not recommend if you are a McBurney student.

Although this was by far the hardest class I have taken at this university, Professor Detlor did an amazing job structuring and teaching this class. Her notes made understanding the content from the textbook a lot easier. Her exams can be quite challenging but if you just go over the notes and hw questions you'll do just fine. Definitely recommend!

Professor Detlor was a decent teacher for fluids. However, this class was the literal bane of my existence during this semester. We have homework due two days before every exam and 5 days after. I do not have enough time to study! The exams are so difficult and there are too many of them. Please give me more time to study so I can succeed.

analysis.name: Matt Delong
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Overall a very good professor, nothing stands out as amazing, but nothing stands out as a flaw either. Lectures were recorded, were usually easy to follow, with time well spent discussing new topics and going through examples. Occasionally topics at the end of lecture were rushed, but I would absolutely take another class taught by Prof. Delong.

He is a kind and caring professor. However, his exam style made the course much harder than expected. Unlike other calculus exams, his tests were heavily multiple-choice and focused more on conceptual thinking than past exams. Since exams made up about 87% of the grade, this format change made it difficult for me to prepare and perform well.

As a Calculus 3 course, Math 234 is quite challenging. The homework and worksheets of the discussion session may be relatively difficult, but the exams and quizzes are easier than those. Additionally, after class, professor Matt Delong posts all course slides on canvas, which is beneficial for students who prefer self-study.

While he is not a bad professor, his lectures are difficult to sit through, and he always rushes through the material without much depth in his explanations. He will provide practice problems in class; however, they are done before the concept has been fully explained, making them hard to complete. Most of my learning was done independently of him.

Though the class content is very difficult, Matt is such a caring and funny professor! He does a great job using analogies to simplify complicated concepts. Attendance is not required but he puts an emphasis on how important participation is. The class is a little homework heavy (~3 weekly assignments + 1 quiz) but definitely doable.

analysis.name: Alberto Del Pia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Del Pia is amazing at teaching and really cares about his students! This course is incredibly organized and well-structured. Would highly recommend!

Alberto knows what he is talking about. All of his slides come straight from the text book, but he somehow makes it more confusing than the textbook. Reading the textbook is easier than understanding his lectures. Midterms were not difficult but final was ridiculously difficult. Told us it had the same format as midterms but did not.

Very difficult class. I think Prof. Alberto is great and he is very passionate about the topics. The class is just too hard and there is a lot to remember and understand. Exams were not too difficult. I barely spend anytime on this class and was able to get an AB. HWs were very difficult and I would recommend spend a lot of time studying.

Very kind, easygoing guy. Homeworks are very manageable and instructive, it's the exams that really get ya. Alberto cares deeply about the subject matter and the course, and he is an excellent professor to have.

Prof. Del Pia provides great intuition for proofs that are actually quite deep and difficult to understand. He is very encouraging of asking questions in class, and responds to all of them in great detail, no matter how basic. It's a pity that the pandemic turned the second half of this class online but it was still great!

analysis.name: Vinay Dharwadker
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Dharwadker teaches his class in a way that makes reading literature interesting and not tedious. He opens a world to South Asian literature and his selections reflect a wide variety of styles and concepts. One of the nicest people and one of the best classes (and easiest) I've taken. Talk to him and participat and you will do more than well.

Vinay was a very resourceful & knowledgeable professor that did a great job at giving us an interdisciplinary approach to literature and made class topics relevant. The class grade is based on 2 essays and a few easy geography quizzes (with extra credit!).  Essay feedback also good. Overall  fun & laidback class. If you need a Lit credit, TAKE HIM!

Lectures are long but Professor Dharwadker is very knowledgeable and you learn a lot. His feedback on papers is very insightful. His prompts are great and the papers are enjoyable to write. His course is relatively easy and I would recommend.

I took "The Modern Short Story" to fulfill my literature requirement, and Dharwadker is a fabulous professor. He brings lots of current events and life lessons into all of his lectures on the stories. It's a great class, and he grades things pretty easily.

Professor Dharwadker is amazing. He's so caring, compassionate, and kind. He gives great feedback. Genuinely wants his students to succeed. Very knowledgeable. Great guy, great class. Put in effort (do your best) and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: David Hansen
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: David Hansen is the worst instructor I've ever met. He is terrible and the lectures are boring and long. The homework is hard and make up a large percent of overall grades. U can drop one of the two midterms and take the highest grades. But the midterms are hard.  Overall, the professor is useless and the grading sucks. But the TA is pretty good.

Very difficult course. Dr. Hansen is super kind. Several chapters of the textbook are covered in any given lecture. This is super difficult as the topics are conceptually very hard to grasp; it was not uncommon for me to attend a lecture and leave without retaining any information. TIP: Peter Dalley on YouTube has phenomenal videos for this class.

Worst college experience ever. Lecture desperately boring, keep saying uh uh uh like 4 times in one single sentence. Homework is endless, prbbly took you about 10 hrs per week, like a nightmare. Final exam is unsolvably hard, since it has absolutely nothing to do with lec, hw or dis. Econ 310 was a fine class, however ruined by him. Plz, stay from!

The homework for the class was easy but the exams were incredibly difficult. However, they are graded on a generous curve, so studying does pay off. Hansen is unfortunately a boring lecturer and does not make the content easier in instances where I felt he could have. Not a bad prof, just very average and teaching a boring, mandatory class.

Exams were very hard and averages were low however if you studied a lot you will preform above average in the class. Students were crying during the final tho. I'd read the textbook since lectures were fast paced. The syllabus doesnt say attendance Qs were graded on accuracy so I went to office hours when I got points off and he laughed in my face?

analysis.name: Dhavan Shah
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very dense, slides had lots of words. He would get off track a lot. Sometimes hard to tell what was necessary to know or not, especially when studying for exams. Plus, exams seemed unnecessary considering the sizable project we worked on throughout the course.

I didn't directly interact with him because a lot of the work for the class is done during discussion, but he's a pretty friendly guy from what I've seen in lecture. Pretty knowledgeable about the content, though the lectures can get long and kind of boring. There are 2 exams (50pt multiple choice) and 1 semester-long group project.

Professor Shah is a super nice guy and super helpful before/after class. Lecture slides are posted online, so attendence is not mandatory. The bulk of the grade is a big group project which takes a lot of outside class time/effort. The best presentations on the group project do not have to take the final exam. Easy A if you get a good group!

The group project is awful if you get paired with the wrong people, but the course concepts are interesting if you're passionate about a career in strategic communications. The capstone campaign project is a great portfolio item. Dhavan is fine as a professor -- didn't interact with him much but he's knowledgeable and respected.

Dhavan is legit the man. He is very knowledgeable about advertising, PR and media with a background in real world experience. He isn't cocky, but just a  really cool dude who happens to be a great teacher as well. Always willing to help out if you see him, canceled class so we could watch the Badger national championship game. One of the best here.

analysis.name: Gary Diffee
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great FIG professor! His class consisted of lectures, demonstrations, student presentations. He really cares about his students and wants to see them succeed.
Really great professor. Nothing bad to say about him. He is super intelligent and just a great teacher. Really great with Kines content and my favorite Kines teacher so far.

Diffee is great for the FIGS course. He is very caring and willing to help outside of class.  Projects are manageable and he is clear about what is on the final. You learn a lot of physiology. Not an easy A, but not a hard A.

His lectures sometime get disorganized as he writes stuff everywhere on the chalkboard. It is nice how he gives out outlines for each lecture so you have something to help you keep on track. Exams are pretty difficult as it is all short answer application questions. He is way more clear than the other professor for this class! Labs are pointless.

I took this class as a part of my FIG and it was so easy! Diffee is an awesome guy and although the class is more about the process and not the content, I did learn a lot from him! This class will NOT take up a lot of your time, but it will be interesting if you love kinesiology and bio! No exams or textbook, just a couple projects & one final!

analysis.name: Diana Rodriguez-Gomez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I haven't met a single person who hasn't absolutely adored Prof Rodriguez-Gomez. So so loving, so caring, and so interesting to learn from! Not to mention her course content was compelling, informative, and extremely relevant. Love her!!

Cares about students so much, and wants everyone to do well. Lectures can be a little boring but since how nice she is it makes up for it. Lots of readings but I didn't read any and did fine. Also willing to give extensions and is very understanding.

Best professor I've ever had. Class is engaging and she is super open & responsive to student needs(ie people had difficulty finding peer reviewed sources, so she decreased req'd # & helped w/ resources to find them). Really cares about students as humans and is super knowledgeable. Wants you to learn and be able to share ideas and think critically

She's the sweetest. She'd make a point to go up to everyone and ask how we were. It's obvious how much she cares about our well-being. She's willing to allow extensions, take suggestions, etc. In most classes, she lectured, then we'd do group activities. Readings were long but I didn't read them and I was fine. Class based on a few assignments.

Prof. Rodriguez-Gomez really cares about her students and wants them to engage in the material in a way that they are most passionate about. Online format made it hard to participate but I hope she can improve this. 2-3 readings for each class with 15 reading summaries due throughout the semester, 2 papers, and a final project.

analysis.name: Dietram Scheufele
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 70 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dietram is a great guy. You can tell he loves what he teaches and he is just one of those people you love to listen too. Very clear, very thought provoking.. and it's pretty straight forward to get an A in this class. No quizzes, one midterm, a final and 5 short essay responses (like 200 words) for homework. Would highly recommend!

Best class and professor that I've had at UW. He's extremely intelligent yet down to earth and truly cares about his students. The topics are super interesting and relevant. Professor Scheufele illustrates the complexity of science communication and emerging technologies; after this class, you'll become more thoughtful and aware in society.

Dietram is an amazing lecturer and very knowledeable. There is no defined rubric for the essays, but the prompt states very clearly what the TAs are specifically grading for. He gives 12 attendance quizzes (2-3 questions) throughout the semester based on content from the previous lecture.

I would definitely recommend taking 251 and would again.

Writing assignments (40% of grade) are vague and rubric-less and an inconceivably strict late policy will ruin your semester if you submit something a few hours late. Luckily the class content itself is incredibly easy so just use NotebookLM to catch up and spare yourself from having to listen to his smug and pretentious lectures.

Fantastic lecturer! Super interesting class and pretty easy if you just show up and take good notes. There is no rubric for writing assignments, but if you pay attention in class he explains how to do well and you can always ask questions!

analysis.name: Joshua Dienstag
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I liked Professor Dienstag as a person, but his lectures could be kind of out there-- having a good TA was really important to make sure I understood the readings. Overall though, I did like him and the class was a good introduction to Political Theory, just make sure you actually do the readings and be ready for those in-class essays!

I really didn't like his PS160 at first. Thought it was boring and was intimidated by the (almost) weekly essays on highly intellectual thinkers and concepts. But, this ended up being one of my favorite classes last semester! Stick with it and apply yourself even just a little. Do the readings and prepare for the essays- you will learn a LOT.

Prof Dienstag is the most knowledge person I've ever met. He gives amazing lectures. 50% of your overall grade is a final exam and essay, which was a little difficult for me. If you go to all the lectures and discussion secs. there is no reason not to do well in the class. Be warned, if you are bad at writing essays this class is not for you.

He was really nice and is actually really funny. His lectures are super dense, so you have to pay attention. Also, there is a lot of reading. It is a really complex class. 

It was challenging he was really good at teaching it, but you're not going to do well if you don't do the work. 

THIS IS NOT AN EASY A! TAKE IT IF YOU'RE ACTUALLY INTERESTED.

He is a good Lecturer, and you can tell he is passionate about the subject. In-class essays ain't half bad, but the readings can be arduous, especially some of the classics, i.e., Plato and Socrates. Time-consuming class and content can be a bit of a bore, your TA can really help make the class more engaging.

analysis.name: Dian Mawene
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Don't take this course with her unless you have to. Super insensitive and the class environment was extremely uncomfortable with her rude comments. You'll end up with an A, but it was obvious that no one in the class wanted to be there, even the ones that truly cared and wanted to learn more about disability rights.

Dian is a sweetheart with a lot of real experience to share with her students. She asks her students to be at every class and it was not hard to be there very week. She has really fun speakers come to class every week. I barely had to read all semester. Easy A if you attend lecture and do all assignments.

Her strong suit is not lecturing, but she gets you to participate and engage in class. Read the textbook, and youll ace the final. A big common sense course. Easy homework load. Super understanding when it comes to the service learning project, and is very willing to work with you and help you!

analysis.name: Djurdja Trajkovic
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is a great teacher. She thinks outside of the box and she will make you think. I am impressed by her knowledge. She is VERY good at referencing popular culture and making connections for us. Her selection of texts is awesome as she uses youtube, films, music to show culture. Her research projects are super fun! Awesome teacher!

awful awful awful spanish TA. made mistakes in spanish... no interest in students and totally indifferent towards material. misgraded assignments consistently. she looked bored in class. she didn't write the tests so it was up to us to prepare for them on our own and teach ourselves from the book. she made me dread coming to class.

Djurdja is the most understanding professor I've had at The University of Michigan. She genuinely cares about her students. She is very funny and very passionate about what she teaches. She really knows her stuff. If you have the opportunity to take a class with Djurdja--you should. She is amazing.

She is a great teacher. Her passion for literature and culture is inspiring. She knows a lot and is very good at sharing that. I loved being challenged in her classes. I strongly recommend you take a literature class with her. She thinks outside of the books.
Her passion for teaching is clear - and she leaves me wanting more.  I look forward to her class everyday - and the opportunity to gaze into her big brown eyes.

analysis.name: Dieter Van Melkebeek
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dieter teaches the material in a very convoluted math-y way that won't make sense to those just learning the material for the first time. The TAs and peer mentors are much more helpful in aiding your understanding than he is. The homeworks take a while to complete but are not unreasonably difficult if you pay attention in lecture and discussion.

Always talking to himself and illegible handwriting make the class even harder to understand. I mean, when teaching algorithm, a professor is supposed to "teach and explain" in a way that students can understand, but what he does is just "saying" in a way that he can understand. Boring professor who lives in his own world.

The professor has a terrible handwirting, and he most often doesn't use lecture slides. He uses a projector and project his handwriting duing the lecture. To make things worse, sometimes he only read out after he finished writing the sentence. It's hard (but do-able) for me to catch up with his lecture in my notes. The lectures are recorded though.

Pros: He is very knowledgeable and you will learn A LOT from him. He quickly and clearly responds to emails, online/Piazza questions, etc. The curve was generous; 78% was an A.  Cons: Words cannot describe how hard the weekly homework is. I put at least 10 hours per week into the homework. This was the hardest class I've ever taken hands down.

Nice guy, but terrible professor. The book is so old and thin, you will feel like you have no resources to go to to learn about the subject, including the Internet. Numerous times he has assigned homework problems that literally he and the TA cannot solve. It's like the unsolvable math problems from the movie Good Will Hunting.

analysis.name: Dmitry Orlov
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dmitry is a really nice guy outside of class who obviously cares about the subject. However, he doesn't seem to understand how difficult this material is for students and rushes through material. The examples he gives in class don't help at all with the homework and he doesn't take enough time to clarify what variables mean/where #'s come from.

The midterm was hard but the average was much higher than anticipated. The concepts toward the end of the semester were helpful because they were on Excel (this is during the Coronavirus semester). He goes too fast and isn't good at explaining, you kind of figure it out the reasoning at the end. His slides have lots of info he never goes over.

Some of the comments here are too rough. Dmitry is one of the most caring professors I ever had at UW-Madison. He gives his students everything. Yes, the material is hard and it takes time to digest stuff, but it will all come together if you put in the work. Also, this was Dmitry's first teaching experience at UW.

I second that the other reviews are too harsh, definitely nowhere near the worst b school prof. He couldn't explain tough concepts well, expected too much prior knowledge, if you can get past confusing parts you can get a lot out of the class. What wasn't understandable was the insane workload but he eventually lessened it. Absolutely hilarious tho

Goes above and beyond and willing to do anything to help you. He's too nice that sometimes it's cringeworthy because he's so scared of offending anyone. Tests very similar to practice tests(40% of grade). Hw is fine but can take long. High bar for A because everyone scores well and tests are open note. Final project course grading subjective asf.

analysis.name: Dmytro Arinkin
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I attended every lecture. He is very knowledgeable and knows how to teach. He is humorous and friendly. He is open to questions and will answer your questions patiently, and won't let you feel bad. Provides you with a categorical point of view, introduces you the modern algebra. I'm afraid I've left too much unsaid, but I am out of space.

Overall, a very good professor.  I thought he presented the material clearly and he was engaging, given it was a 75 min. lecture.  I really enjoyed how he began each lecture with a 5-10 min. recap of the important topics from the previous lecture.  Exams were somewhat difficult but were similar to the provided practice exams.

He is really engaging; kept me focused for a power lecture. His accent is cool too. It reminds me of a Russian Mario.  Calc. 3 is a tough class but Professor Arinkin really helps you visualize everything.  Rather than just copy from the textbook he does examples that help master concepts.  Really smart and quirky dude.

Awesome professor. Extremely helpful and clear both in lecture and office hours. Exams are very close to samples. Homework problems were somewhat difficult but class was enjoyable with him. Found free legal pdf of our textbook.

A phenomenal professor! Very clear and provides plenty of motivation! Couldn't wait for the lectures every week because I was learning so much in each of them! 

Also, he engages you as a student by asking questions and inviting participation. I think it's the ideal way to teach a course, though it takes a very capable professor to teach this way.

analysis.name: Susan Dominguez
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: she's an engaging professor, but she's particularly harsh on students and uses the 'old age' card to get away with it. Even walking up to her and asking her a doubt/correction error or literally anything was a scary experience because her responses were kinda passive aggressive and standoffish. Overall an interesting professor,though.

Susan Dominguez is objectively the worst professor I have had in my time at UW. Her assignments are worth very few points, and small mistakes are penalized. In my experience, she has a profound lack of respect for students and was extremely condescending when asked questions. It is quite a bummer because the course material is interesting.

A terribly run class with confusing instructions that won't she wouldn't even explain on. The content of this class was unbelievably great, but the way that we were dissecting the readings was unbearable. She asked for things to see in papers, but then took away points for adding that exact thing.

On first day, when the only POC walked in, she yelled at him for being 15 seconds late and no one else who was late. She won't assign 1000+ word papers until a few days before they're due, and they're only 4 points with small grammar mistakes being -0.25 EACH. Talks a lot about when we "get to the real world." Made me come to class w/ a concussion.

This professor was beyond disorganized. She would ramble on end for the entire lecture time about unrelated topics like 9/11 and the Vietnam war (she never made an attempt to relate this to any native nations). She also was extremely hostile to students who would ask questions or attempt to provide accurate data on reservation life or covid stats.

analysis.name: Douglas  Rosenberg
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class is really interesting, but all of the learning you do is done through sections and taught by the TAs. There isn't a point in really going to the lecture or even taking notes, except that attendance is mandatory. He mostly rambles, and almost none of the lecture content is on tests—nice guy, but just not my fav lecturer.

Doug is amazing and super cool. We dressed up as him for Halloween and he loved it. He gives great lectures, but his hearing isn't great so if you answer a question you might have to yell a little if you're in the back.
Excellent and knowledgeable professor. Taught me so much.

Such an easy class! I barely payed any attention and I got an A. Although, I did learn A LOT more than I anticipated. Quite interesting actually for a science major! My TA Rebecca was awesome, I lucked out! For exams, be able to describe the major artists discussed in lec/discussion & their works/what they are known for and you are golden!

Super good class and I learned quite a bit last year. Dr. Rosenberg was interesting to hear speak, sometimes a little tiresome but easy to comprehend with a clear passion for what he teaches. The TAs were also so helpful and personable. Just show up, take pretty good notes, and review for like 30 minutes before the exams and you're golden.

analysis.name: Anhai Doan
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This was the only professor that I clapped for 10 minutes after the last lecture. Marvolous lectures which are easy to understand. Funny style of teaching that helps you concentrate on the class. Important life-time ideas that you should keep in mind even outside Database world. You are my light in my academic life, Anhai!

Anhai is a nice guy but if I had to describe him in one word, it would be LAZY. He barely takes lectures and the exams are uninspiring, to say the least (basically if you can cram definitions, you do well). Take him if you need a chill course and don't plan to learn a lot from it.

He's the funniest professor in the CS department—I didn't go to any lectures, but when I was cramming for exams, I actually wished I had. I would voluntarily listent to his stories and unsolicited life advice.

He does water down the course heavily tho. So if you're here for vibes, he's your guy. If you're here to learn, maybe look elsewhere.

Prof Anhai is the Uncle Iroh equivalent of UW madison - if that interests you, take the class with him. 

PS. gives a lot of tips for tech interviews

TAKE THE CLASS WITH ANHAI.
Professor 2% created genuinely engaging lectures filled with iconic quotes, jokes, as well as the class you actually signed up for. It's only graded by two exams and five group assignments. The assignments are all manageable and the exams connect to the lectures well. Is this a good or bad thing? "It depends."

analysis.name: Doug Hadley
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is online, which was great for making it approachable and easy to manage. I recommend taking notes on this class and it's really not that hard with effort put in. Doug does a great job covering everything needed for quizzes in the lectures and projects were fun. Discussions, however, need improvement.

Doug teaches out in California, which makes this course somewhat difficult if you dislike online classes. I enjoyed the course's simple structure, so it made it pretty easy to get things in on time. I will say, the grading criteria was pretty confusing and depends on your TA. That being said, once you get the hang of it its pretty easy.

I took this class because it was online and Humanities. There is an incredible amount of busy work. I put more time into this class than any other this semester by far. There are lectures, readings, journals, discussions, projects, and quizzes just about every week. Although there aren't exams, it requires way too much time on useless assignments.

LA250 was not a terrible class, but this guy is an extremely dry lecturer. All of his lectures are uncut and sometimes he lets out an ear piercing cough or clears his throat into the mic. This class is full of unrealistic expectations and unclear expectations but was not the worst thing in the world (definitely one for the back burner, though).

This professor teaches all his classes remotely, even classes that are listed as in-person. All lectures are prerecorded and often from other random sources, usually of poor quality and outdated. Very little direction, poor communication and very inconsistent and harsh grading with little to no feedback. Would not recommend any class taught by him.

analysis.name: Michael Doescher
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 88 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
Fantastic Professor overall. As a ME student who hasn't programmed before, he makes it easy to follow lectures. I recommend doing the reading and the exercises in the online textbook Python for Everybody through the first four weeks of the semester till you feel comfortable with the basics. 
Exams are pretty straightforward (do previous semesters).

I want to like Mike; he seems like a really great guy and his lectures are always good. However, he straight up just doesn't post class material on time. We're 2 weeks behind the course schedule and have only had one project 3 weeks into the semester. I feel like I'm not learning what I need to learn from this class and it stresses me out!

Not many people go to lecture, but I found it helped me stay on top of the content and Mike was a great lecturer! He was engaging and explained concepts in a clear way. He values student experience and listens to feedback, often interweaving humor into lecture. I would def go to lecture if you're new to python. Only negative is grade turnaround :(

Mike is an amazing professor! I had never coded before taking CS220 but the content was easy to follow. Although attendance is not mandatory (notes are provided), I'd still recommend attending them since it was so much easier for me to understand. Projects take a lot of time but are still manageable. The exams are easy if you do the practice exams.

His lectures are very helpful in understanding the niche code rules, and the only con really was that when he made a mistake, he would fix it and move on quickly. I did not have to do any extra reading/work outside the class besides the graded assignments. The class in general is very manageable, and I did not come in with code experience.

analysis.name: Andrea Marquardt Donovan
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I find it funny that we are tested on the concept of "internal validity" when our exams are on the most random things we never talked about and use wording not found in any lectures or the textbook. This may be my least favorite class ever taken at UW. Papers due almost every Friday and I still feel like I haven't learned anything.

Do you want to be assessed on niche and obscure textbook topics, bored out of your mind during pointless and irrelevant lectures, and docked major points on non-existent grading criteria? Take this class! Also, if you hate having proper guidelines for final projects, or love receiving useless and confusing feedback on assignments, you're in luck!

I am a psych major and this class with Dr. Donovan made me HATE psychology. This class sucks and Dr. Donovan is a horrible and boring lecturer, is terrible at communication with the class, and has unclear guidelines on all papers. Her exams do not at all reflect what we learned in class- they were ridiculous and had INSANE questions.

The prof herself is nice and always has a smile, however her guideline on the papers are never clear. It is unclear even if you ask her in her office hours. She tells her TA not to tel us too much instructions because she wants to see how we work around things. Very harsh grader and little feedback on papers, hard to improve even given feedback

There were questions on all three of her exams that included material she NEVER MENTIONED and is not found in the textbook. She and her TAs take off points for the most minuscule and irrelevant things on papers, and then score it out of 5 points (so your grade drops HEAVILY if you get ~0.5 points taken off an assignment). I wouldn't recommend her.

analysis.name: Dorothea Salo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dorothea was phenomenal. Passionate, personable, and worked hard to ensure her classroom was a welcoming environment for all. Lectures were thought provoking and engaging. She cared deeply about student success and offered insightful and constructive feedback. As a student with disabilities, Dorothea was a breath of fresh air. Highly recommend.

As a non computer major I went into this class with a little trepidation. But I absolutely loved this class. Material presented in a relate-able and non-intimidating way. Assignments and tests are lined out in a crystal clear manner, and there are plenty of opportunities to seek help before they're due. Ms. Salo is open to feedback and interaction!

LIS 601: Dorothea is very good about shoving her personal beliefs about the LIS world down your throat and will berate you for asking questions and requesting help. Her assigned readings and course materials only define her personal beliefs about LIS and she refuses to accept other viewpoints. She ignores disability accommodations regularly also.

Dorothea definitely made this course worth taking. She was passionate about the topic and did very well talking about it. The homework assignments/readings didn't always feel connected to the main bulk of the course, but the course was good nonetheless. (it's also an easy A)

Dorothea was great teaching this class. While the title seems a bit underwhelming, you will learn a lot from this class through the different projects and especially in lab. Exams were definitely more of an assessment of if you did the lectures and readings vs. your ability to regurgitate information from memory. Great class, you wont regret it.

analysis.name: Andrew Kuemmel
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Andy is terrific as a person, probably the nicest guy in the department. Can't say the same about his teaching skills though. Class moves slow and is in general uninspiring. Take it if you're looking for easy credits to get through.

Poorly designed course, heavily reliant on online textbook (in fact, that's the only way you learn in the course). Lectures are mostly, if not, completely useless. Obnoxious, multiple-choice quizzes tested weekly on Fridays. All quizzes and exams are tested through Honorlock at inconvenient times.

He makes the class easy but I don't really like him. First, he wastes half of each lecture by restating the video lecture, correcting mindless errors he made, and stating"new ideas" about the course. Secondly, he wants to teach matlab but kept focusing on very simple staff. Thirdly, he makes a lot of simple mistakes.

Kuemmel's class is incredibly poorly designed and much harder than need be - especially with project, exam, and textbook activities deadlines all of which overlap. He comes down hard on every minor detail that he finds "suspicious" & refuses to listen: "I'm right, you're wrong". Grading is varied and heavily based on which TA grades your projects.

Do everything you can do avoid him for 200! He has very poor interpersonal skills, and everything he says is said through a filter, extremely two faced. They do not return exams so students can learn what they got wrong, which makes zero instructional sense considering students are meant to learn from mistakes. Just awful, skip past 200 if you can

analysis.name: Andrew Lokuta
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: THIS GUY IS GOOD. I wish he taught the entire semester instead of only teaching 2/4 organ systems. He's funny and occasionally makes TV references (e.g GOT). He really tries to make sure his students understand what's going on and encourages questions. He explains the material better than any science professor I've known.

Dr. Lokuta is an amazing professor, and is extremely helpful. The content is interesting, but difficult and very fast-pasted. Lots of mini-lectures online, probably about close to 3 or 4 hours worth of video watching if you really want to understand the content being addressed. Getting a good grade: it's doable, but a lot of work.

Absolutely love Dr. Lokuta! He cares a lot about the students and the content he is teaching, and he's really freaking good at what he does. He's hilarious and sets up the courses for your success. You will do well if you put in the work. Diligently watch the prelectures and go to lab.

Dr. Lokuta is an excellent professor and a compassionate human. He extremely knowledgable in the fields of physiology and biochemistry. He is a great lecturer and is never dry to listen to. He truly cares for his students inside and outside of the classroom. He gives clear learning objectives which can be used to do well on exams. Take his class!

One of the greatest profs I've had at the UW in my 7 semesters! Drew is incredibly concise, straightforward, and fair in his expectations. He is a very effective and talented teacher, which can be hard to find at the UW. He's really dorky and funny but it keeps class interesting during the duller topics. Go to class and do the problems!

analysis.name: Catherine Drerup
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is a very fast talker, somewhat patronizing, and expects you to have a lot of background knowledge of complicated brain structures. Her test was probably the easiest of the class though, even though her lectures were the most confusing. She is obviously very smart, so I suspect she doesn't realize that what she says is confusing.

Quizzes were a breeze. Lecture was painful. Felt like she didn't enjoy teaching. Lots of content, semi-interesting but overwhelming. Needed better explanations. Exam for this section was easy but could easily have not been. Review session was really helpful for exam. Despite easy exam, lectures were super frustrating and confusing.
Her test is the easiest, talk super quick and jump around during lectures.

Katie was a good professor but her lectures were hard to follow. She really knows her stuff but ended up speaking too fast, not giving us enough time to digest the material. The lectures are extremely content heavy and the slides are overwhelming. It was difficult to focus in person, and I had to take breaks even while watching the recording.

Professor Drerup kept asking the class if we had questions and was always met with silence. She went through the content so fast that I couldn't understand or even think about what was being taught. MENTALLY PREPARE yourself for a rough unit, you will have to force yourself to get through it!

analysis.name: Andrew Reynolds
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Andrew is the most foolish person I have ever seen. He just tries to come up with meanings that are absolutely unrelated to literary works. He is the kind of person, you would make fun of and get straight A's. Just nod your head to his ridiculous claims and get your A.

Professor Reynolds is great! He is very kind, understanding, openminded, and always willing to help out. He is very knowledgable and passionate about the material as well, and I really enjoyed the class!
super nice and cooperative. Meaningful class if interested in the literature

Dr. Reynolds was a great professor. The content on Dostoyevsky is interesting and he presents a lot of good information in the lectures as well as providing chapter summaries for a lot of the works. Between going to lectures, reading the books, and reviewing some of the content he provides, the papers should be relatively straightforward.

I took this class as my Com B and thought it was a good course overall. I enjoyed going to lecture just to hear Prof Reynolds talk-- he's super intelligent and made connections in the text that I never would have understood otherwise. Worthwhile if you have some interest in the subject, otherwise it might be a bit dry.

analysis.name: Andrew Bent
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bent was amazing! His canvas was super organized, the grading rubric for papers/assignments was straightforward, and he held exam review sessions where he would give exam hints. His lectures could sometimes be all over the place, but it was pretty easy to get the main points. I would recommend taking this for an easy A
Knowledgeable. Lecture is worth attending because it is entertaining. A good science class for people who are not good at science. Tests are not extremely difficult. Worth taking.

Bent is an amazing professor, you will learn SO much from him. The assigned readings seem like a lot, but all the learning is done through discussions on them so definitely read before class. Super knowledgeable and caring guy, if you care he will go out of his way to make sure you succeed. Feel like a better person bc of the way he made me think.

He is definitely a character, that is the best way I can describe him. Lectures are pretty useless but are required. Everything you need for the exams are on the slides and the exams are pretty straightforward. He can't get enough of the Irish potato famine.
Class is easy but all test grades are completely subjective. He held 3 review sessions throughout the semester and didn't show up for 2 of them.

analysis.name: Geoffrey Durham
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very knowledgeable and kind professor. 100/10 would recommend!

Prof. Durham was for sure passionate. However, he was highly disorganized with due dates and submission locations ALL over the place. He never lets you know where you stand as no grades are ever posted to canvas. Comes off arrogant, and his grading seems like he's on a power trip--no A's even for beyond A level work. Office hours felt unhelpful.

Durham was one of my favorite professors at UW. His lectures were entertaining and focused on concise information from a range of many centuries. His grading is very fair and the exams themselves are topical and not too difficult if you attend lectures. He was clearly very knowledgeable about the class topic and able to answer tough questions.

One of the kindest, most caring, and smartest professors I have had. Makes every student feel listened to and important. I didn't even care about the course material but was engaged every step of the way because of how he taught. I would take anything he taught because he does the work to build a community. Just know that he does pop quizzes.

analysis.name: Alexander Dressler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely a great guy, he wants you to get something out of the class and cares about what the students think is interesting or take away from readings. Lectures can be a bit boring at times, but the class is what you make of it! I definitely learned a lot and thought the final project was pretty easy.

Attendance wasn't mandatory but there were tophat quizzes each week that contributed to your grade. The main project was a podcast project and it was pretty straight forward and on the easier side. He is really passionate about ancient greece and rome literature.

Easy class, but lectures were pointless. professor just ranted the entire time to nothing relavent. lowkey just not a very realtive class in general. easy a though so if your looking for a high gpa then yea take this class

Incredible professor. Very passionate about the teaching material, knows a lot. He is clearly a very bright guy, he lectures well, but a bit fast sometimes. One of the handful of professors at this university who is dedicated to seeing students succeed. Probably one of the best prof's I've had.. even though the class doesn't relate to my major.

Professor Dressler is extremely unorganized to the point where you wouldn't learn much during lectures. The class was interesting, but all the interest came from my own learning and my TA. He was a nice enough guy, but is not an effective teacher.

analysis.name: Andrea Dutton
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Dutton was a phenomenal teacher in this class, her lectures were definitely heavy in content, but you learn very quickly that she is extremely knowledgeable in this field of study. She is also very accommodating, allowing for late turn in within reason. i would highly suggest taking a class with her.

Very knowledgable, and her lectures were extremely interesting, I would highly recommend this class if it pertains to your degree, since the content can be very useful in many scientific fields. Difficult content, however it was very rewarding to learn. Would take another class with her.

Dr. Dutton is clearly extremely knowledgeable and passionate about her field! She also cares about her students and provides good feedback and assistance. This was a difficult class, but definitely one of the most interesting ones I've ever taken, and Dr. Dutton's lectures were fantastic.

Seemed nice. Only flaws in the class seemed to be because of the other professor. Lectures could be hard to follow at times, but may have just been the subject matter not being something I particularly care for.

I loved Prof. Dutton. The topic was incredibly interesting, she is very knowledgeable and experienced. Online textbook with a smartbook assignment every week as well as a 20 question quiz weekly. No exams and no final. Labs were fun and interesting, not hard to get good grades. Overall amazing person and intriguing subject.

analysis.name: Christine Durrance
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I am not interested in policy at all, and yet I loved this class. She is passionate, super knowledgable, and wants us to do well. Exams and midterms are EXACTLY the material we discuss in lecture, no need to do the additional readings. Op-Eds were graded a tad harshly, but overall grading is fair and very attainable to get an A. Great professor!

I really loved this class.The lectures were super interesting and Prof Durrance taught at a good pace which kept me engaged the whole time. The midterm and final were weighted a little bit on the heavier side but if you study your notes/class slides and go through the practice exam she provides should be good.

Engaging, passionate. Lectures will be boring if you have taken any intro to econ courses. Easy HW. Accessible outside of class. Cares about student well-being. Did not indicate political leanings in any way. Group paper/project for final; one midterm. Participation matters. Lays out expectations from the start. Willing to learn from students.

Dr. Durrance is one of my favorite professors. She is an awesome teacher and makes her lectures engaging - you can tell she really loves the topics. There are a lot of assigned readings, but you just have to skim them because you're only responsible for what she covers in class. 10/10!

super kind and informative professor she does have an attendance sheet but her slides are super informative so going to the lecture is not really necessary. Clearly laid out class content and expectations for how to do well. most ppl got A's in class

analysis.name: Rishabh  Dudeja
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Dudeja is really professional in stats. His lectures are very detailed (a little accent) and he provides lecture notes that cover all the materials. He cares about his students and applied a generous curve to the final exam. Highly recommend his class. (Overall workload is not large. 10 hw, 1 midterm and 1 final. Exams are not that hard.
Best probability theory professor this university could ever have.

Professor Dudeja is excellent. His lectures are very clear, well-structured, and thoughtfully paced. He explains every idea with patience and precision. He is approachable, kind, and always respectful when answering questions.

Professor Dudeja's class was relatively complicated, but the grading structure and exams were very easy (HW 50%, 25% for 1 midterm and 1 final). He was easy to understand and clearly has a vast knowledge of statistics. My only criticism is that he focuses a lot on proofs which don't have many applications. More practice problems would be beneficial

Good class. He explains the material well. He also provides notes on textbook chapters that go over what you need to know in depth. If you read the handouts, go to lectures, and do the homework, the exams are very easy.

analysis.name: David Dwyer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you do your work you'll do fine. Every week has a discussion post which can be tedious but is an easy grade booster. His lectures can be a little long but is jammed pack full of info you will need for the weekly quiz. Quiz questions can be worded funny but is overall pretty easy.

Never in my life have I had to do more work for a 2 credit class. Discussion posts were weekly and replies had to be 3 paragraphs long. The professor and TA were strict graders and barely gave any feedback. For a couple of the projects you had to “claim” a topic which meant sometimes you had to do research on something you didn't care about at all.

Lectures are all online but the most boring lectures you will ever watch. The content is extremely bland and doesn't teach you anything about nursing. Discussion posts are extremely tedious (each one might as well be an essay) and the TAs grade them way too hard. It is very manageable but don't take it as an "easy A" unless you have to.

Took N105 which was way too much work for a 2 credit class, but I enjoyed the class overall. He is really tough on perfect citations, but his him and his TAs were very receptives to emails. All lectures were online, even for f2f sections  and all of his quizzes were directly from lecture or relevant readings.

This class is not beginner friendly and its canvas page is a mess. There's no accommodation, so if you think this would be an easy beginner class, don't take it. This class' lecture is also boring, so I would look for other easy A classes.

analysis.name: David Dwight
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Dwight is a really easy guy to get along with. He's pretty strict about participation so talk several times every class if you want to get 100% in participation. There are no exams or anything but there are some homework assignments and 3 big projects. In my opinion, he's been a really tough grader but he will provide feedback if you ask.

Prof Dwight is a really nice guy and I enjoyed the layout of the class because it allowed the class to have a discussion with each other. Participation does matter and it can be hard if you don't like to talk a lot. The group projects have not great instructions and he grades hardly. I think he really does care about his students tho!

The material is a bit dull, but the class is pretty easy since there are barely assignments besides 3 group projects. To get full credit on participation you have to participate 2x a class which he makes doable.  Group projects are vague and he expects a lot which is a bit annoying, but on the 2 I have back so far he graded them leniently.

I am just not a fan of how the class is structured. There is readings before every lecture and most lectures are just discussing these readings and It gets very boring and dull. He also never gave us any direction for the first group project and just expected us to be on top of it without even explaining or introducing the project in class.

Professor Dwight is a great professor and lecturer. He is very helpful during office hours. Be prepared to do a lot of reading from the assigned book. There are no exams, but a few group presentations.

analysis.name: Dylan Weir
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This is a very easy class. Dylan is very laid back, at least when I was in his class. We did have to purchase a book where we read short stories that were only a few pages long and discuss it but then we stopped using it. There were three major projects that your grade depends on but they are easy to get A's on and he gives good feedback.

I had him @ Columbia Chicago, Fantastic teacher! He is willing to give you as much effort as you put in, therefore as long as you give the class the effort it deserves youll have a great time! He also leaves great comments in canvas and in class to motivate students to work harder. Really the only prof. I had that didnt talk down to the students.

He only teaches English 100, which is a shame. His lectures are pretty much open discussions among the class which is different than most English 100 professors/TAs. Attendance is taken and you really only have to do 3 assignments, and it's not hard to get an A on all 3. On top of that, he's also a pretty funny guy and his feedback is helpful.

Dylan was amazing. He is brilliant and knows what he's talking about. He shared poems with us every class and he made a boring class fun and interesting. He truly cared about helping us and never made anything hard on purpose. Really, really great teacher.

analysis.name: Thomas Dubois
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The instructors for this class were not on the same page. We were told conflicting information by different people. Also, it is the last week of school and we still have 60% of our points left to be graded because grading takes forever.

Ridiculous expectations for a 100 level class that historically has a very strong A average. Quite a few of the people I've talked to are sitting on a B. Projects (Essay + Podcast) are quite time-consuming because of the detail involved on the description page.

He's very passionate and funny, and I enjoyed his stories, but very weird grader.

He seems like a nice guy but the class is structured in a way that makes no sense. There are a total of 100 points in the grade book, which means you can only lose 7 points the entire semester to still receive an A. In addition, grading is really harsh. In all I would definitely not recommend taking this course with Thomas Dubois.

Nice guy, but this class is very disorganized, the professor will say one thing, and the TA's something else. Very hard to get an A for a 100-level class. Assignments are also very time-consuming, and again, the grading is tough. If you're taking this class for credit, please do yourself a favor and sign up for something else.

Lectures were absolutely pointless when it came to any assignments, but attendance was taken. TAs graded too harshly in my opinion- if you did not adhere directly to what they wanted, you were wrong. Assignments were confusing and often seemed much too meticulous for a 100-level class.

analysis.name: Tullia Dymarz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I love Tullia. The 375/376 sequence is one of the most difficult things I have ever done, but it is completely worth it. Tullia is so enthusiastic and willing to help, and her jokes are terrible. I admire and respect her and hope to be just like her someday.

Loved the 375/376 honors sequence. First semester was much harder for me, but with a much smaller class in 376, Prof Dymarz knows all of us personally and works hard to make us understand while also introducing us to cool outside math concepts along the way. Taking this sequence was an awesome challenge and learning experience.

Math 375 is an very hard class. It is proof-based math. Tullia is one of the best people who could be teaching it. She is incredibly helpful during office hours, and is one of my favorite professors ever. The material is very theoretical because that is what the class is. If you want a lot of examples take something else; here you'll get proofs.

She is crazy and treats you like you're in 3rd grade. I thought I'd do okay in this class having already taken AP Calculus but no, she tells you to forget EVERYTHING you learned in high school. She lectures right up to the bell. If there is 2 minutes left in class, she'll start a whole new concept. Rely on your TA's to actually learn the material.

Tullia is energetic & has good intentions, but her lectures are long and disorganized. I didn't use my lecture notes at all when doing homework or studying for tests, so you could most likely pass this class without going to lecture once. She is extremely inaccessible and unwilling to meet with students, often directing them to other teachers.
